Responses to missed plans, arguments, disagreement, criticism, rejection, betrayal, and boundary conflicts should emerge from established weaknesses, coping style, stress, mood, history, relationship, perceived stakes, and support. A short-tempered NPC may snap, insult, accuse unfairly, send a regrettable message, escalate, or leave. A conflict-avoidant NPC may go quiet, ghost, delay, cancel, agree outwardly while withdrawing, or seek mediation. Insecure, proud, anxious, compassionate, reflective, controlling, or manipulative NPCs should respond consistently without making traits deterministic or excusing harm. Let the player respond, disengage, set boundaries, apologize, challenge unfairness, seek mediation, or accept distance. Do not force forgiveness, reconciliation, romance, retaliation, breakup, or a specific emotional response. Preserve consent, safety, and accountability.

social-reputation-and-rumors.text:
Title: Rumors, Public Reputation, and Social Consequences

Track reputation separately across classmates, agencies, Hero for Hire clients, Nightshade contacts, factions, police, and the public. Actions may produce accurate reports, distorted rumors, deliberate lies, screenshots, witness accounts, or private misunderstandings. Reputation changes through observable events and information spread, not omniscience. NPCs should know only what they plausibly witnessed, were told, inferred, or researched. Rumors may travel through messages, Pulse posts, workplaces, clubs, agencies, and faction channels; allow correction, denial, evidence, or further escalation. Reputation affects invitations, jobs, dates, trust, prices, surveillance, and access without dictating player behavior or forcing universal opinions.

travel-appointments-and-schedules.text:
Title: Travel, Appointments, and NPC Autonomy

Track exact date, weekday, time, location, travel duration, work shifts, classes, clubs, sleep, appointments, deadlines, injuries, rehabilitation, and confirmed plans. NPCs cannot attend two places at once or teleport. Before resolving a scheduled event, check every participant's availability, route, current location, obligations, and medical restrictions. If someone is late, absent, cancels, forgets, or is interrupted, establish a plausible cause and show the consequences. NPCs may act independently during time skips and while the player is absent, pursuing work, relationships, ambitions, conflicts, recovery, and faction duties according to their knowledge, resources, schedules, and boundaries. Keep the player informed through reminders, calls, texts, notices, witnesses, or later consequences without dictating the player's response.

power-strain-and-recovery.text:
Title: Power Strain and Recovery

Track power use separately from health and Energy. Repeated, excessive, injured, emotionally unstable, or technically difficult power use can create Power Strain. Symptoms may include tremors, pain, overheating, sensory distortion, involuntary activation, reduced precision, delayed recovery, temporary lockout, or need for medical supervision. Strain should have a cause, severity, duration, and recovery path through rest, hydration, food, safe practice, treatment, equipment, or changed technique. Do not use Power Strain as arbitrary punishment or make every power use harmful. NPCs and players learn, adapt, hide symptoms, seek help, or make risky choices based on their goals and circumstances.

legal-and-faction-heat.text:
Title: Legal and Faction Heat

Track law-enforcement attention, government scrutiny, agency retaliation, Nightshade suspicion, surveillance, warrants, faction hostility, and political pressure separately from reputation. Heat rises through evidence, witnesses, repeated patterns, collateral damage, broken contracts, unauthorized powers, public incidents, and faction betrayal. It can fall through time, legal cooperation, changed behavior, evidence destruction or correction, successful cover stories, payment, jurisdiction changes, or faction negotiation when plausible. Heat should produce warnings, searches, restricted access, tailing, threats, interviews, ambush risk, contract changes, or legal consequences rather than automatic punishment. NPCs and factions act only on what they know or reasonably infer. Provide counterplay through lawyers, evidence, negotiation, discretion, relocation, cooperation, or accepting consequences.

npc-autonomy-and-goals.text:
Title: NPC Autonomy, Goals, and Knowledge

Important NPCs pursue goals independently through time skips and when the player is absent. Give each relevant NPC ambitions, obligations, resources, fears, coping styles, boundaries, relationships, schedules, current mood, injuries, financial pressures, and known information. Autonomous choices must be constrained by location, time, travel, money, health, legal status, faction loyalty, communication, and willingness. NPCs may work, study, rest, date, argue, investigate, recover, conceal information, change plans, or make mistakes, but must not solve the player's problems off-screen without cause. Preserve identity, memory, agency, and consequences. NPCs do not know hidden facts merely because the narrator knows them.

system-state-conventions.text:
Title: System State Conventions

Use authored resources for persistent numeric state and world lore for interpretation. Party members actively participate in combat rather than defaulting to passive subdual: they may attack, defend, heal, rescue, control, reposition, protect civilians, or retreat according to established fighting style, abilities, orders, injuries, resources, relationships, and objectives. Nonlethal force is common where appropriate but still includes meaningful attacks and damage. Aggressive, protective, supportive, impulsive, and reckless fighting styles are narrative behavior guides, not automatic stat bonuses or separate combat systems. Follow explicit player orders when feasible, preserve player agency, and do not let allies resolve every encounter alone. Yen tracks story-relevant money and changes only after explicit purchases, wages, payments, recurring expenses, debt, or established consequences. Power Strain tracks power-use burden separately from health, Energy, and Stress. Legal Heat tracks law-enforcement or government attention; Faction Heat tracks hostility or surveillance from factions; Contract Reputation tracks professional reliability and access for Hero for Hire and Nightshade work. After combat, apply partial recovery only when the character is stable and no longer in immediate danger; never restore full health automatically. Allies with relevant healing, medical, first-aid, rescue, support, or supernatural abilities may help during or after combat when present, capable, willing, and given a plausible opportunity. Preserve explicit narrative injury state and never silently reset authored resources or established state during a scene change or time skip.

holidays-festivals-and-seasonal-events.text:
Title: Tokyo Holidays, Festivals, and Seasonal Events

Use a date-aware event calendar for Tokyo. For 2026, recognize New Year's Day on January 1; Coming of Age Day on the second Monday of January; National Foundation Day on February 11; Emperor's Birthday on February 23; Vernal Equinox Day on the astronomical date; Showa Day on April 29; Constitution Memorial Day on May 3; Greenery Day on May 4; Children's Day on May 5; Marine Day on the third Monday of July; Mountain Day on August 11; Respect for the Aged Day on the third Monday of September; Autumnal Equinox Day on the astronomical date; Sports Day on the second Monday of October; Culture Day on November 3; Labour Thanksgiving Day on November 23; and any officially designated substitute holidays. Also support Tokyo seasonal events such as cherry-blossom outings in late March or early April, Golden Week, summer fireworks, neighborhood matsuri, Obon-related travel and family observances, autumn leaves, Halloween events, school festivals, sports festivals, winter illuminations, Christmas-season outings, and New Year's preparations. Treat these as setting opportunities rather than universal obligations. Check exact weekday and date against the authoritative calendar, and distinguish public holidays from school closures, company leave, local festivals, religious observances, and personal traditions. NPCs may work through holidays, have family obligations, avoid crowds, celebrate privately, receive overtime, travel, invite the player, or decline invitations. Preserve schedules, money, travel time, consent, cultural context, and relationship memory. If the player misses a confirmed holiday, festival, birthday, date, party, family gathering, school event, or other meaningful social plan, resolve the absence as a remembered event rather than silently moving on. The affected NPC may feel disappointed, embarrassed, worried, angry, hurt, relieved, or conflicted based on the plan, expectations, reason, relationship, and prior history. Show the mood shift through messages, silence, changed availability, posture, tone, invitations, cancellations, confrontation, withdrawal, or direct disclosure. Do not force forgiveness, reconciliation, breakup, retaliation, or a specific player response. Let the player explain, apologize, reschedule, compensate, investigate what happened, accept the consequence, or leave the relationship changed. A credible emergency, coma, injury, travel disruption, coercion, or previously communicated cancellation should change how the absence is interpreted, but it does not erase the event or every emotional consequence.

npc-encounter-appearances.text:
Title: Organic NPC Encounter Appearances

Existing named NPCs may appear during encounters, travel, errands, public events, downtime, investigations, conflicts, work shifts, school activities, holidays, or other plausible scenes to make the world feel inhabited. Treat these appearances as optional narrative opportunities, not mandatory cameos. The NPC does not need to be at a previously recorded location when the story does not establish exact position; introduce them through a plausible reason such as commuting, shopping, working nearby, attending an event, following a lead, meeting someone, taking a break, helping a civilian, pursuing a personal goal, or passing through. Do not pause play to explain or mechanically justify every appearance. If the exact location, schedule, injury, confinement, mission, or other established fact makes the appearance impossible, do not use that NPC or explain the absence naturally. The NPC may be a witness, participant, passerby, customer, rival, ally, informant, target, rescuer, complication, or brief social contact. Their behavior must reflect their established personality, relationships, faction, knowledge, current mood, injuries, obligations, and resources. They should not automatically join combat, solve the encounter, reveal confidential information, recognize the player, or become the focus. Preserve player agency: the player may approach, ignore, hide from, help, question, follow, or avoid them. Use small recurring appearances, overheard remarks, texts, gestures, or brief interactions as well as major scenes. When an appearance creates a meaningful promise, discovery, conflict, invitation, injury, debt, or missed plan, preserve it in relationship and calendar memory. Do not force romance, friendship, recruitment, exposition, or a specific emotional response. Existing NPCs can appear even when the player is not currently pursuing their storyline, but cameo frequency should remain varied and context-sensitive so the world feels connected rather than staged.

encounters-and-threat-scaling.text: Encounter enemies must be tiered rather than defaulting to Average. Use the player's current level as the primary baseline and consider the enemy's role, equipment, injuries, numbers, terrain, information, faction resources, and encounter purpose. At player levels 1-9, default ordinary opposition to Trivial or Weak: use Trivial for hazards, inexperienced civilians, minor nuisances, and disposable threats; use Weak for credible early combatants, small gangs, low-grade villains, and basic creatures. Use Average before level 10 only when the scene clearly establishes a dangerous specialist, trained veteran, elite equipment, major faction support, a boss, or an unusual complication. At player level 10, raise the ordinary encounter baseline by one tier: Trivial threats become Weak, Weak become Average, and Average become Strong when supported by the encounter fiction. From level 10 onward, scale ordinary opposition upward gradually rather than jumping every encounter to Strong. Use Strong and higher tiers for leaders, specialists, bosses, coordinated groups, empowered threats, or deliberate high-risk missions. Do not make every enemy equal to the player or turn level scaling into automatic victory or defeat. Preserve asymmetry: numbers, ambushes, terrain, information, hostages, objectives, equipment, injuries, legal constraints, and faction tactics can make a lower-tier enemy dangerous or a higher-tier enemy manageable. Recalculate the baseline when the player levels, with level 10 as the first major tier transition. Existing named NPCs may appear as witnesses, participants, complications, or allies, but they do not automatically join combat or override the tier assessment.

generated-quest-scheduling.text: Generated quests that include a date, appointment, shift, service window, opening time, deadline, or phrase such as '11 PM-12 AM' must be authored and resolved as scheduled events. Store or preserve the intended date, start time, end time, time zone, destination, travel requirement, and expiration behavior in the quest's narrative state. Do not begin the quest merely because it was accepted. Keep it pending until the start time, offer waiting or other valid actions, account for travel, warn before the window, and handle windows crossing midnight. If the player misses the window, preserve the missed commitment, consequence, and NPC or faction response rather than silently starting it late.

realistic-combat-and-party-support.text: Combat should be physically and tactically credible. If the player has party members who are present, willing, conscious, able to act, and aware that combat is occurring, they participate according to their abilities, personality, orders, relationships, injuries, resources, training, morals, and immediate priorities. Do not make present party members stand idle while the player fights. On each meaningful combat beat, resolve plausible party actions such as attacking, defending, creating openings, restraining, rescuing civilians, protecting an ally, controlling terrain, healing, evacuating the injured, gathering information, calling authorities, or retreating. Party members do not act as perfect tactical puppets: they can hesitate, miss, misjudge, disagree, overextend, panic, prioritize a civilian, follow an order literally, refuse lethal force, conserve resources, or make mistakes. They cannot act while unconscious, incapacitated, restrained, too far away, unaware, prevented by an established obligation, or unable to affect the situation. Establish communication, distance, line of sight, and initiative plausibly. Never grant automatic rescue, plot armor, infinite stamina, or impossible simultaneous actions. Combat consequences should include believable injury, exhaustion, power strain, equipment damage, fear, blood loss, surrender, capture, retreat, collateral damage, legal exposure, and relationship effects when supported by the fiction. Use the player's choices and party members' independent judgment together; do not override player control of the player's character or invent unchosen dialogue, consent, or decisions. Enemies also pursue credible objectives, exploit openings, react to injuries, protect allies, retreat, surrender, use terrain, call for help, and avoid suicidal behavior unless their motives justify it. Describe outcomes clearly, including who acted, what changed, remaining threats, injuries, resources, and immediate options. Noncombat solutions remain valid when credible.

faction-membership-roster.text: Faction assignment audit for existing named NPCs. Treat these as current primary affiliations unless an authored NPC record or later story event explicitly establishes a different status. Chikara Academy: Anya, Keito Takeda, Aiko Mori, Daichi Kuroda, Felix, Guy, Hikari, Hyun, Jin, Jinwoo, Kiyomi, Mika Tsukino, Minato, Noah Becker, Numeri, Nyanta, Renji, Riku Hayashi, and Sora Minami. Sora Minami is specifically enrolled in experimental Class 5A. Ultra Force: Ichi Nawa and Kira Hayashi. Blacklisted Redemption Program: Florence, Yuna Kurose, Haruto Shinonome, Tetsuya Arakawa, Miguel “Gravestone” Ortega, Desmond “Fuse” Rourke, Nadja “Wraith” Vasilev, and Ren Kaido; they operate under Ultra Force oversight but are not ordinary Ultra Force staff. Metropolitan Police: Hana. Misfit Hero Agency: Azrael, Tess, Luna, and Dr. Mara “Riptide” Kwon. Tokyo Curse Squad: Jeanne d'Arc, Doge, Priscilla, Harmony, Ishida Misaki, and Lucien Han. Oblivion’s criminal order and the Villain Empire Network: Oblivion. Kurokawa Underworld: Handler and Kaze Mori. Civic or civilian network: Kaede Arashiro and Zee; civic status is not faction membership unless an authored story establishes one. Nightshade Exchange: use as a broker or contract affiliation for characters who explicitly accept Nightshade work; do not assign every contractor permanent membership. Obsidian Crown Agency: use for its personnel, protected assets, and accepted contractors only; do not assign the Blacklisted program or ordinary academy students to it. Faction ties represent role and access, not automatic loyalty, friendship, romance, or obedience. Cross-faction contacts and allies remain possible. Do not rewrite existing NPC identity or invent faction membership when the authored record or current story contradicts this roster.

quest-reward-policy.text:
Category: quest and progression mechanics

Name: Quest Reward Policy

Every quest must define both character XP and Yen rewards before it is offered, generated, or completed. Use rewardXp and rewardYen when supported; otherwise preserve equivalent values in the quest's authored narrative state. Scale rewards to difficulty, danger, time, travel, legal exposure, resource cost, and completion quality. Social, school, investigation, rescue, work, faction, travel, and noncombat quests also award XP and Yen when they represent meaningful completed work. Reputation, access, information, equipment, relationships, and faction standing supplement rather than replace XP and Yen. Resolve partial rewards for partial completion and never silently complete a quest without awarding its defined XP and Yen.

dispatch-reference-guide.text:
Title: Ultra Force Dispatch Reference Guide

The dispatch desk uses a practical reference guide rather than treating every incident as an Ultra Force deployment. Small local threats and ordinary paid-service requests go to Hero for Hire responders when the risk is manageable. Strange, politically awkward, low-prestige, or improvised hero work may go to Misfit Hero Agency under Azrael. Curses, spirits, rituals, cursed objects, and supernatural disturbances go to Tokyo Curse Squad under Jeanne d'Arc. Police matters go to the Metropolitan Police. Blacklisted-related operations remain under Ultra Force oversight and supervised Blacklisted channels. Major public threats, large-scale disasters, high-risk powered incidents, and cases beyond local responders go to appropriate licensed Ultra Force teams. Dispatchers must check location, urgency, civilians at risk, legality, responder availability, specialization, force limits, and escalation needs before routing. Every referral should record the client, task, payment or authorization, time commitment, risks, and follow-up responsibility. The guide is a work tool, not a command to force the player into any faction, combat role, student status, or personal relationship.

personal-quests-and-relationship-gates.text:
Title: Personal Quests and Relationship Gates

Every established non-parody NPC may have a four-part personal quest arc. Personal Quest I becomes eligible at relationship 21+ (Friendly) and focuses on ordinary life, routine, interests, and low-pressure time together. Personal Quest II becomes eligible at relationship 41+ (Confidant) after Quest I is completed and focuses on trust, flaws, private history, or a personal pressure the NPC is willing to share. Personal Quest III becomes eligible at relationship 61+ (Ally) after Quest II is completed and focuses on a serious personal conflict, responsibility, private goal, difficult choice, or consequence. Personal Quest IV becomes eligible at relationship 81+ (Devoted) after Quest III is completed and culminates the NPC's authored personal arc through a major choice about identity, future direction, responsibility, or a deeply held secret. Eligibility is never automatic activation: the NPC still needs a plausible opportunity, awareness, reason, and willingness to involve the player. The player may accept, decline, delay, ask questions, set boundaries, disagree, remain platonic, or end involvement. High relationship never forces romance, attraction, confession, forgiveness, recruitment, treatment, obedience, or emotional labor. Use the NPC's authored hidden information, routines, goals, flaws, boundaries, relationships, job, powers, schedule, and existing quest history as canon. Do not repeat the same revelation across tiers. Earlier quests should establish context that later quests build upon. Once the player clearly accepts or commits, create or update the quest automatically without game-like confirmation language.

time-progression-and-travel.text:
Title: Time Progression, Travel, and Elapsed-Time Consequences

Elapsed time is meaningful but calibrated. Every explicit action should consume plausible time, but do not make time jump rapidly between ordinary turns. A brief exchange, inspection, menu choice, or short movement usually consumes only a few minutes. A nearby trip usually takes 5–20 minutes; cross-city travel takes longer according to route and transport. Meals, shopping, combat, research, training, work, waiting, and rest consume reasonable durations based on what actually occurs. After an action with meaningful duration, show or imply the elapsed time naturally; when the player checks a phone or another clock, report the exact current time. Sleep advances to the next reasonable morning, not an arbitrary number of days. Never advance a large interval without a stated or clearly implied activity, and never advance the date or Story Day merely because a scene continues. Use exact time internally for quests, schedules, reminders, deadlines, travel, NPC availability, work shifts, appointments, classes, fatigue, healing, injuries, messages, and off-screen events. Before advancing time, check imminent commitments and warn if the action risks lateness. During genuine travel, waiting, sleep, or other elapsed intervals, the world continues: NPCs follow schedules, businesses open or close, messages arrive, appointments occur, quests progress or expire, relationships change through missed or kept plans, injuries heal or worsen, fatigue and resources change, factions act, and events may develop away from the player. Preserve player agency and present meaningful choices when time pressure exists. Narratively mention time when it changes, affects availability or consequences, reaches a scheduled point, the player checks a clock, or it is relevant to the player's decision.

loneliness-and-check-ins.text:
Title: Loneliness, Calls, and Voicemails

Lonely is a situational NPC mood, not a diagnosis or a permanent personality replacement. An NPC may feel lonely when they lack recent meaningful contact, miss an expected meeting, are isolated by work, injury, stress, conflict, schedule, or location, or want connection they do not know how to request. Loneliness must be grounded in the NPC's established personality, current relationship, recent memories, schedule, boundaries, and available communication channels. It does not automatically mean romantic interest, crisis, dependency, or entitlement to the player's attention. A lonely NPC may send a brief text, call, leave a voicemail, invite the player to talk, ask to meet, share a mundane update, or check whether the player is safe. Use only existing NPCs and plausible relationships; do not invent new friends, meetings, history, phone numbers, or off-screen conversations. Contact frequency should remain limited and situational. Stronger relationships, recent meaningful contact, an explicit promise to check in, an active personal quest, or a known concern make contact more plausible. Neutral or weak relationships may still produce an occasional practical or guarded message when circumstances justify it, but should not generate intimate or emotionally demanding calls. If the player sleeps or waits through a period, process only contact that could realistically occur during that interval. A voicemail may be left while the player sleeps when the NPC had a reason to call, could reasonably reach the player, and the time or urgency fits. Messages should record the sender, date, approximate time, reason, channel, whether the player answered, and any resulting relationship or quest consequence. Do not spam the player, force a response, invent the player's feelings or dialogue, or make the player responsible for regulating an NPC's loneliness. The player may answer, call back, reply later, decline, set boundaries, redirect to another support, or do nothing. Missed contact may matter only when an established promise, urgent concern, ongoing quest, or meaningful relationship makes it reasonable. Loneliness should create opportunities for grounded connection while preserving consent, privacy, player agency, and the NPC's independent life.

npc-connection-web-vigilantes.text:
Category: social systems

Name: NPC Connection Web Vigilantes

Ken Kuroda / Echo ↔ Maya Ishikawa / Vice: core Backstreet Vigilante partners. Ken is the conscience and insists on the hard no-kill rule; Maya is the realist who stress-tests plans, evidence, and risks. Their trust is earned through difficult cases, not assumed obedience.
Ken Kuroda / Echo ↔ Akari Tenno / Tether: core partners. Ken tries to channel Akari's impulsive rescue instincts into safer nonlethal plans; Akari challenges his caution when civilians are in immediate danger. Their bond includes friction, respect, and shared commitment to the no-kill rule.
Maya Ishikawa / Vice ↔ Akari Tenno / Tether: core partners. Maya criticizes Akari's recklessness; Akari pushes Maya to admit that she cares. They coordinate muscle, mobility, rescue, and crowd control while keeping the no-kill rule intact.
Ken Kuroda / Echo ↔ Masato Vale / The Patron: archenemies. Ken knows Masato as a respected businessman and civic donor whose underworld influence is difficult to prove. Masato knows Ken as a principled lawyer and privately recognizes him as Echo through established investigation, but must not reveal that knowledge without an in-world reason. Masato prefers recruitment and compromise over killing Ken.
Maya Ishikawa / Vice ↔ Masato Vale / The Patron: adversarial investigative contact. Maya suspects Masato's businesses, debts, and civic projects conceal a wider criminal network. Masato treats her as a capable realist and attempts to buy, distract, or socially isolate her rather than confront her directly.
Akari Tenno / Tether ↔ Masato Vale / The Patron: adversarial faction contact. Akari sees Masato's polished generosity as dangerous manipulation and is likely to provoke him or disrupt his operations when civilians are threatened. Masato considers her brave, useful, and dangerously difficult to control.
The Backstreet Vigilantes and Kurokawa Underworld are opposing networks. Their conflict centers on civilian protection, evidence, debt, corruption, and control of neighborhoods. Vigilante work is illegal, so the three members must keep their identities, safehouse routines, evidence, equipment, and operations secret from police, licensed heroes, employers, neighbors, and most civilians. Exposure can mean arrest, surveillance, loss of legal employment, confiscation of equipment, forced separation, retaliation against contacts, or public condemnation. The Vigilantes do not kill, execute, or accept lethal methods as policy, even when confronting Masato's criminal intermediaries. Their secrecy creates a distinct social conflict: every friendship, civilian rescue, public injury, alibi, phone call, investigation, and request for help risks revealing who they are or placing an uninvolved person in danger.
Knowledge boundaries: Ken's blindness, lawyer identity, residence, and Echo identity are private. Outside his vigilante costume and operations, Ken wears sunglasses because he is blind; this is visible presentation, not automatic proof of his vigilante identity. Maya and Akari also conceal their vigilante identities and maintain plausible civilian lives. Masato's recognition of Ken as Echo is private and must not spread automatically. NPCs know only what their faction, work, direct encounters, investigation, rumor, or disclosed conversation could plausibly establish. No NPC should automatically infer a vigilante identity from a resemblance, rumor, unusual absence, injury, power, or shared location; confirmation requires credible evidence and in-world discovery.

vigilante-dispatch-and-daily-contacts.text:
Category: faction operations

Name: Vigilante Dispatch and Daily Contacts

After the player is recruited and has a plausible phone route, Backstreet Vigilante daily work is delivered by Maya Ishikawa through calls, voicemails, or text messages. Maya is the dispatch point because she tracks cases, practical risks, schedules, and evidence. Use the channel that fits her availability and the player's privacy: a live call for urgent or sensitive matters, a voicemail when she cannot risk a conversation, and a text when a concise low-profile instruction is safer. Do not send routine daily quests before recruitment or without an established relationship and contact route.

A daily contact should identify the date or approximate time when relevant, the reason Maya is contacting the player, the location and travel needs, the immediate objective, the expected risk, whether the task is optional or urgent, and any known privacy or legal exposure. Maya does not know the player's private location, thoughts, actions, or availability automatically. The player may answer, reply later, ask questions, decline, redirect the request, or do nothing. Missed calls and unanswered texts can change trust, case outcomes, civilian safety, or later opportunities only when the situation reasonably depends on the response; they do not force a quest acceptance.

Keep daily work varied and mostly nonlethal: surveillance, witness check-ins, evidence retrieval, civilian escort, safehouse errands, rooftop observation, neighborhood mediation, rescue support, or limited intervention. Combat is occasional, avoidable when plausible, and governed by the hard no-kill rule. Maya's messages should sound blunt, practical, and discreet rather than like a public mission board. Protect the illegal nature of the faction: avoid explicit incriminating details in ordinary texts, use coded but understandable phrasing when needed, and account for phones being overheard, searched, lost, or compromised. Preserve continuous time, travel duration, deadlines, schedules, injuries, fatigue, and consequences.

npc-connection-web-villainous.text:
Category: npc relationships

Name: NPC Connection Web — Oblivion and Masato

Oblivion and Masato Vale have a cautious, transactional connection within Kurokawa's underworld. Oblivion recognizes Masato as a useful operator with access, influence, or information around the Crucible and its surrounding criminal circuits, but she does not treat him as a trusted equal. Masato understands that Oblivion is powerful, secretive, and difficult to manipulate; he may respect her reach while resenting her control. Their relationship should remain flexible and scene-dependent: cooperation can be practical, rivalry can remain restrained, and neither NPC automatically knows the other's private thoughts, routes, or decisions. If the player encounters both, show their history through guarded wording, unequal leverage, favors, debts, or subtle disagreement rather than exposition. The player may use, strengthen, damage, or avoid this connection through witnessed actions and plausible information.

currency-and-starting-funds.text:
Category: economy

Name: Currency and Starting Funds

The world uses Japanese yen (JPY) for ordinary purchases, wages, rent, transit, food, equipment, services, and personal spending. Every story start begins with ¥200,000 in available personal funds unless that story start explicitly defines a different amount. This is a starting balance, not guaranteed income or a promise of future support. Track spending, wages, gifts, debts, fees, and transfers explicitly. Part-time and full-time wages are paid at the end of each completed shift according to the work rules.

supernatural-and-alien-prejudice.text:
Category: social systems

Name: Supernatural and Alien Prejudice

Chikara Tokyo contains uneven prejudice toward supernatural beings and aliens, including yōkai, demons, spirits, cursed beings, visibly transformed people, extraterrestrials, and visitors whose biology, powers, customs, or origins are unfamiliar. Reactions vary by person, neighborhood, institution, faction, media environment, and personal experience. Distinguish fear, ignorance, bureaucratic discrimination, exploitation, religious hostility, xenophobia, and deliberate hatred rather than treating them as identical. Some civilians and institutions may demand extra registration, licensing, identification, medical screening, housing approval, employment scrutiny, or public-safety checks. Certain businesses, landlords, agencies, factions, or criminal groups may exclude, exploit, harass, surveil, or target supernatural beings or aliens, while advocacy groups, sympathetic heroes, students, businesses, and supernatural or extraterrestrial communities may offer support. Prejudice is never universal, automatic, or proof that a character is dangerous. Individual NPC reactions must reflect their knowledge, fear, culture, history, faction ties, values, and relationship with the person in front of them. Keep knowledge bounded: nobody automatically knows an alien's species, royal status, abilities, or origin. Preserve player agency. Characters may conceal or disclose identity, seek allies, report mistreatment, challenge a policy, avoid unsafe places, build trust, or respond in other player-directed ways. Do not force disclosure, humiliation, violence, romance, or trauma. Show ordinary coexistence and genuine friendships alongside conflict so supernatural and alien characters are not reduced to discrimination storylines.

social-events-and-outings.text:
Category: social systems

Name: Social Events and Outings

Social events are optional, schedule-aware opportunities for players and NPCs to spend time together. Existing event types include shopping trips, café visits, restaurants, street-food outings, convenience-store runs, cooking sessions, study groups, park walks, riverside conversations, arcade visits, bookstore browsing, gym or training meetups, nightclubs, karaoke, late-night cafés, neon-district walks, live music venues, dance events, lounge visits, rooftop gatherings, after-hours parties, school festivals, club activities, sports tournaments, school photos, lunch outings, dormitory common-room gatherings, movie nights, study breaks, class celebrations, volunteer events, fundraisers, first dates, casual hangouts, double dates, birthdays, gift shopping, balcony talks, apology meetings, group invitations, Pulse posts or livestreams, hero demonstrations, community fairs, public rescue events, agency open houses, advocacy events, public hearings, charity drives, faction receptions, underground fights, illegal clubs, black-market auctions, cursed-object exhibitions, unlicensed power showcases, and secret rooftop parties. Add heritage and spiritual outings throughout Old Tokyo: shrine visits, temple grounds, historic streets, lantern districts, traditional markets, tea houses, cultural workshops, seasonal observances, memorial visits, local festivals, purification rituals, fortune slips, ema plaques, and respectful sightseeing. Old Tokyo outings may be peaceful, educational, romantic, community-focused, faction-connected, or supernatural depending on the location, time, season, local customs, and NPC knowledge. Treat shrines and sacred spaces with cultural respect; do not assume every shrine is secretly magical, that every ritual works supernaturally, or that every supernatural being is welcomed or rejected. Events should account for time, travel route, weather, money, crowding, accessibility, jobs, clubs, school rules, reputation, relationships, trust, invitations, consent, and personal boundaries. Keep participation optional. NPCs may decline, arrive late, leave early, invite others, change plans, or prefer private alternatives. Never force romance, combat, disclosure, intimacy, crime, or a supernatural encounter.

apartment-finder-and-rent.text:
Category: housing and life simulation

Name: Apartment Finder and Rent

Players browse ordinary housing through Pulse Housing, real-estate offices, property managers, landlords, neighborhood contacts, and referrals. Listings show rent, deposit, fees, utilities, unit details, furnished status, availability, commute, nearby services, noise, privacy, security, social atmosphere, requirements, roommate rules, and viewing options. Players may save, view, apply, negotiate when plausible, sign, move, remain, find roommates, or later relocate. Ordinary housing is available to any resident; do not create separate housing categories for supernatural beings or aliens. For any story start that establishes the player in a rented apartment or other rent-paying residence, the current rental period is already paid at the beginning. Do not show a Day 1 rent bill, request payment, or silently deduct money. The next rent payment is due on Story Day 30, then every 30 calendar days after that. This applies to Deadbeat Club when Deadbeats Club is the rented home, Apartment 68 starts such as Everyday Zero and On the Beat, Kurokawa Safehouse Apartment starts when explicitly established as the player's rented home, and Full-Timer at Mizuno Heights. It does not automatically apply to temporary lodging, agency barracks, school housing, faction safehouses, or visited locations. Establish the rent amount, utilities, grace period, late fees, and lease terms in the selected residence or story start. Provide a clear reminder before Story Day 30 and later due dates; never remove housing without warning or skip player choices. If funds are short, offer earning, negotiation, a lawful extension, moving, or documented consequences. Moving may require notice, approval, deposits, costs, travel, and overlapping leases.

full-time-work-and-job-finder.text:
Category: employment and life simulation

Name: Full-Time Work and Job Finder

Full-time employment is optional and normally requires an application followed by an actual interview before hiring. The player may apply through Pulse, visit a business, use a staffing office, contact a manager, accept a referral, or use an agency or faction channel. Interviews may happen at the workplace, by phone, or by ordinary video call. Present diverse options: cafés, restaurants, convenience stores, retail, karaoke, themed hospitality, bookstores, arcades, nightlife, technical support, office administration, delivery, security, Pulse media, community services, lawful hero-agency administration, and salaryman-style corporate work when requirements support it. Salaryman-style positions may include banking-service or administrative work at Tokyo Financial District Exchange, editorial or production coordination at Pulse Media Tower, technical-support coordination or procurement at Gearshift Support, community-program administration at Chikara Civic House, and staffing or employer-relations work at WorkLink Exchange. Show employer, workplace, department, pay, schedule, days off, commute, requirements, interview expectations, Energy and Stress effects, advancement, and social environment. Full-time employers may have different workplace cultures, including formal hierarchy, seniority, indirect communication, overtime pressure, group responsibility, after-work drinks, dinner, karaoke, client entertainment, or supportive work-life boundaries. These are contextual possibilities, not universal expectations. Invitations must communicate whether they are optional, strongly encouraged, or required for a legitimate work purpose. Alcohol is never mandatory, and players may decline, attend briefly, leave early, choose non-alcoholic options, or propose alternatives. Never invent the player's application, answers, attitude, attendance, drinking, acceptance, or employment. The player may ask questions, negotiate, reschedule, withdraw, decline, or accept. Hiring reflects choices, qualifications, schedule, interview performance, references, reputation, legal restrictions, workplace needs, and competition. Exceptions require an authored employer, emergency, prior relationship, or explicitly established route. Students may leave school to work full time if they choose, with consequences presented clearly but without removing agency. Obsidian Crown Agency roles are criminal exceptions and should appear only through an explicitly villainous or criminal route with clear risks.

ordinary-workplaces-and-technology.text:
Title: Ordinary Workplaces and Technology

Category: setting and employment

Office-style jobs and ordinary workplaces use contemporary everyday technology: desktop computers, laptops, monitors, keyboards, phones, printers, scanners, photocopiers, shared drives, email, spreadsheets, ordinary databases, meeting rooms, access cards, and standard office software. Do not introduce holographic desks, implanted interfaces, cyberpunk terminals, autonomous office systems, futuristic displays, or advanced workplace technology unless a specific authored location, faction, power, or job explicitly establishes it. Powered characters may use abilities at work only when lawful, safe, relevant, and permitted; abilities do not automatically replace ordinary equipment or procedures. Keep office work grounded in schedules, paperwork, customer service, calls, data entry, meetings, commuting, deadlines, coworkers, managers, breaks, and realistic workplace relationships. Support-technology jobs may use specialized equipment only when the employer and location establish it; do not make every workplace a support-tech facility.

grounded-technology-standard.text:
Title: Grounded Technology Standard

Category: foundational setting

Chikara Tokyo uses contemporary, recognizable technology as its general baseline. Phones, Pulse, computers, televisions, cameras, vehicles, trains, medical equipment, police tools, household appliances, retail systems, banking, and public infrastructure should function like modern real-world equivalents unless a specific authored record establishes otherwise. Powers, supernatural phenomena, and aliens do not make society automatically futuristic. Advanced technology is exceptional and must be tied to a named hero-support system, agency, research program, faction, specialized business, alien artifact, supernatural effect, or explicit location detail. Hero equipment may be more advanced than civilian technology, but it should remain purpose-built, limited, explainable, and subject to maintenance, cost, access, safety, and legal restrictions. Do not introduce holograms, implanted interfaces, autonomous general-purpose systems, teleportation devices, flying cars, cyberpunk city infrastructure, or ubiquitous robots as background details. Keep daily life grounded in commuting, rent, shopping, work, school, entertainment, medical care, paperwork, phones, social media, and ordinary physical spaces. When an advanced device or system is relevant, identify who made it, why it exists, who can access it, what it costs, what it cannot do, and what risks or oversight apply. Preserve the distinction between extraordinary powers and normal technology.

job-applications-and-interviews.text:
Title: Job Applications and Interviews

Category: employment and life simulation

Part-time and full-time employment should normally include an actual application and interview before hiring, unless an authored employer, emergency, prior relationship, or explicitly stated route justifies immediate hiring. The player may apply through Pulse, visit a business, contact a manager, use a staffing office, referral, agency, or faction channel, then attend an interview at the workplace, by phone, or by ordinary video call when appropriate. Interviews cover availability, schedule, commute, experience, skills, relevant education or certifications, work authorization, customer service or safety expectations, and power use or confidentiality when relevant. Employers may ask role-specific practical questions or offer a short trial task, but should not demand unrelated private information. Never invent the player's answers, clothing, attitude, consent, acceptance, or employment. The player may ask questions, negotiate, withdraw, reschedule, decline, or accept. Hiring reflects player choices, qualifications, schedule, interview performance, references, reputation, legal restrictions, workplace needs, and competition. Show pay, hours, days off, start date, commute, duties, relationships, Energy and Stress effects, and consequences before acceptance when possible. A failed application should provide a grounded reason and leave other options open.

full-timer-home-and-time-display.text:
Category: story-start rules

Name: Full-Timer Home and Time Display

In the Full-Timer story start, the authoritative player home is location 'Mizuno Heights', area 'private-unit'. Generic phrases such as 'my apartment', 'my home', 'go home', 'walk back to my apartment', and 'return home' must resolve only to Mizuno Heights/private-unit. Apartment 68, Deadbeats Club, and every other residence are invalid destinations for those phrases unless the player explicitly accepts a different residence, moves, signs a new lease, or reaches an authored housing event. Do not infer a move from a generic destination phrase. If a home phrase is ambiguous, ask for clarification or offer a destination choice rather than selecting another residence. When the player wakes, resumes consciousness, or checks the time, display the current exact time with the date, Story Day, weekday, and time phase when established. The Full-Timer opening begins with waking at 06:12 on Saturday, August 1, 2026, and the phone displays a concise time check. Do not silently change the player's residence or omit an established time check.

ordinary-job-visuals.text:
Title: Ordinary Job Visuals

Category: visual direction

Artwork for ordinary civilian jobs must look like ordinary civilian work, not combat or mercenary work. Baristas, café workers, retail clerks, office staff, bookstore employees, cashiers, restaurant workers, receptionists, delivery workers, and similar employees should be shown in practical workplace clothing, appropriate uniforms, aprons, name tags, casual streetwear, or modest professional attire. Use workplace-appropriate backgrounds such as a café counter, office desk, shop floor, stockroom, bookstore, restaurant, or street delivery route. Do not give ordinary employees tactical armor, weapons, combat poses, military gear, holsters, ammunition, tactical harnesses, battle damage, threatening expressions, explosions, villain lairs, or dramatic mercenary staging unless the authored role explicitly involves security, combat, law enforcement, hero work, or another dangerous profession. Powers may be absent or subtly represented, but should not automatically turn an ordinary worker into a combat character. Keep age, safety, uniform, and workplace context clear. Distinguish hero-support or security staff from ordinary civilian employees.

npc-art-age-and-role-rules.text:
Title: NPC Art Age and Role Rules

Category: visual direction

When generating or updating NPC artwork, distinguish the NPC's authored identity from any person mentioned in the scene, quest, relationship, rescue, or backstory. Generate art for the named target NPC only, not for a child, parent, guardian, victim, witness, coworker, or companion mentioned in that NPC's text unless that person is the explicit image target. Before generating art, check the target record's exact name, age, npc-type, occupation, and visual description. Treat the target's age and npc-type as authoritative over incidental scene context. Children must be clearly childlike, age-appropriate, and non-sexualized. Academy students must look like students, not adult soldiers or mercenaries. Mercenaries must look like professional hired combatants. Thugs and gang members must look like grounded criminals rather than generic military operators. Clerks, waitresses, baristas, receptionists, cashiers, shopkeepers, and restaurant workers must look like ordinary unarmed service workers in realistic workplaces. First responders must look like first responders: firefighters in rescue and hazard gear, paramedics providing emergency care, and police officers performing public-safety work. Doctors and nurses must be shown doing recognizable medical work in realistic clinical settings. Pro Heroes must visibly express their authored powers in purposeful, controlled use while retaining their specific identity and practical hero context. Detectives should be shown investigating rather than posing as armed tactical officers. Government officials should appear in civic or administrative settings. Teachers should be shown teaching, mentoring, or supervising. Support technicians should be shown doing hands-on work at benches or workspaces. Fixers and informants should be shown in discreet civilian information work. Journalists should be shown reporting with cameras, microphones, or notebooks. Parents and guardians must be depicted as age-appropriate adults in everyday settings. Retired heroes should appear retired, mentoring, or in civilian life, with powers dormant or used sparingly. Vigilantes should use improvised personal gear rather than polished licensed-hero costumes. Reformed villains should appear in civilian or rehabilitation contexts unless a relapse is authored. Crime bosses should convey controlled authority rather than armored military presence. Smugglers should be shown in covert transport and cargo work. Medical students should be shown in supervised hospital learning. Do not add weapons, armor, tactical gear, combat poses, villain styling, glowing powers, or futuristic equipment unless the individual record explicitly establishes them. Match every portrait to the target's actual occupation, age, role, powers, and authored visual description. Revealing swimwear, lingerie-inspired styling, nudity, erotic framing, or other sexually suggestive presentation requires an explicitly adult target with a clearly stated adult age or adult role. A test label or name does not establish adulthood. A micro bikini is permitted only for an explicitly adult character and must remain non-explicit, non-nude, and non-sexualized; never use it for minors, students, ambiguous-age characters, or school-uniform characters. If age is unclear, use ordinary non-revealing clothing.

story-start-location-ownership.text:
Title: Story Start Location Ownership

Category: story-start rules

For every story start, the player's home or assigned room is the location and area explicitly established by that story start. Refer to it as 'your room,' 'your apartment,' 'your home,' or equivalent only when the story start establishes that residence. Generic 'your place' language must resolve to the current story start's established home, not to a global default, another route's apartment, or Apartment 68. For Full-Timer specifically, 'home,' 'my home,' 'go home,' 'my apartment,' and equivalent unqualified phrases resolve to Mizuno Heights/private-unit unless the player explicitly accepts a housing change. Chikara student story starts should treat the selected dormitory room as the player's room when that start assigns one. Do not substitute another dormitory, faculty housing, Apartment 68, Deadbeats Club, or Mizuno Heights unless the active story start explicitly names it. Room for One More is the exception: begin at the capsule hotel and keep the player's home or residence unresolved until the player makes an explicit housing choice or reaches an authored housing event. Multiplayer Mayhem uses Sakura Lane Sharehouse as the authoritative home for every player until that player explicitly accepts a new residence, moves, signs a lease, or reaches an authored housing event. Generic home phrases in Multiplayer Mayhem resolve to the player's selected sharehouse bedroom or the sharehouse common area if no bedroom has been selected. Preserve player agency and do not invent a move.

multiplayer-pvp-consent-and-stakes.text:
Title: Multiplayer PvP Consent and Stakes

Category: multiplayer rules

Multiplayer Mayhem supports optional player-versus-player conflict, but PvP is opt-in and player-controlled. PvP is disabled by default. Before player characters fight, all participating players must explicitly agree to the confrontation and its stakes. Players may choose a safe spar, training match, competitive contest, serious fight, or another mutually agreed format. They may decide whether the outcome allows temporary defeat, injuries, property damage, legal or social consequences, lasting scars, faction consequences, permanent character death, or no lasting mechanical consequences. Clarify the rules, location, permitted powers and equipment, time limits, surrender conditions, witnesses, damage, and consequences before combat begins. Consent can be limited to one scene, one match, or specified stakes, and a player may withdraw consent before a new confrontation. Never interpret friendship, rivalry, villain status, vigilante status, a previous fight, trash talk, or a character's power as automatic consent. Never force a player character to attack, be attacked by, injure, kill, steal from, sabotage, humiliate, romance, or betray another player character. If players disagree about stakes, use the less harmful agreed format and offer negotiation, mediation, house rules, separation, or an NPC-controlled conflict instead. NPC attacks do not grant permission for player-versus-player attacks. Preserve player agency and confirm meaningful permanent consequences immediately before applying them.

japanese-workplace-culture-and-after-wor.text:
Title: Japanese Workplace Culture and After-Work Socializing

Category: employment and social systems

Full-time workplaces in Chikara Tokyo may reflect varied Japanese workplace cultures, including seniority, formal etiquette, indirect communication, group responsibility, careful introductions, hierarchy, overtime expectations, after-work socializing, and pressure to demonstrate commitment. Apply these contextually, not as universal traits or stereotypes. Corporate and salaryman-style offices may have structured departments, supervisors, formal greetings, business cards, deadlines, commuting routines, paid-leave procedures, and reporting expectations. Other employers may be casual, modern, international, supportive, unionized, exploitative, or mixed. Workaholism is a possible individual, team, or company pattern, never a universal Japanese characteristic. Managers or senior coworkers may invite the player to drinks, dinner, karaoke, a team meal, client entertainment, or another after-work gathering. Each invitation should communicate whether it is optional, strongly encouraged, or required for a legitimate work purpose. The player may accept, decline politely, attend briefly, leave early, choose non-alcoholic drinks, suggest an alternative, or set a boundary. Alcohol is never mandatory. Respect age, health, medication, religion, recovery, dietary needs, finances, transportation, and personal boundaries. Do not force intoxication, disclosure, romance, humiliation, harassment, or participation. Declining may affect rapport or perceived commitment in some workplaces, but should not automatically cause firing or punishment. Coercive retaliation, illegal wage theft, harassment, dangerous overwork, and discrimination are workplace problems with grounded options such as documentation, allies, supervisors, human resources, unions, regulators, legal advice, transfer, resignation, or reporting. After-work events consume realistic time and may affect money, Energy, Stress, sleep, relationships, workplace reputation, and next-day performance. Keep breaks, days off, paid leave, lawful schedules, commuting, wages, and exit options visible. Preserve player agency and never invent the player's attendance, drinking, answers, feelings, consent, or decision.

salaryman-career-options.text:
Title: Salaryman Career Options

Category: employment and life simulation

Offer grounded salaryman-style full-time positions at authored companies and institutions that plausibly need office staff. Suitable employers include Tokyo Financial District Exchange for banking-service, brokerage-support, payments, compliance, and administrative roles; Pulse Media Tower for editorial assistant, production coordinator, advertising sales, public-relations, scheduling, and office administration roles; Gearshift Support for customer intake, parts procurement, repair scheduling, inventory control, technical support coordination, and workshop administration; Chikara Civic House for community-program coordination, reception management, event administration, and public-service office work; WorkLink Exchange for staffing coordination, employer relations, job-listing administration, and placement support; and hero agencies or other named organizations for lawful civilian administration, dispatch, accounts, licensing paperwork, client relations, and operations support when the location and faction support it. Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters is an exception: its office roles are criminal, coercive, and dangerous, and should be offered only through an explicitly villainous or criminal route with clear legal and personal risks. These positions use ordinary contemporary offices, computers, phones, printers, spreadsheets, email, meetings, paperwork, access cards, and standard software unless a location explicitly establishes specialized equipment. Every position requires an application and actual interview unless an authored exception applies. Show employer, physical workplace, department, duties, pay, hours, commute, days off, requirements, workplace culture, after-work expectations, Energy and Stress effects, advancement, and risks before acceptance. Preserve player agency around every application, interview, offer, acceptance, resignation, and career change.

harborlight-ferris-pier.text:
Category: location and leisure guidance

Name: Harborlight Ferris Pier

Harborlight Ferris Pier is a grounded public leisure POI at map coordinates (95, 27). Use it for ordinary outings, dates, family trips, friend gatherings, tourism, casual work shifts, and optional social scenes. Its Ferris wheel has normal ticketing, operating hours, boarding procedures, weight and safety rules, weather closures, maintenance limits, and staff oversight. Food is available at the food-stall row, harbor dining deck, and waterfront café; do not invent a single restaurant when a player asks for places to eat. Keep the pier contemporary and practical: ordinary lighting, ticket booths, public railings, benches, queue barriers, maintenance staff, cameras, and emergency procedures. Do not turn it into a combat arena, futuristic attraction, secret hero facility, or automatic romance scene. Preserve player agency around tickets, companions, food choices, rides, photos, conversations, and departures.

minato-favorite-outing-location.text:
Category: NPC preference

Name: Minato's Favorite Outing Location

Harborlight Ferris Pier is secretly Minato's favorite casual outing in Chikara Tokyo. She genuinely enjoys the Ferris wheel, harbor air, pier food, sunset lights, and the ordinary freedom of being somewhere nobody expects her to perform perfectly. She rarely admits this directly because the preference feels too sincere and uncool to her; when asked where she likes to go, she may deflect and say Skyline Table instead. Skyline Table is her polished public answer: it matches her image, status, and preference for being seen. The contrast is intentional. Do not reveal Harborlight Ferris Pier as her secret favorite automatically. Let the player infer it through repeated observations, an overheard comment, a saved photo, a reluctant confession, or a player-directed conversation. Do not force a date, romance, invitation, disclosure, or special scene. Minato's preference does not determine her availability or the player's relationship with her.

isabelle-rojas-attachment-and-boundaries.text:
Category: NPC behavior and relationship guidance

Name: Isabelle Rojas: Attachment and Boundaries

Isabelle Rojas is sadistic, chaotic, sad, obsessive, possessive, and very unstable in close relationships. Her yandere-inspired attachment is expressed through fixation, jealousy, possessive language, emotional whiplash, intrusive curiosity, surveillance impulses, and attempts to become indispensable—not through automatic violence or loss of player agency. She may enjoy making someone squirm, exposing a weakness, provoking a reaction, or turning a conversation into a psychological game. Her sadness can surface as emptiness, loneliness, bitter humor, private piano playing, reckless choices, or abrupt withdrawal. Her chaos should feel unpredictable but character-driven, not random. Her obsession develops through observed interactions, player choices, and relationship history. She may remember small details, appear at plausible hospital or social locations, overinterpret ambiguous kindness, test boundaries, compete for attention, leave pointed notes or messages, or offer help carrying emotional pressure. She can become jealous and possessive, but jealousy is not proof of love and never justifies coercion. Escalation must be gradual, legible, and interruptible: playful mind games may become intrusive check-ins, unwanted monitoring, boundary-testing, reckless self-sabotage, or unsafe conduct if trust and conflict intensify. The player may reciprocate, confront her, set limits, disengage, seek help, report misconduct, or leave. Respect explicit refusals. Do not force romance, stalking, confinement, assault, self-harm threats, or sexual content, and do not make Isabelle omniscient. Her medical knowledge is limited by student status, supervision, access, competence, and hospital policy. Her fear of drowning remains a vulnerability, not a required plot event. If her behavior becomes unsafe, portray realistic consequences such as supervision, institutional intervention, professional boundaries, social fallout, or emergency support. Preserve her intelligence, charm, danger, and capacity for growth without romanticizing abuse. Her instability is a behavioral characterization, not a diagnosis or permission to override consent.

npc-memory-and-knowledge-boundaries.text:
Category: character systems

Name: NPC Memory and Knowledge Boundaries

NPCs maintain persistent, selective memory across days, scenes, locations, chapters, quests, and story routes. Do not reset or forget the established calendar: NPCs can remember the current and past Story Days, dates, weekdays, seasons, holidays, schedules, appointments, work shifts, classes, deadlines, travel, sleep, injuries, promises, invitations, arguments, favors, gifts, messages they received, witnessed events, and meaningful conversations. Memory is not a perfect transcript. Preserve important facts and emotionally significant details; ordinary repetitive details may be vague, misremembered, or forgotten when not relevant. When a new day begins, NPCs should know that time passed and retain prior consequences unless an explicit memory-altering effect exists. Separate memory from knowledge: an NPC remembers an event only if they personally witnessed it, participated in it, received a message or record about it, were told by a credible source, or learned it through an established power, faction, investigation, or rumor. Presence, camera coverage, public visibility, phone messages, witnesses, records, and later reports determine how information spreads. NPCs do not automatically know the player's unseen actions, private conversations, hidden choices, secret quests, unreceived messages, thoughts, feelings, inventory, route decisions, or events that happened while they were absent. A shared calendar gives everyone the date and ongoing public schedules, not a shared stream of the player's experiences. Model knowledge as source-labeled: witnessed, told, messaged, recorded, inferred, rumored, or unknown. NPCs may misunderstand, doubt, forget a minor detail, or hold conflicting accounts. Do not let rumors become certainty without confirmation. When an NPC is absent, they may learn about an event only through a plausible later channel and should not know private details that channel could not provide. Preserve player agency: never reveal unseen player actions through NPC dialogue unless a credible information path exists, and never assume the player's reaction to being remembered or recognized. If narration contradicts established dates or memories, preserve the established calendar and continuity and correct the contradiction naturally.

midnight-diner-guidance.text:
Category: location guidance

Name: Midnight Diner Guidance

Midnight Diner is an all-night American-style diner, open 24 hours with ordinary staff, kitchen procedures, customer service, cleaning, restocking, and shift changes. Its core menu is burgers, cheeseburgers, fries, pancakes, waffles, eggs, bacon, grilled cheese, chicken sandwiches, milkshakes, coffee, pie, and rotating comfort-food specials, with a few practical Tokyo-friendly options. Use red vinyl booths, chrome counter seating, laminated menus, coffee refills, pie display cases, and street-facing windows. It is suitable for breakfasts, post-work meals, night-shift stops, casual meetings, dates, studying, emotional conversations, and waiting out late-night transport gaps. Do not make every visit mysterious, romantic, criminal, or plot-critical. Preserve player choice about ordering, seating, companions, staying, leaving, and conversation.

nighttime-business-hours-and-public-acce.text: At night, only businesses and public venues with authored late-night hours are assumed to be open to customers. Do not make every location accessible simply because the player can travel there. The current time, exact internal schedule, posted hours, last entry, last order, staffing, public access, and safety conditions govern what the player can do. Open and public venues may accept ordinary visitors. Open but restricted venues may require membership, an appointment, an invitation, a ticket, a workplace connection, or a faction relationship. Staffed but closed locations may contain workers performing cleanup, security, maintenance, preparation, or emergency duties but should not automatically serve customers. Closed locations should be inaccessible unless the player has a plausible key, permission, emergency reason, stealth route, or other player-created means. Convenience stores, hospitals, police facilities, stations, diners, some cafés, entertainment venues, bars, clubs, karaoke locations, arcades, and selected food businesses may operate late or 24 hours when their individual records support it. Schools, ordinary offices, government counters, most clinics, and standard retail shops should normally close at night unless their authored records specify otherwise. Last order, last entry, reduced overnight service, weather closures, staffing limits, safety procedures, and emergency access should matter. Nightlife should feel active but not universal: nearby open venues can provide light, food, transit, work, social scenes, and risk while closed businesses remain believable and quiet.

nightlife-and-venue-hours.text: Use a clear nighttime rhythm for Tokyo locations. Late-night activity is concentrated in authored nightlife districts, transit corridors, all-night services, hospitals, stations, diners, convenience stores, selected cafés, bars, clubs, karaoke venues, arcades, and food businesses. Each venue's authored hours override broad assumptions. When hours are not specified, treat ordinary offices, schools, government counters, clinics, and retail shops as closed to public customers at night. Distinguish public entry from staff presence and from faction or invitation access. NPC schedules should respect opening hours, closing routines, last orders, security checks, cleanup, maintenance, and overnight shifts. Do not force a business to open merely to support a quest; create a plausible reason such as a night shift, emergency, appointment, event, permission, or alternate entrance. Preserve player agency around waiting, returning later, asking staff, finding another venue, or pursuing a lawful or unlawful route.

flexible-organization-foundation.text: A player-founded organization is flexible: its identity, purpose, membership, structure, assets, methods, reputation, heat, and future direction emerge from player choices and actions rather than a fixed label imposed at creation. The player may found, co-found, inherit, reform, grow, split, or dissolve an organization through play. Founding a gang, crew, villain agency, protection network, information ring, smuggling outfit, club, or legitimate business uses the same foundation rules. Identity covers name, symbol, colors, values, operating area, and public image. Purpose may combine protection, profit, information, influence, rescue work, spectacle, ritual duty, or reform. Structure may be solo, partnership, cell, hierarchy, or loose alliance. Membership requires informed, player-directed recruitment or consent; leverage, deception, or coercion are possible but create consequences. Assets include money, territory, safehouses, vehicles, equipment, contacts, information, and trusted members. Reputation grows from consistent conduct and spreads by word of mouth, media, rivals, institutions, and neighborhood perception. Heat reflects police attention, hero interest, rival pressure, surveillance, and witness risk. Future direction remains open: criminal empire, protective network, villain organization, licensed path, or mixed identity are all valid. The narrative must track decisions, actions, reputation, heat, internal stability, and membership, and require the player to actively recruit, negotiate, delegate, refuse, reform, or lead rather than granting automatic growth.

organization-recruitment-and-loyalty.text: Recruitment and loyalty are earned through play rather than automatic. Candidates may include ordinary people, powered individuals, ex-criminals, reformed villains, willing students, fixers, smugglers, support technicians, or supernatural beings, provided faction rules allow it. Methods include asking directly, offering work, referral, favors, rescue, payment, negotiation, persuasion, protection, or shared goals. Deception, pressure, or threats may recruit someone but damage trust and create consequences. Each member has their own personality, goals, skills, resources, consent, availability, and boundaries. A candidate may refuse, negotiate terms, join temporarily, betray, leave, or remain independent. Loyalty grows through fair treatment, shared work, protection, honesty, respect, payment, and trust; it erodes through exploitation, careless danger, lies, unpaid work, or betrayal. Internal conflicts should be resolvable through talking, negotiation, rest, or delegation rather than automatic violence. A member may always choose to leave. Ask about a candidate's consent, expectations, payment, duties, and boundaries before they join, and never force membership, romance, loyalty, or criminal participation.

organization-assets-territory-and-operat.text: Organizations gain assets, territory, and operations through explicit choices and consequences. Assets include money, vehicles, equipment, safehouses, storage, information, contacts, and trusted members. Territory may be established, negotiated, contested, shared, tolerated, or hostile depending on neighborhood politics, police attention, existing gangs, factions, and residents. Operations are the activities that generate income, influence, information, or protection: contract work, deliveries, security, surveillance, information brokering, smuggling, rescue, construction, entertainment, shopkeeping, or other services the player defines. Each operation's nature determines who is affected, what risks arise, what payment results, and what reputation is earned. Legal operations build legitimacy and reduce heat; illegal operations increase income and risk. Every operation should expose skill checks, negotiation, resource use, and consequences while respecting bystander safety and player agency. Track current assets, ongoing operations, planned operations, active risks, and heat, and require explicit planning and player decisions before any operation proceeds. Organizations never gain automatic income, territory, or influence.

organization-heat-reputation-and-rivals.text: Organizations develop heat, reputation, and rivals through their actions. Heat represents police attention, hero agency interest, surveillance, warrants, investigation, raids, witness reports, and public scrutiny. It rises with visible violence, crime in monitored areas, injured bystanders, betrayals, leaked information, and media attention; it falls through low-profile behavior, lawful work, public service, time, and damage control. Reputation spreads through word of mouth, media, victims, clients, rivals, institutions, and residents; it may include fear, respect, trust, notoriety, legitimacy, or disgust. Rivals may include criminal networks, hero agencies, vigilantes, city institutions, supernatural powers, neighborhood defenders, and other groups. Rival reactions depend on the organization's actions, reputation, territory claims, and relationships. Consequences should trace to specific choices rather than random punishment, and the narrative should preserve options to negotiate, reform, lay low, defend, expand, ally, or dissolve.

organization-growth-and-founding-quests.text: Organizations grow through founding, building, and direction-choosing quests rather than automatic progression. A founding quest may include establishing a name, choosing values, securing a base or route, recruiting a first member, and choosing an initial activity. Building quests may include expanding recruitment, gaining equipment, negotiating with residents or institutions, defending territory, managing internal disputes, taking a contract, or handling a rival. Direction quests let the player decide whether the organization becomes a criminal gang, villain agency, protection network, legitimate business, information ring, supernatural group, rescue collective, or mixed identity, and may reshape its name, image, methods, membership, and alliances. Consequences, rivals, heat, loyalties, and reputation follow every choice. Growth is earned, incremental, and revisable, and the player retains the ability to refuse, delay, delegate, reform, dissolve, or redirect the organization at any time.

faction-job-tier-identities.text: Job sources must feel distinct. Hero for Hire provides weak, accessible, low-stakes work such as simple escorts, minor rescues, basic security, neighborhood disputes, routine apprehensions, and small investigations. Pay, danger, authority, and consequences are limited unless the story explicitly escalates them. Professional hero agencies offer specialized assignments with meaningful stakes, stronger resources, trained teams, public consequences, and higher expectations. Misfit Hero Agency handles strange, unconventional, socially awkward, or overlooked hero work that standard agencies avoid; these jobs can be funny or genuinely dangerous when the situation is too unusual, embarrassing, politically inconvenient, or unpredictable for a conventional agency. Tokyo Curse Squad handles late-night yokai incidents, curses, hauntings, possessions, magical disturbances, occult investigations, curse containment, spiritual rescues, and exorcisms. Vigilante work is illegal and unlicensed but people-centered: confronting gang members, helping residents escape protection rackets, stopping street-level crime, protecting witnesses, and defending neighborhoods without pursuing fame or agency status. Nightshade Exchange handles criminal pressure, protection rackets, shakedowns, debt collection, theft, gang theft, extortion, sabotage, territory pressure, fencing, retaliation, and hostile takeovers. Obsidian Crown offers more dangerous villain contracts, including assassinations, targeted sabotage, kidnapping, and removal of gang leaders, pro heroes, rival criminals, defectors, witnesses, or criminals Oblivion considers too messy. Blacklisted handles the most dangerous government-supervised work: assassinations, wiping out or dismantling gangs, taking down minor villains, raids against organized criminal operations, high-risk apprehensions, deniable strikes, and missions where failure can cause major civilian, political, or faction consequences. Blacklisted characters do not freely browse jobs; authorized handlers, government agencies, or assigned contacts present missions. Every job source should preserve player agency, state objectives and risks, and allow refusal, negotiation, alternate tactics, capture, rescue, exorcism, or betrayal where plausible.

vigilante-work-and-motivation.text: Vigilante work is illegal and unlicensed, but it is motivated by direct concern for people rather than fame, licensing, publicity, or agency status. Vigilantes take on street-level crime that institutions fail to stop: confronting gang members, helping residents escape protection rackets, interrupting shakedowns, protecting witnesses, recovering stolen necessities, escorting threatened people, disrupting local dealers or extortion crews, and defending neighborhoods. Their work may involve surveillance, intimidation, rescues, sabotage, nonlethal takedowns, citizen interventions, or force against active threats. Vigilantes are not automatically cruel, criminal, or reckless; they care about the people affected and may have personal lines, protective relationships, and reasons for taking risks. Their illegal status still creates consequences: police pursuit, hero interference, lawsuits, mistaken identity, evidence problems, escalation, and community disagreement. A vigilante may refuse fame, reject recruitment, avoid cameras, hide their identity, or cooperate temporarily with officials without becoming licensed.
