A clean connection does weapon-tier damage for the weapon used, about 55-70, modified by skill, positioning, defenses and declared intent, and the opponent loses the rhythm of their next action. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It needs line of sight and a moment of observation; it works poorly on an opponent whose power has no visible tell, on crowds, or while the character is pinned or blinded. It grants no supernatural effect and cannot cancel a power, only beat its timing.

No Power: Contingency Play.name: No Power: Contingency Play
No Power: Contingency Play.description: The character produces a countermeasure they plausibly prepared and carry, chosen for the opponent in front of them: a light source against darkness, an insulated barrier against current, a restraint against a brute, a smoke screen against a marksman. For a short exchange, one opponent's power is hampered and the character follows through with a committed attack; a clean connection does about 70-90, modified by the weapon, defenses and how well the counter fits. Costs 2 Combat Energy and drains Energy as real physical exertion. The item is spent or damaged after use, it must be something the character could own, and it cannot stop a power outright, affect more than one main opponent, or work against a threat they had no reason to expect.

No Power: Human Limit.name: No Power: Human Limit
No Power: Human Limit.description: The character commits to one continuous, rehearsed sequence against a single opponent: closing distance through terrain and cover, breaking guard with gear or feint, and delivering a finishing technique with their chosen weapon or style. A clean connection does about 90-120, modified by defenses, preparation and how the opening was earned; it can also end in a secure restraint instead of damage. It spends the character's Ultimate Charge and leaves them exhausted, with Energy badly drained and a real chance of a pulled muscle, cracked rib or worse. It cannot affect more than one main opponent, cannot cancel or steal a power, and it fails if the character has no route, footing or line to the target. It is entirely human and grants no supernatural effect.

Elemental Power: Tempered Lance.name: Elemental Power: Tempered Lance
Elemental Power: Tempered Lance.description: Compress the chosen element into a single tight lance, beam, spike or bolt aimed along one line. A clean connection deals roughly 55-70 damage, modified by element, available material, range, defenses, Power Strain and the player's choice; because the force is narrow, it causes far less spillover damage than a burst and rarely hits what the character did not aim at. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It needs material or energy to draw on as the player defined, loses strength quickly at long range, and cannot curve around cover unless the element itself could. Firing it repeatedly in one scene raises Power Strain fast.

Elemental Power: Dominion Field.name: Elemental Power: Dominion Field
Elemental Power: Dominion Field.description: Take hold of the chosen element across an area about the size of a large room or a short street section for a short exchange. Inside the field the character can raise or remove barriers and footing, hinder movement, sense motion through the element, and strike from any point within it for roughly 70-90 damage on a clean connection, modified by element, material, defenses, Power Strain and choice. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain each exchange it is held. It cannot reach outside its edge, cannot conjure material that is not present, and anyone or anything in the field, allies and property included, is affected unless the character spends attention to spare them. Breaking concentration ends it.

Elemental Power: Unbound Element.name: Elemental Power: Unbound Element
Elemental Power: Unbound Element.description: Release the chosen element at full scale for one decisive action: a firestorm across a plaza, a flood surge down a street, a wall of stone the height of a building, a lightning strike called down on a point. Against a target caught in it, a clean connection deals roughly 90-120 damage, modified by element, material, defenses, Power Strain and the player's choice, and everything in the area is affected. It spends the full Ultimate Charge and inflicts heavy Power Strain; afterward the character's power is sluggish or locked for the rest of the scene. It cannot be aimed finely, cannot spare bystanders by default, cannot exceed the material actually present, and cannot destroy a district or kill a named opponent outright.

Mutation Power: Honed Form.name: Mutation Power: Honed Form
Mutation Power: Honed Form.description: Commit the character's one mutation fully to a single decisive action: a strike with claws or a reinforced limb, a lunge using reach, a sense pushed to pick out one heartbeat in a crowd, or armour braced to take a hit meant for someone else. As an attack it deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by the target's defenses, Power Strain and how well the mutation suits the job. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It cannot create a second mutation, change what the mutation is, or reach beyond the body's physical limits; repeated use in a scene adds Power Strain as soreness, torn skin or shaking muscles.

Mutation Power: Surge State.name: Mutation Power: Surge State
Mutation Power: Surge State.description: Push the character's mutation into a heightened state for a short fight or crisis. Everything the mutation already does is markedly stronger: armour turns blades and small-arms fire, claws or limbs strike for roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, senses read a whole building, reach crosses a room. Defenses, Power Strain and fit still modify the result. Costs 2 Combat Energy to enter and adds heavy Power Strain when it ends, more the longer it is held. It cannot change the mutation into something else, cannot be concealed while active, and holding it past the body's tolerance causes real injury such as torn muscle, bleeding or a collapse.

Mutation Power: Apex Form.name: Mutation Power: Apex Form
Mutation Power: Apex Form.description: For one defining action the character's mutation runs at its absolute peak. Used as an attack it delivers roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Power Strain and fit; used defensively or for a feat, it achieves one thing ordinary bodies and lesser powers cannot, such as shrugging off a blow that would kill or breaking through a reinforced barrier. Costs a full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain afterward: exhaustion, injury, bleeding or a collapse once the scene allows. It cannot change the mutation into another, cannot kill a named NPC outright, and leaves the body too spent to repeat it soon.

Parasite: Living Arsenal.name: Parasite: Living Arsenal
Parasite: Living Arsenal.description: Grow a chosen adaptation and keep it through a short exchange, switching it once for another without letting go: a grown weapon becomes armored skin, a burst of speed becomes a new sense. A committed attack with a grown weapon deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by the adaptation, the host's condition, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. Afterwards the parasite takes its due: hunger rises, the skin aches, or a small change lingers into the next scene. It cannot heal serious wounds, affect anyone but the host, or hold more than one adaptation at full strength at once.

Parasite: Overgrowth Form.name: Parasite: Overgrowth Form
Parasite: Overgrowth Form.description: Let the parasite reshape the whole body into a combat form for a fight: armored hide that soaks a blow, reach across a room, and grown weapons on demand. Strikes in this form deal roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by the form, defenses, the host's condition and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain to enter, and more each exchange it is held. When it ends the parasite is ravenous, a visible change stays for days, and dropping the form badly hurt can leave the host shaking and slow. It does not heal the host, cannot infect or control anyone else, and cannot be hidden while it lasts.

Parasite: Final Molt.name: Parasite: Final Molt
Parasite: Final Molt.description: The parasite sheds damaged tissue and regrows the host into an apex form for a few moments. One committed strike in this form deals roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain, and the molt shrugs off part of a fresh injury, enough to stay standing, not to be whole. Costs Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain. Afterwards the host crashes: barely able to move, ravenous, and carrying a permanent change chosen with the player. It cannot heal anyone else, cannot undo death, does not spread the parasite, and cannot be used again until the host has fed and rested.

Psychic Power: Focused Spike.name: Psychic Power: Focused Spike
Psychic Power: Focused Spike.description: The character drives their psychic power into one target they can see or clearly sense, as a sharp mental shock, a burst of sensory static or a break in concentration. A clean connection does about 55-70 as pain, disorientation and nausea, modified by the target's will, training, distraction and the character's Power Strain; against a powered target it can also spoil the focus of their next power use. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It cannot plant thoughts, read memories or control a player character, and a strongly resisting or shielded mind takes much less. Pushing it through barriers, crowds or long distance adds Power Strain as headaches and nosebleeds.

Psychic Power: Room Resonance.name: Psychic Power: Room Resonance
Psychic Power: Room Resonance.description: The character opens their power across a room, a train car or a street corner. They sense the emotional state of everyone in range and can find hostile intent, fear or concealment among them, then press one broad feeling across the area: calm, dread, focus or doubt. Willing people take it fully; unwilling people may resist with will, training or distraction, and determined individuals act anyway. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain, rising sharply with crowd size and duration. It cannot give commands, read specific memories, control a player character, or make anyone act against their core intent. Holding it too long brings migraines and dulled senses for the rest of the scene.

Psychic Power: Mind Overload.name: Psychic Power: Mind Overload
Psychic Power: Mind Overload.description: The character pours the full force of their psychic power into a single target they can see or clearly sense. A clean connection does about 90-120 as overwhelming sensory and mental shock, modified by the target's will, training, psychic defenses and the character's Power Strain, and the target's power use falters for a short exchange. It spends the character's Ultimate Charge and inflicts heavy Power Strain: nosebleeds, shaking and dulled senses, with a real risk of being unable to use their power for the rest of the scene. It affects one target only, cannot plant commands, erase memories or control a player character, and a strong will or another psychic can shrug off much of it.

Construct Power: Articulated Construct.name: Construct Power: Articulated Construct
Construct Power: Articulated Construct.description: Create one construct with moving parts that performs a defined action or short sequence: a grappling arm that catches and pulls, a folding barrier that snaps open, a spring platform that launches an ally, a cage that closes on a target. If the player's definition allows striking constructs, a clean hit deals roughly 55-70 damage, modified by size, durability, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. The construct does only what it was designed for; asked to improvise, it jams or breaks. It cannot be alive, think, power itself like a real machine, or outlast its substance's duration, and holding it under attack costs Power Strain.

Construct Power: Raised Architecture.name: Construct Power: Raised Architecture
Construct Power: Raised Architecture.description: Build one large structure from the defined substance for a scene: a bridge, staircase, shelter, barricade line, enclosure or set of walls covering roughly a large room or a short street section. It can hold several people, block heavy fire, or redirect a crowd or a vehicle, and a falling section or a collapsing wall can deal roughly 70-90 damage to someone caught under it if the player chooses. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain; each heavy blow it absorbs adds more. It cannot contain functioning machinery or living parts, cannot become stronger than its substance, and when the character's focus breaks the whole structure fails at once.

Construct Power: Masterwork Edifice.name: Construct Power: Masterwork Edifice
Construct Power: Masterwork Edifice.description: Create one masterwork construct at full scale and full complexity for a short, decisive stretch: a fortress around a block, a colossal frame that moves as designed, a giant shield over a crowd, or a tool big enough to stop a vehicle or hold up a collapsing structure. If it strikes, a clean connection deals roughly 90-120 damage, modified by defenses, durability and Power Strain. It spends the full Ultimate Charge and inflicts heavy Power Strain, and the character's power is near locked for the rest of the scene once it fades. It cannot be alive or think, cannot last beyond the scene, cannot exceed the substance's rules, and cannot kill a named opponent outright.

Mobility Power: Slipstream Strike.name: Mobility Power: Slipstream Strike
Mobility Power: Slipstream Strike.description: Fold a strike into the character's movement: close distance in a blink, hit while the target is still turning, and be out of the counter. It deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by defenses, momentum, the destination's footing and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It stays within the character's established range and needs whatever the movement normally needs (sight, open air, a run-up). It cannot pass through what the power cannot pass through, and a blind or crowded arrival risks collision, injury or collateral.

Mobility Power: Relay Rush.name: Mobility Power: Relay Rush
Mobility Power: Relay Rush.description: Run the character's movement as a rapid chain across a scene, or bring others along. Options: carry a few willing people or one heavy load out of danger, cross a large area in moments, or hit several targets in quick succession for roughly 70-90 each on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and significant Power Strain and Energy. It respects the power's range and needs; passengers can be hurt by a bad arrival, and an unwilling target cannot be carried. It cannot cross sealed or warded spaces the power could not already enter.

Mobility Power: Vanishing Point.name: Mobility Power: Vanishing Point
Mobility Power: Vanishing Point.description: One impossible movement: the character resolves a whole situation in a single run, reaching every point that matters in a scene before others react. As an attack it lands a decisive hit for roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain; as a rescue it moves everyone it can reach out of immediate danger. Costs a full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, leaving the character exhausted and slow for some time. It obeys the power's range and needs, cannot carry the unwilling, cannot enter sealed or warded spaces, and cannot kill a named NPC outright.

Energy Power: Redirected Surge.name: Energy Power: Redirected Surge
Energy Power: Redirected Surge.description: Catch an incoming attack of the user's own energy type, or draw from a nearby source the player defined (a power line, a fire, the sun), hold it a breath, and release it with the user's own output added. A returned discharge deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by how much was caught, range, defenses, available Energy and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. Catching more than the body can hold costs Power Strain and burns the user. It cannot absorb a different kind of energy, physical force or ordinary weapons, and a missed catch takes the full hit.

Energy Power: Overload Bloom.name: Energy Power: Overload Bloom
Energy Power: Overload Bloom.description: Release the energy outward over an area the size of a room or a short stretch of street: a wave of heat, a flash of light, a crackling storm. Everyone in it takes roughly 70-90 at full power on a clean hit, modified by distance from the user, cover, defenses, available Energy and Power Strain; the user can try to spare chosen people, which takes control and weakens the whole bloom. Costs 2 Combat Energy, a chunk of Energy, and real Power Strain. It damages property, cannot be aimed precisely, and a spent user afterwards manages only sparks.

Energy Power: Critical Mass.name: Energy Power: Critical Mass
Energy Power: Critical Mass.description: Gather all available Energy plus whatever the user can draw from nearby, then release it as one discharge in a chosen line or point. It deals roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by range, defenses and Power Strain, and anything behind the target in its path is hit too. Costs Ultimate Charge, all remaining Energy, and heavy Power Strain. After it, the user can only spark for the rest of the scene, may be burned or blinded by their own output, and pushing further risks injury. It cannot be dialled down for a crowd, cannot be split between targets, and is impossible to hide.

Cursed Item: Paid in Full.name: Cursed Item: Paid in Full
Cursed Item: Paid in Full.description: The character invokes their item's defined benefit at greater strength by paying its established curse up front, more heavily than usual. If the benefit is a weapon or harmful effect, a clean connection does about 55-70, modified by defenses, the item's limits and Power Strain; if it is protective, sensory or utility, it works more fully or for longer within the same rules. Costs 1 Combat Energy, plus the item's curse paid in the scene as the player defined it, and Power Strain. It cannot provide a benefit the player did not define, cannot avoid or postpone its curse, and does nothing if the item is not in the character's possession or reach.

Cursed Item: Unsealed Bargain.name: Cursed Item: Unsealed Bargain
Cursed Item: Unsealed Bargain.description: The character opens the item's deeper bargain and calls on its unsealed mode or second defined benefit, at a broader scale than before: a wider area, a heavier blow, a longer protection or a stranger effect, as the player defined it. If it deals harm, a clean connection does about 70-90, modified by defenses, the item's limits and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy, real Power Strain, and the deeper curse paid in the scene exactly as agreed. It cannot provide anything outside the defined bargain, cannot shift its curse onto others unless that was the agreed cost, and it fails if the item is lost, sealed or broken.

Cursed Item: Final Clause.name: Cursed Item: Final Clause
Cursed Item: Final Clause.description: The character invokes the item's full authority for one decisive act, the strongest form of its defined benefit. If harmful, a clean connection does about 90-120, modified by defenses and the item's nature; if protective or utility, it achieves the largest effect the item's established rules allow for a short span. It spends the character's Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, and the item exacts its deepest curse in the scene, with a lasting consequence the player agreed to. It cannot resurrect, cannot instantly kill a named opponent, cannot grant undefined powers, and it announces the item's presence to anyone attuned to such objects.

Technological Hero: Integrated Module.name: Technological Hero: Integrated Module
Technological Hero: Integrated Module.description: Activate a second, player-defined core function now built into the technology: a weapon system, sensor package, grapple or thruster rig, shield emitter, drone link or similar. Offensive modules deal roughly 55-70 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, battery, heat, damage to the device and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. Each use draws battery and builds heat that the narrator tracks in the scene, and a damaged or overheated module degrades or shuts down. It only does what it was built to do, needs maintenance through Support Engineering, and stops working if the device is taken, hacked or run flat.

Technological Hero: Full Deployment.name: Technological Hero: Full Deployment
Technological Hero: Full Deployment.description: Switch the whole technology into its combat or rescue configuration for a short exchange: armor sealed, all defined modules powered and linked, sensors sharing data. While deployed the character moves, strikes and protects at a clearly higher level, and a fully committed attack deals roughly 70-90 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, heat, battery and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and drains battery heavily; heat climbs every exchange it runs. It cannot add functions that were never built, and if a key component is damaged while deployed, related modules can fail together. Afterward the gear needs repair and recharge before it can deploy again.

Technological Hero: Redline Protocol.name: Technological Hero: Redline Protocol
Technological Hero: Redline Protocol.description: Override every safety limit in the technology for one decisive action: a full-power strike, an all-systems shield, a maximum-thrust rescue, a sensor sweep that cuts through every countermeasure the design can handle. A fully committed attack deals roughly 90-120 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, battery, heat and Power Strain. It spends the full Ultimate Charge and leaves the technology heavily damaged, overheated or drained, often unusable until repaired, and the character takes Power Strain from the backlash. It only pushes functions that exist, cannot be repeated until the device is fixed, and cannot kill a named opponent outright.

Supernatural: Veil Breach.name: Supernatural: Veil Breach
Supernatural: Veil Breach.description: Let the character's supernatural condition reach outward in force, shaped by its origin: a blight, a burning mark, grasping shadow, a ghostly cold, as fits the player's concept. As an attack it deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Power Strain, and whether the target is unusually vulnerable or resistant to that kind of force. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It must follow the condition's activation, cost and weakness; if the weakness is present it fails or rebounds. It cannot grant a new supernatural nature or ignore the origin's rules.

Supernatural: Awakened Aspect.name: Supernatural: Awakened Aspect
Supernatural: Awakened Aspect.description: Enter a deeper state of the character's supernatural condition for a scene. Its existing effects grow markedly stronger and broader; offensive manifestations deal roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain, and the condition may resist ordinary harm its origin should shrug off. Costs 2 Combat Energy to enter and heavy Power Strain when it ends. In this state the origin's weakness bites harder, and exposure to it can force the state to break. It cannot create abilities outside the origin, and the character remains themself, acting as the player decides.

Supernatural: Sovereign Rite.name: Supernatural: Sovereign Rite
Supernatural: Sovereign Rite.description: Call the full depth of the character's supernatural origin into one defining effect. As an attack it delivers roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Power Strain and the target's affinity to that force; otherwise it achieves one great effect true to the origin, such as banishing a lesser entity or sealing a haunted space. Costs a full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, and leaves the character vulnerable to the origin's weakness for a time. It cannot resurrect the dead, kill a named NPC outright, control a player character, or act outside the origin's rules.

Spirit Manifestation: Barrage Rush.name: Spirit Manifestation: Barrage Rush
Spirit Manifestation: Barrage Rush.description: The character summons their manifestation and drives it into a rapid flurry of strikes against one opponent within its established range, usually with a shouted callout in the user's own voice. A clean connection does about 55-70 across the flurry, modified by defenses, the manifestation's established form and the user's Power Strain, and it can knock a lighter opponent off their feet. Costs 1 Combat Energy. The manifestation does not speak and does not act on its own initiative; it cannot strike beyond its established range, and any blow it takes in return is felt by the user as Power Strain.

Spirit Manifestation: Second Verse.name: Spirit Manifestation: Second Verse
Spirit Manifestation: Second Verse.description: The character directs their manifestation to use its unique, player-defined ability: one clear supernatural effect fitting its name and nature, applied to a target, object or small area within its range. If the effect is directly harmful, a clean connection does about 70-90, modified by defenses and Power Strain; otherwise it creates one strong advantage, such as halting, sealing, binding or redirecting something. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain. It cannot control minds, revive anyone, affect things outside the established ability, or work beyond the manifestation's range, and the manifestation never speaks or acts independently.

Spirit Manifestation: Final Encore.name: Spirit Manifestation: Final Encore
Spirit Manifestation: Final Encore.description: The character pushes their manifestation to full power for one decisive assault: a relentless barrage combined with its unique ability against a single opponent, usually with the user's own shouted callout. A clean connection does about 90-120, modified by defenses, the ability's established limits and the user's Power Strain. It spends the character's Ultimate Charge and costs heavy Power Strain; every blow the manifestation takes in return is felt doubly, and afterward the manifestation may be unable to appear for the rest of the scene. It affects one main opponent, cannot instantly kill a named opponent, and the manifestation never speaks or acts independently.

Invoker: Seal-Woven Spell.name: Invoker: Seal-Woven Spell
Invoker: Seal-Woven Spell.description: Cast a strengthened form of the character's own Invocation Magic, channelled through the Seal hand: an offensive spell, barrier, binding, reinforcement, ward, trap or support technique matching what the player established in play. An offensive casting deals roughly 55-70 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, range and Power Strain; defensive and support castings give a matching protective or utility effect. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It works whether or not the Invocation is manifested, belongs to the Invoker rather than the Invocation, and cannot borrow the Invocation's class abilities, command it, or spend a Command Seal.

Invoker: Pact Resonance.name: Invoker: Pact Resonance
Invoker: Pact Resonance.description: Offer a resonance through the Pact: the Invoker casts their own Invocation Magic in step with the manifested Invocation's action, and if the Invocation chooses to join, the two efforts combine into one strike, barrier, rescue or maneuver. A combined attack deals roughly 70-90 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Bond, Power Strain and both partners' choices. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain for the Invoker. The Invocation acts on its own judgment and can decline or alter the plan; a low Bond weakens or wastes the resonance. It cannot force obedience, replace a Command Seal, use the Invocation's abilities without it, or work while the Invocation is absent.

Invoker: Shared Legend.name: Invoker: Shared Legend
Invoker: Shared Legend.description: With the manifested Invocation's agreement and a strong Bond, the Invoker pours their Invocation Magic into the Pact for one decisive combined act: the Invocation's Legendary Release stabilized and empowered by the Invoker, or the Invoker's own greatest spell carried by the legend's weight. A clean connection deals roughly 90-120 damage, modified by defenses, Bond, Power Strain and both partners' choices. It spends the full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, leaving the Invoker near lockout for the scene. The Invocation may refuse or change the act; it cannot be forced except by a Command Seal. It cannot kill a named opponent outright, resurrect anyone, or erase the Invocation's will.

Magical Power: Bound Formula.name: Magical Power: Bound Formula
Magical Power: Bound Formula.description: A prepared working of the character's tradition, readied ahead of a scene and released with a short word or gesture: a stronger bolt, a firmer ward, a binding that holds a little longer, a revealing that sees through more. A fully formed offensive working deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by preparation, components, defenses and Power Strain; wards and utilities resolve by their actual effect. Costs 1 Combat Energy. Without its requirements it fails or misfires, and it cannot exceed what the tradition allows.

Magical Power: Grand Circle.name: Magical Power: Grand Circle
Magical Power: Grand Circle.description: Perform a field ritual of the character's tradition: a working that covers an area, binds a significant foe, wards a building, or releases an offensive effect over a zone, dealing roughly 70-90 on a clean connection to those caught, modified by preparation, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and heavy Power Strain. It requires time, components and concentration; interruption makes it fail or misfire. It cannot exceed the tradition's rules, cannot be cast without its requirements, and any bargain involved demands its due.

Magical Power: Arcanum Unsealed.name: Magical Power: Arcanum Unsealed
Magical Power: Arcanum Unsealed.description: Release the culminating working of the character's tradition with full preparation. As an attack it delivers roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by preparation, defenses and Power Strain; otherwise it achieves one great effect such as a ward that holds back a disaster or a binding on a powerful foe. Costs a full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, and may consume a rare component or call in a bargain. It requires its full requirements and cannot resurrect, kill a named NPC outright, control a player character, or break the tradition's rules.

Gravity Power: Gravity Well.name: Gravity Power: Gravity Well
Gravity Power: Gravity Well.description: Set a point of pull within sight for a few moments: loose objects and people nearby slide or are dragged toward it, then the user can slam them together or drop them hard. A committed crushing use deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by mass, distance from the point, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. The user stays unaffected by their own well. It cannot pull something anchored or far heavier than a car without heavy Power Strain, and anyone near the point is pulled in unless the user shapes it to spare them.

Gravity Power: Inverted Sky.name: Gravity Power: Inverted Sky
Gravity Power: Inverted Sky.description: Turn the direction of gravity in an area the size of a street corner for a few moments: things fall sideways, upward, or toward a chosen surface. The user can carry allies through it or let enemies fall into a wall or back to the ground; a committed slam deals roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by height, mass, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and Power Strain each beat it is held. When it drops, everything in it falls at once. It cannot hold for long, struggles with anchored or very heavy mass, and spares no one unless shaped to.

Gravity Power: Collapse Point.name: Gravity Power: Collapse Point
Gravity Power: Collapse Point.description: Compress gravity into one point for a few moments. The target at its heart takes roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by mass, defenses and Power Strain, and everything loose across a street-wide area is dragged inward and battered. Costs Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain; the user bleeds from the nose, may black out, and cannot use the power at all for a while afterward. It cannot be held more than a few moments, cannot swallow buildings or erase anything from existence, and will catch bystanders and property unless the user spends effort shaping it to spare them.

Shadow Power: Shade Ambush.name: Shadow Power: Shade Ambush
Shadow Power: Shade Ambush.description: From concealment in shadow, the character emerges and strikes a single target within short reach, the shadow lending weight or edge to the blow. A clean connection does about 55-70, modified by available darkness, light sources, defenses and Power Strain, and a target caught unaware is briefly off balance. Costs 1 Combat Energy. The character must begin hidden in genuine shadow; a lit area, flashlight held steady or alert observer looking the right way spoils it. Sound, heat and cameras can still reveal them before the strike.

Shadow Power: Blackout Veil.name: Shadow Power: Blackout Veil
Shadow Power: Blackout Veil.description: The character fills an area around them, such as a room, corridor or alley, with deep shadow that they can see and move through normally. Others inside have their sight badly restricted, and the character may strike from within; a clean connection does about 70-90, modified by available darkness, light sources, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy, with steady Power Strain for every moment it is held. A strong, steady light cuts through and shrinks it, and it does not stop sound, heat, cameras, dogs or anyone already holding onto the character. It cannot be made solid as a barrier.

Shadow Power: Eclipse Passage.name: Shadow Power: Eclipse Passage
Shadow Power: Eclipse Passage.description: The character becomes living shadow for a short span, sliding along connected darkness through a floor, wall shadow or building interior and passing untouched by ordinary physical blows. They return to form with a single decisive strike on one target; a clean connection does about 90-120, modified by available darkness, light sources, defenses and Power Strain. It spends the character's Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain. Strong light forces them out early and painfully, cutting the strike short. It cannot cross unbroken light, carry others, last beyond a short span, or instantly kill a named opponent. Sound, heat and cameras may still reveal them.

Sound Power: Tuned Beam.name: Sound Power: Tuned Beam
Sound Power: Tuned Beam.description: Focus sound into a narrow beam or tight cone aimed at one target or object. Against a person, a clean connection deals roughly 55-70 damage and can disorient them, modified by range, defenses, the user's own ears and Power Strain; against an object, the character can tune to its resonance to crack glass, loosen bolts or jar a held weapon loose. Costs 1 Combat Energy. Allies outside the beam are spared, but nearby people still hear it and walls still echo. It cannot pass through heavy soundproofing at full strength, cannot shatter what the sound cannot reach, and repeated use quickly adds ringing and Power Strain.

Sound Power: Standing Wave.name: Sound Power: Standing Wave
Sound Power: Standing Wave.description: Fill an area about the size of a large room or short street section with a sustained field of sound and vibration for a short exchange. Inside it the character maps movement by echo, unsteadies footing and aim, muffles or carries voices, and can drive a pressure surge that deals roughly 70-90 damage on a clean connection, modified by range, defenses, the user's own ears and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain each exchange it is held. Everyone inside is affected unless the character spends attention sparing allies, the field shakes nearby structures, and it weakens badly in open air or against thick soundproofing.

Sound Power: Crescendo Break.name: Sound Power: Crescendo Break
Sound Power: Crescendo Break.description: Release the full power of the character's sound for one decisive action: a crescendo roaring through an area the size of a city block, or an absolute silence over the same space. Against a target caught in the crescendo, a clean connection deals roughly 90-120 damage and can knock them down, modified by range, defenses and Power Strain; the silence blocks all sound inside for a short moment. It spends the full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, usually leaving the character temporarily deaf and near lockout. Everyone in range is affected unless the player defined how to spare allies, it breaks glass and alarms nearby, and it cannot kill a named opponent outright.

Time Power: Stolen Beat.name: Time Power: Stolen Beat
Time Power: Stolen Beat.description: Open a tight window and act inside it: a short chain of strikes, a precise dodge, or a few seconds of work while the world barely moves. As an attack it deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by the window's length, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It affects only the character and their immediate space; it cannot freeze people for long, undo anything that has happened, or grant extra turns beyond the window. Each use is paid back as Power Strain and Energy afterward.

Time Power: Tempo Field.name: Time Power: Tempo Field
Time Power: Tempo Field.description: Lay a field of altered time over a small space or a few people: enemies inside move sluggishly, or one ally briefly moves at the character's quickened tempo. Strikes landed inside the field deal roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and heavy Power Strain, growing the longer it is held; a field held too long collapses on the user. It cannot cover more than a small space, cannot freeze anything completely, cannot undo or rewind events, and cannot affect the story beyond the present moment.

Time Power: Still Point.name: Time Power: Still Point
Time Power: Still Point.description: Hold a moment almost perfectly still in a small area and act within it: move people out of harm's way, reposition, or deliver a decisive strike for roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs a full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, often leaving the character exhausted, disoriented or briefly unable to use the power. It covers only a small area and a brief instant, cannot undo or rewind anything, cannot affect events outside the present scene, and cannot kill a named NPC outright.

Probability Power: Stacked Deck.name: Probability Power: Stacked Deck
Probability Power: Stacked Deck.description: Lean a short run of uncertain outcomes in the scene toward one goal: each small chance along the way (a slip, a jam, a timing, a ricochet) is raised a step of success or falls the user's way by plausible accident. Costs 1 Combat Energy. If it helps an attack land, the attack does its own damage; the power adds none. It never guarantees anything, never touches an outcome that was not already possible, and the larger the run, the larger the coincidence that costs later. Important outcomes still resist.

Probability Power: Jinx Cascade.name: Probability Power: Jinx Cascade
Probability Power: Jinx Cascade.description: Turn the odds against a single opponent for a short fight, or for the user's allies: a string of small plausible failures for a foe (jams, slips, misfires, a missed step) or small plausible breaks for friends. Each outcome shifts by a step at most; the target can still succeed through skill or plain chance. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain. It never decides an important outcome or a named character's choice, and nothing impossible happens. The bill comes due bigger and wider: a coincidence that costs the user, an ally, or someone the user cares about.

Probability Power: Long Shot.name: Probability Power: Long Shot
Probability Power: Long Shot.description: Choose one outcome in the scene that is possible but deeply unlikely (the shot through a moving gap, the beam that holds, the bystander who walks out unhurt) and lean everything on it. It becomes a real chance instead of a near-impossibility and is raised as far as plausible luck allows, but it can still fail. Costs Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain. It never makes the impossible happen, never directly kills or decides a named character's choice, and leaves nothing provable behind. The bill is severe and arrives soon: a misfortune that costs the user or someone close to them.

Barrier Power: Interception Ward.name: Barrier Power: Interception Ward
Barrier Power: Interception Ward.description: The character casts a barrier to protect an ally, civilian or small group within sight, placing it between them and an incoming attack or hazard. It stops roughly what a reinforced wall would stop and can also be driven forward as a shield bash; a clean bash does about 55-70, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. Every hit the barrier takes costs the user Power Strain, and if it breaks the user is stunned for a moment. It can only be placed where the user can see, covers a person or small group, and cannot stop what the player defined as passing through.

Barrier Power: Sanctuary Dome.name: Barrier Power: Sanctuary Dome
Barrier Power: Sanctuary Dome.description: The character raises a large barrier dome or wall big enough to cover a street section, station platform or crowd, or shapes it to contain one dangerous opponent. It stops roughly what heavy structural walls would stop; what passes through remains as the player defined. Costs 2 Combat Energy, and every hit the field takes costs significant Power Strain. If it breaks, the user is stunned and those inside are exposed. It cannot cover an entire district, cannot be maintained indefinitely, and a contained opponent who strikes it repeatedly drains the user quickly.

Barrier Power: Unbreaking Line.name: Barrier Power: Unbreaking Line
Barrier Power: Unbreaking Line.description: The character raises a barrier that holds against a single catastrophic force for a short span: a collapsing building, a villain's strongest attack, an explosion or a crashing vehicle. It covers a crowd, a section of street or a team, and for that span it does not break. It spends the character's Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain; when it ends, the user is stunned or collapses, with real risk of injury or losing access to their power for the rest of the scene. It cannot last beyond the short span, cannot protect an entire district, and does not heal or undo harm already done.

Portal Power: Return Gate.name: Portal Power: Return Gate
Portal Power: Return Gate.description: Open a gate in the path of something already in motion, such as an incoming attack, a falling person or a charging opponent, and its exit where the character chooses within range. A redirected attack hits whatever it is sent at with its own force; a strike or projectile the character sends through deals roughly 55-70 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, timing and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It needs the exit point seen or known as the player defined, cannot carry anything the player's rules forbid, and a mistimed gate lets the attack through or sends it somewhere the character did not intend.

Portal Power: Linked Thresholds.name: Portal Power: Linked Thresholds
Portal Power: Linked Thresholds.description: Open and hold a small set of linked gates within range, or one gate large enough for a group or a vehicle, for a short exchange. The character can route allies, civilians or objects between them, shift a whole team's position, or bring an opponent's charge back to its own starting point. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain for each exchange the network stays open, more under heavy load. Every gate needs its far side seen or known, carries only what the player's rules allow, and works both ways, so enemies and attacks can come through too. A gate that collapses mid-transit or opens to a bad destination is a consequence, never a free escape.

Portal Power: Horizon Door.name: Portal Power: Horizon Door
Portal Power: Horizon Door.description: Open one extraordinary gate for a single decisive moment: either to a place far beyond the character's normal range that they know intimately, or wide enough to swallow a massive incoming threat such as a collapsing structure, a flood or a full-power attack and release it somewhere empty. If the character sends a blow or a falling weight through it to strike a target, a clean connection deals roughly 90-120 damage, modified by defenses and Power Strain. It spends the full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, leaving the character near lockout. It needs a known destination, works both ways while open, cannot cut a named opponent apart or remove them from the story, and a bad exit is a consequence.

Illusion Power: Phantom Ambush.name: Illusion Power: Phantom Ambush
Illusion Power: Phantom Ambush.description: Weave a layered, multi-sense illusion around a fight: false attackers, a misplaced self, an approaching sound, a blinding flash that is not there. It convinces targets until touched, contradicted, or doubted with reason, and gives the character and allies a clear opening against anyone fooled. The illusion itself does no damage, but a strike made through that opening is resolved normally with the advantage of surprise. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It cannot compel belief, control actions, or harm anyone directly, and a mind that knows sees through it.

Illusion Power: Living Mirage.name: Illusion Power: Living Mirage
Illusion Power: Living Mirage.description: Sustain a broad illusion over a space and several targets: a false room, a disguised street, a crowd of figures, a vanished doorway. It holds while the character attends to it and follows their movements, convincing everyone inside until touched, contradicted or doubted with reason; once one target breaks through and says so, others may follow. Costs 2 Combat Energy and significant Power Strain, growing with size and duration. It deals no harm, cannot compel belief or control anyone's choices, and fails against a mind that knows.

Illusion Power: Grand Deception.name: Illusion Power: Grand Deception
Illusion Power: Grand Deception.description: Build one nearly flawless illusion across a large area for a brief time: every sense the power covers, detailed enough that even trained observers hesitate. It holds until touched, contradicted, doubted with strong reason, or until the character's focus breaks. Costs a full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, leaving the character exhausted and sensory-blurred afterward. It deals no damage, changes nothing physical, cannot compel belief or control a player character, and cannot kill a named NPC; what convinced targets do remains their own act.

Nullification Power: Severing Touch.name: Nullification Power: Severing Touch
Nullification Power: Severing Touch.description: On contact or within the user's defined reach, suppress one active power and keep it suppressed through a short exchange while the user moves and fights. Costs 1 Combat Energy, plus Power Strain each beat the hold continues. The user can sense the shape of an unfamiliar power as it goes quiet. A stronger or stranger power resists and may break free; the suppression ends when contact or reach is lost or the user's concentration breaks, and the power returns intact. It does nothing to ordinary weapons, strength or falls.

Nullification Power: Silent Zone.name: Nullification Power: Silent Zone
Nullification Power: Silent Zone.description: Project a zone of suppression around the user, about the size of a room, for a few moments: every active power inside weakens, flickers or fails, allies' and the user's own included unless the user strains to exclude someone. Costs 2 Combat Energy and Power Strain each beat it is held. Stronger or stranger powers resist and may keep working at reduced strength. Powers return intact the moment the zone drops. It does nothing to guns, fists, falls, or ordinary equipment, and the user is left exposed to them.

Nullification Power: Total Stillness.name: Nullification Power: Total Stillness
Nullification Power: Total Stillness.description: Seize one target's power within reach and silence it completely for a few moments, overriding most resistance; only the very strongest or strangest powers get a chance to keep a flicker. Costs Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain; afterward the user is numb and shaking, and their own power, if they have one, stays quiet until they rest. The target's power always returns intact when the hold ends, with no lasting harm. It never erases a power permanently, affects only one target, and does nothing to guns, fists, falls or anything ordinary.

Healing Power: Field Triage.name: Healing Power: Field Triage
Healing Power: Field Triage.description: The character moves through a small group of injured people, briefly touching or sensing each, and stabilizes them all: stopping bleeding, closing wounds and steadying failing bodies. Each patient recovers a modest share of lost health and is safe for a time, enough to move or keep fighting. Costs 1 Combat Energy, plus Power Strain and Energy that increase with the number and severity of injuries. It cannot restore lost limbs, cure lasting conditions or reverse death, and it is less effective under fire or when the healer is badly strained.

Healing Power: Shared Burden.name: Healing Power: Shared Burden
Healing Power: Shared Burden.description: The character lays hands on one gravely injured person and pulls part of their wound into their own body, stabilizing them and restoring a large share of lost health. The healer takes a real portion of the injury, felt as pain, bleeding or bruising, and must recover from it normally. Costs 2 Combat Energy and significant Power Strain and Energy. It cannot restore lost limbs, reverse death or cure lasting conditions, and it is dangerous to use repeatedly or when the healer is already badly hurt.

Healing Power: Last Light.name: Healing Power: Last Light
Healing Power: Last Light.description: The character releases their full healing power in a single surge across everyone they can reach nearby, stabilizing all and restoring a large share of lost health to each. It spends the character's Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain and Energy, leaving the healer exhausted or collapsed, with real risk of injury or losing access to their power for the rest of the scene. It cannot reverse death, restore lost body parts, cure lasting conditions, or heal anyone outside its reach, and it is weaker on wounds far beyond what bodies can bear.

Demonic Contract: Amended Clause.name: Demonic Contract: Amended Clause
Demonic Contract: Amended Clause.description: Invoke the newly negotiated second clause of the pact: a strength, sending, weapon, protection, sight or other benefit agreed in play, distinct from the original clause. A fully committed offensive invocation deals roughly 55-70 damage on a clean connection, modified by the terms, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy, and the clause's own agreed price is paid as the contract states, in the scene or when collected. It grants only what the clause says, cannot create hidden terms or new consent, weakens in consecrated places if the contract says so, and the entity notices any attempt to stretch it.

Demonic Contract: Infernal Mantle.name: Demonic Contract: Infernal Mantle
Demonic Contract: Infernal Mantle.description: Take on the contracted entity's partial manifestation for a short exchange, as the contract defines: shadowed limbs, a burning brand, a demonic sight or weapon. While it lasts, the character's agreed clauses run at a higher level, and a fully committed attack deals roughly 70-90 damage on a clean connection, modified by the terms, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy, real Power Strain, and a heavier agreed price paid in the scene or collected later. Consecrated ground, faith and true names may weaken or break the mantle as the contract specifies. It grants no unagreed benefit, does not hand the entity control of the character, and ends early if the character overreaches the terms.

Demonic Contract: Grand Covenant.name: Demonic Contract: Grand Covenant
Demonic Contract: Grand Covenant.description: Invoke the highest clause of the contract for one decisive act: the entity's full agreed power acting through the character as a strike, protection, sending or sight beyond anything they normally command. A fully committed offensive invocation deals roughly 90-120 damage on a clean connection, modified by the terms, defenses and Power Strain. It spends the full Ultimate Charge, inflicts heavy Power Strain, and triggers the major price negotiated in advance, collected in a scene as the contract states. It grants nothing the contract did not agree to, cannot kill a named opponent outright, cannot control another person, and may be blunted by consecrated ground.

Alien: Stellar Lance.name: Alien: Stellar Lance
Alien: Stellar Lance.description: Focus the Astral Core into a concentrated beam: a narrow line of cosmic energy that pierces and burns. It deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Power Strain and the core's current acclimation. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It can punch through light cover but risks collateral behind the target. It cannot exceed the core's acclimated limits; if strained or unstable, it may flare unpredictably. Each use leaves a visible energy signature that trackers and observers can notice.

Alien: Core Ascendant.name: Alien: Core Ascendant
Alien: Core Ascendant.description: Channel the Astral Core through the whole body for a scene: blasts, barriers, short flight and localized gravity all strengthen and can be used together. Offensive bursts deal roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and heavy Power Strain, growing with duration. The state cannot be hidden, and holding it too long risks the core destabilizing, with collateral and a forced end to the state. It cannot exceed the core's limits or grant new kinds of power.

Alien: Starfall Release.name: Alien: Starfall Release
Alien: Starfall Release.description: Release the Astral Core's full strength in one defining act: a blast, a barrier over a crowd, or a gravity surge holding down a massive threat. As an attack it delivers roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs a full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, leaving the core dim and the character exhausted for some time. It has a limited area, cannot destroy a city or district, cannot kill a named NPC outright, and draws immediate government and faction attention.

God: Sanctified Ground.name: God: Sanctified Ground
God: Sanctified Ground.description: Consecrate an area around the user, about the size of a room, for a short fight with the player's defined blessing: allies inside are steadied, protected, or granted clarity, and a committed strike from the ground deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by belief present, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. The effect strengthens with witnesses who believe and thins without them; it ends when the user leaves the ground. What is asked in return is as the player defined. It cannot heal grave wounds, force belief, or work as a claim no one sees.

God: Divine Mandate.name: God: Divine Mandate
God: Divine Mandate.description: Invoke the connection across a crowd or a street with believing witnesses present, for one broad effect of the defined kind: a protection over many, a revelation everyone sees, a mending of many minor hurts, or a judgment that deals roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by belief present, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain. Without witnesses it falls back to a single small blessing. It cannot force anyone to believe, cannot command player characters, and what is asked in return becomes heavier.

God: Manifest Divinity.name: God: Manifest Divinity
God: Manifest Divinity.description: For a few moments, let the god show through the user in front of believing witnesses: one overwhelming expression of the defined kind, such as a great protection, a revelation that cannot be denied, or a strike that deals roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by belief present, defenses and Power Strain. Costs Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, and the god asks something serious in return, on the player's defined terms. It cannot bring back the dead, command player characters, or work without witnesses, where it collapses into a lesser blessing.

Turned: Crimson Lash.name: Turned: Crimson Lash
Turned: Crimson Lash.description: The character extends their predatory manifestation in a fast strike against one opponent within its established reach, then retracts it. A clean connection does about 55-70, modified by defenses, hunger, injuries and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. Heavy use or injury raises hunger; while hungry, Hunger Eyes may appear. It cannot extend beyond its established form or range, and the manifestation is physical flesh, so it can be cut, burned or restrained.

Turned: Blood Bloom.name: Turned: Blood Bloom
Turned: Blood Bloom.description: The character expands their manifestation into a larger, more complex living form the player defines, such as wings, armored plating or branching tendrils, and uses it to attack, defend or move. A clean strike does about 70-90, modified by defenses, hunger, injury and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain, and leaves the character hungry; Hunger Eyes are likely unless they feed. It cannot exceed its established nature or become magic or a separate creature, and while expanded it is a larger target for cutting, burning or restraint.

Turned: Apex Form.name: Turned: Apex Form
Turned: Apex Form.description: The character unleashes their manifestation in its fullest form for a short span, moving and striking with overwhelming predatory force. A clean connection does about 90-120, modified by defenses, hunger, injury and Power Strain. It spends the character's Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, leaving them severely hungry and with Hunger Eyes unless they feed afterward. It cannot become magic or a separate creature, cannot last long, and cannot instantly kill a named opponent. Feeding remains entirely the player's choice.

Kitsune: Fox Step.name: Kitsune: Fox Step
Kitsune: Fox Step.description: Flicker a short distance within sight in a blur of foxfire, leaving behind an afterimage illusion that fools eyes for a moment. The character can dodge an attack, slip past a guard, reach an ally or line up a foxfire strike that deals roughly 55-70 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Power Strain and positioning. Costs 1 Combat Energy. The afterimage deceives perception only; it cannot be touched, block attacks or act on its own. Fox Step needs open space and line of sight, cannot pass through walls or barriers, and struggles when the character is grabbed, bound or cut off from their charms.

Kitsune: Foxfire Procession.name: Kitsune: Foxfire Procession
Kitsune: Foxfire Procession.description: Release a procession of foxfire lights across an area about the size of a large room or short street section for a short exchange. The character can bless allies with a temporary edge, ward a position, mark foes, weave illusions that confuse sight and sound, or turn the lights on a target for roughly 70-90 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Power Strain and positioning. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain each exchange. Illusions deceive but cannot control actions, blessings fade after the scene, curses require their conditions, and the procession scatters if the character is struck hard, restrained or loses concentration.

Kitsune: Spectral Fox Form.name: Kitsune: Spectral Fox Form
Kitsune: Spectral Fox Form.description: Assume a spectral fox form for one decisive moment, all tails unfurled and foxfire blazing. The character can deliver a single overwhelming foxfire strike dealing roughly 90-120 damage on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Power Strain and positioning, or weave one grand illusion, ward or blessing that covers an area the size of a city block. It spends the full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain, leaving the character near lockout and exposed afterward. It cannot permanently raise attributes, rewrite reality, control another character's actions, or kill a named opponent outright, and being grabbed or sealed before it completes can break it.

Custom Power: Signature Expression.name: Custom Power: Signature Expression
Custom Power: Signature Expression.description: A refined, signature use of the player's own custom power, built from its stated effects, activation and visual expression: a more powerful strike, defense, utility or control effect within the power's limits. As an attack it deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by defenses, Power Strain and fit. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It must follow the player's written activation, strengths, limitations and risks, cannot add new effects the player did not define, and still carries the power's stated costs.

Custom Power: Unbound Expression.name: Custom Power: Unbound Expression
Custom Power: Unbound Expression.description: Push the player's custom power to a broader or more intense mode that grows from its own description: wider reach, longer duration, more targets, or greater force. Offensive uses deal roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and heavy Power Strain. It must follow the player's stated activation, strengths, limitations and risks, cannot add effects the player did not define, and its drawbacks hit harder at this scale.

Custom Power: Final Expression.name: Custom Power: Final Expression
Custom Power: Final Expression.description: The ultimate technique of the player's custom power, as described in its desired ultimate: one defining action at the height of its scale. As an attack it deals roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs a full Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain. It must follow the player's written activation, strengths, limitations and risks, cannot add undefined effects, and cannot resurrect, kill a named NPC outright, control a player character, or cause world-ending effects.

Yōkai: Second Aspect.name: Yōkai: Second Aspect
Yōkai: Second Aspect.description: Call on a second player-defined manifestation that grows from the same yōkai concept and folklore: another trick, form, sense or elemental expression, set with the player. A committed offensive use deals roughly 55-70 on a clean connection, modified by the manifestation, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy. It must stay within the concept, cannot invent undefined powers or universal yōkai rules, cannot force another character's actions, and the character's taboo still binds it fully.

Yōkai: Unveiled Form.name: Yōkai: Unveiled Form
Yōkai: Unveiled Form.description: Take the true yōkai form for a fight: every defined manifestation works at full strength, the body becomes harder to harm in the way the folklore allows, and a committed strike deals roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs 2 Combat Energy and real Power Strain to enter. The form cannot be hidden, the taboo binds tighter and breaking it ends the form at once, and it cannot invent new powers outside the concept or force anyone's actions.

Yōkai: Living Legend.name: Yōkai: Living Legend
Yōkai: Living Legend.description: For a few moments, manifest the yōkai at the full scale of its folklore within the defined concept: an area effect across a street or a decisive strike that deals roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain. Costs Ultimate Charge and heavy Power Strain. Afterward the taboo becomes absolute until the user rests, and the user's nature is all but impossible to hide. It cannot step outside the concept's folklore, create universal yōkai rules, revive the dead, or force a player character's actions.

Vampire: Hunter's Lunge.name: Vampire: Hunter's Lunge
Vampire: Hunter's Lunge.description: Burn blood to close distance in a predatory blur and strike before the target can fully react, using heightened speed and strength together. A clean connection deals roughly 55-70, modified by the user's hunger, defenses and Power Strain. Costs 1 Combat Energy and consumes blood or synthetic blood; each use pushes hunger up a step. It cannot pass through the user's defined weakness (sunlight, running water, a threshold, whatever the player set), and a hungry user who lunges in public shows what they are.

Vampire: Crimson Vigil.name: Vampire: Crimson Vigil
Vampire: Crimson Vigil.description: Burn the stored blood reserve to heighten every vampiric capability at once for a short fight: senses, speed, strength and recovery together. Strikes deal roughly 70-90 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain, and lighter wounds close as they are taken. Costs 2 Combat Energy and empties the blood reserve; hunger jumps to starving when it ends and the defined weakness hits harder until the user feeds. It cannot close a grave wound, revive anyone, or work while the defined weakness has the user.

Vampire: Night Unbound.name: Vampire: Night Unbound
Vampire: Night Unbound.description: Release the condition completely for a few moments. One predatory strike deals roughly 90-120 on a clean connection, modified by defenses and Power Strain; the user stays on their feet through one blow that would otherwise drop them, and ordinary bystanders are unsettled enough to back away. Costs Ultimate Charge, the entire blood reserve and heavy Power Strain. Afterward the user is starving, sluggish, and fully exposed to the defined weakness until they feed. It cannot control minds, cannot raise the dead, and the defined weakness still stops it outright.

Jinwoo: Heartstring Slap.name: Jinwoo: Heartstring Slap
Jinwoo: Heartstring Slap.description: Jinwoo fights at close range with sharp, theatrical slaps that strike both body and emotional connection. A successful hit can stagger, interrupt, expose hesitation, or briefly disrupt an active emotional effect, but it cannot create love, override consent, or force obedience. The result depends on distance, timing, target defenses, Jinwoo's intent, and the existing connection between them.

Jinwoo: Boundary Breaker.name: Jinwoo: Boundary Breaker
Jinwoo: Boundary Breaker.description: Jinwoo snaps an emotional tether to protect himself or an ally from an unwanted pull, fixation, panic effect, or manipulative connection. It can sever or weaken a supernatural link when its conditions support that outcome, but it cannot erase genuine feelings, memories, or consequences, and it requires Jinwoo to identify the boundary he is defending.

Kiyomi: Paper Arsenal.name: Kiyomi: Paper Arsenal
Kiyomi: Paper Arsenal.description: Kiyomi folds, weaponizes, and directs prepared paper into sharp cards, binding strips, cutting ribbons, decoys, seals, and briefly rigid weapons. Her paper follows physical limits, available material, line of sight, concentration, and established supernatural strength; it is a versatile control toolkit rather than unlimited matter creation.

Kiyomi: Redacted Command.name: Kiyomi: Redacted Command
Kiyomi: Redacted Command.description: Kiyomi marks a target, object, or piece of information with layered paper text that obscures, redirects, or constrains one clearly defined action or interpretation for a short time. It cannot control a person's entire mind, invent facts, or erase consequences. Strong resistance, broken concentration, or destroying the paper can interrupt it.

Cleo: Foxfire Pursuit.name: Cleo: Foxfire Pursuit
Cleo: Foxfire Pursuit.description: Cleo fires a foxfire-marked round or charm that tags a target, artifact, vehicle, or trail she has plausibly identified. The mark helps her track direction, distance, or recent passage through ordinary obstacles for a limited time, but it can be concealed, disrupted, removed, or misidentified.

Cleo: Contract Shot.name: Cleo: Contract Shot
Cleo: Contract Shot.description: Cleo combines a carefully chosen Glock shot with a stated bounty condition to pin, disarm, interrupt, or expose a target's escape route. It requires a clear contract purpose and a plausible shot; it cannot guarantee a hit, create legal authority, or turn a personal grudge into a valid bounty.

Haruka: Second Self.name: Haruka: Second Self
Haruka: Second Self.description: Haruka creates a temporary physical duplicate of anything she sees clearly reflected, including people, weapons, ordinary objects, or herself. The duplicate copies only visible and demonstrated qualities, not hidden memories, private knowledge, unknown abilities, emotional relationships, or supernatural bonds Haruka does not understand. Distorted reflections produce weaker or unstable copies.

Haruka: Mirror Crowd.name: Haruka: Mirror Crowd
Haruka: Mirror Crowd.description: Haruka uses several reflective surfaces to create up to five weaker duplicates at the beginning of an encounter and flood a battlefield with misleading angles. The copies demand concentration, destabilize after significant damage, and cannot reproduce qualities Haruka has not clearly observed. Breaking a reflective surface prevents new copies through it but does not instantly erase existing ones.

Haruka: False Original.name: Haruka: False Original
Haruka: False Original.description: Haruka creates a self-duplicate and rapidly changes position so an attacker commits to the wrong target. The duplicate is a physical decoy with Haruka's observed movement qualities, not a second full Haruka; careful observation, damaged reflections, or area control can expose the original.

Yurika: Breakup Song.name: Yurika: Breakup Song
Yurika: Breakup Song.description: When Yurika sings and a target clearly hears her actual voice, the target gradually loses emotional attachment toward people they are connected to. Memories remain, but emotional pull weakens. Sound barriers, distortion, interruption, time, and repeated exposure affect the result; stronger bonds are more painful but not necessarily faster to erode, and mass effects become less precise.

Yurika: Feedback Kiss.name: Yurika: Feedback Kiss
Yurika: Feedback Kiss.description: Yurika drives amplified vocal feedback through a nearby space to stagger, disorient, and interrupt opponents. It requires usable acoustics or equipment and can be weakened by sound dampening, distance, competing noise, or breaking the microphone setup.

Yurika: Cold Shoulder.name: Yurika: Cold Shoulder
Yurika: Cold Shoulder.description: Yurika suppresses her own immediate emotional response for a short time, resisting hesitation, fear, distraction, or emotional manipulation. The technique does not erase her memories or permanently remove feelings; the delayed emotional cost can surface afterward.

Satoshi: Word Gets Around.name: Satoshi: Word Gets Around
Satoshi: Word Gets Around.description: Satoshi deliberately starts an understandable rumor. When another person sincerely repeats it, the claim gains supernatural weight: small repetition causes coincidence, while larger repetition can create temporary physical consequences. The rumor must originate from Satoshi and be believed enough to carry social force. Contradictory versions interfere, and mutated rumors may escape his control.

Satoshi: Bad Reputation.name: Satoshi: Bad Reputation
Satoshi: Bad Reputation.description: Satoshi seeds and reinforces a negative claim about a target through nearby listeners. As the claim gains sincere repetition, people become more likely to doubt, misread, hesitate around, or socially isolate the target. It cannot force everyone to believe, and contradictory evidence or counter-rumors can weaken it.

Satoshi: Crowd Source.name: Satoshi: Crowd Source
Satoshi: Crowd Source.description: Satoshi plants several slightly different versions of one rumor through nearby people, allowing social repetition to spread beyond his direct voice. The versions must remain recognizably related, and excessive variation makes the supernatural effect unstable. He risks losing control over how the crowd's interpretation manifests.

Goro: House Edge.name: Goro: House Edge
Goro: House Edge.description: Goro declares a wager tied to a specific possible outcome and stakes something he genuinely values. Reality nudges probability toward the declared result in proportion to the personal value of the stake, never guaranteeing success. The wager must be clearly stated, possible, specific enough to judge, and genuinely meaningful to Goro; a loss immediately collects the stake.

Goro: Double or Nothing.name: Goro: Double or Nothing
Goro: Double or Nothing.description: Goro raises the value of an active wager, strengthening its probability pressure while increasing the consequence of failure. He must genuinely add or risk something personally meaningful; empty bravado cannot power the escalation.

Goro: Bad Beat.name: Goro: Bad Beat
Goro: Bad Beat.description: Goro places a high-risk wager on an opponent failing their next defense, making a plausible opening more likely when he stakes enough. The attack still depends on timing, position, and a possible failure; if the wager loses, the declared stake is collected immediately.

Mikaido: Missing Frame.name: Mikaido: Missing Frame
Mikaido: Missing Frame.description: When no conscious person directly observes Mikaido, he physically moves several meters during the gap in observation. He cannot pass through solid objects, attack during the movement, or activate while one observer maintains uninterrupted direct visual contact. Repeated uses exhaust him.

Mikaido: Blink Test.name: Mikaido: Blink Test
Mikaido: Blink Test.description: Mikaido uses flash, smoke, obstruction, lighting changes, or forced head movement to create a brief gap in direct observation. The setup does not guarantee a successful relocation: another observer, a tracked reflection, or an active camera feed can preserve observation.

Mikaido: Cut Between Frames.name: Mikaido: Cut Between Frames
Mikaido: Cut Between Frames.description: Mikaido relocates through an unobserved gap and reappears at an opponent's blind angle for one fast baton strike or close-range attack. He must reappear before performing the attack, and coordinated observation can deny the route.

Eri: Silent Treatment.name: Eri: Silent Treatment
Eri: Silent Treatment.description: Actions performed against Eri in complete silence fail to affect her properly. The attacking action itself must produce audible sound during execution; ambient noise or a sound made beforehand is insufficient. The rule does not make her invulnerable and does not judge the whole room's volume.

Eri: Mute the Room.name: Eri: Mute the Room
Eri: Mute the Room.description: Eri uses sound-dampening equipment, heavy doors, curtains, positioning, and environmental control to reduce audible cues around an opponent. This makes it harder for the opponent to create a valid audible attack against her, but cannot erase every sound or guarantee Silent Treatment will apply.

Eri: Quiet Work.name: Eri: Quiet Work
Eri: Quiet Work.description: Eri performs a fast close-range attack with minimal warning while an opponent is focused on producing sound. The attack uses joint control, a sweep, a compact blade, or a throwing spike and remains subject to distance, timing, defenses, and the environment.

Reina: Sentimental Value.name: Reina: Sentimental Value
Reina: Sentimental Value.description: Reina channels an object with genuine emotional significance to manifest a temporary quality based on its history, such as endurance, protection, courage, lethality, devotion, or resolve. The object must have real meaning; she cannot choose an unrelated effect and does not automatically know the object's full history. Conflicted meaning creates unstable results, and excessive use can damage the object.

Reina: Don't Throw It Away.name: Reina: Don't Throw It Away
Reina: Don't Throw It Away.description: Reina channels an object associated with protection, safety, or remembrance to absorb or reduce incoming harm. The effect depends on the object's genuine emotional history and can weaken or fail if that history is misunderstood, exhausted, or damaged.

Reina: Bad Memories.name: Reina: Bad Memories
Reina: Bad Memories.description: Reina channels an object associated with violence, betrayal, loss, or another painful history to empower a brutal close-range strike. The effect is powerful but emotionally and physically costly, and the object may be damaged by being used too aggressively.

Toma: One More Chance.name: Toma: One More Chance
Toma: One More Chance.description: Toma designates a person's next attempt at a clearly defined, possible action as their last chance. If the target understands and voluntarily attempts it, success has no further effect; failure temporarily prevents that exact action from being repeated. Toma cannot force the attempt, declare an impossible action, or create an instant-kill loophole. Broad wording weakens and shortens the lockout.

Toma: Hold Your Nerve.name: Toma: Hold Your Nerve
Toma: Hold Your Nerve.description: Toma deliberately refuses to react to feints, provocations, or uncertain threats, preserving his position until an opponent commits to a clear action. It improves his defensive timing and helps him identify a meaningful action to designate, but does not make him immune to surprise or area effects.

Toma: Last Word.name: Toma: Last Word
Toma: Last Word.description: After a target fails an action Toma designated as a final attempt, he immediately punishes the resulting hesitation with a precise close-range counter. The counter depends on distance, timing, and the target's defenses; it does not automatically defeat them.

Romeo: Claimant's Right.name: Romeo: Claimant's Right
Romeo: Claimant's Right.description: Romeo attaches an existing Chain to an action someone is preparing to take. If the person knowingly performs that action, the next link activates. The consequence is enforced through a flexible plausible route rather than direct mind control: an attack might lead to a weapon slipping, being parried, catching on the environment, or being knocked loose. Romeo cannot make someone choose the trigger, and the Chain must already exist before they act.

Romeo: Redline Clause.name: Romeo: Redline Clause
Romeo: Redline Clause.description: Romeo inserts a visible or spoken condition into an existing Chain and makes its consequence operate strictly when the marked condition is met. Crossing a doorway might trigger smoke, debris, a door slam, a reflection, or another interruption that blocks sight of him. It does not mind-control anyone or alter their decision; it controls the surrounding consequences of that decision.
