You restore, stabilize or accelerate biological recovery within defined limits. Its strength is that it undoes harm; its limits are that it cannot restore what is gone, reverse death, or heal faster than the body can bear.

Builds well with: Keyed to Wisdom; Support Class or Recon Class; the Channeler or Sentinel core; Powers Only. Its Awakenings raise Wisdom first.
Healing Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the healing needs (touch, time, the user's own vitality), what it cannot fix, and what it costs the healer. A healer is never off duty: every injury in a scene is a request, hospitals and agencies want them, and the one thing they cannot heal will arrive. Resolve healing through Power Control by default (knowing where to stop); a long triage is Power Endurance, a steadying word that keeps a patient alive is Power Presence, understanding an unfamiliar injury is Power Theory. Healing is paid in Power Strain and Energy; serious injuries, death and lasting conditions stay beyond it. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Demonic Contract.name: Demonic Contract
Demonic Contract.description:
Your power comes from a negotiated pact with a demon or infernal entity: defined benefits, defined terms, a price. Its strength is what the other party can do; its limits are the terms, the price, and the other party's own interests.

Builds well with: Keyed to Charisma; Command Class or Diplomat Class; the Provocateur or Commander core; Powers Only. Its Awakenings raise Charisma first.
Demonic Contract.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who the other party is, what the contract grants, what it costs and when it is collected, what the sign of it is, and whether the other party can be spoken to. The contract is a relationship with an NPC who has interests; it is exact, it never gives an unagreed benefit, and the price is paid in scenes. Resolve contract powers through Power Presence by default (an invocation is authority exercised); bearing the pact's price is Power Endurance, reading its small print is Power Theory. Faith, consecrated places and people who know the signs react; so does the entity when the user overreaches. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Powers Only.name: Powers Only
Powers Only.description: Rely primarily on established powers rather than mundane weapons or unarmed combat. Every exchange starts from the power; fists and tools are what is left when the power is spent, and the fighter knows their meters better than anyone.
Powers Only.traitNarrativeEffects: Power use follows the character's authored abilities, limits, resources, cooldowns and Power Strain; do not invent weapons or combat training. Narrate this fighter as opening every exchange with the power and reading the fight through it: range, Energy, Power Strain and cooldowns are their real position. Resolve their power actions through the lane the action uses (Power Routing); their Power Attribute pick is the tie-break. When the power is spent they are ordinary and exposed, and a good opponent waits for exactly that. Full Commitment is theirs alone: once an encounter, one expression a band harder at the cost of extra Power Strain.

Power and Hand-to-Hand.name: Power and Hand-to-Hand
Power and Hand-to-Hand.description: Combine established powers with punches, kicks, grappling, movement and close-range tactics. The power rides the body: a strike carries its effect, a grapple holds with it, and closing the distance is the plan.
Power and Hand-to-Hand.traitNarrativeEffects: Mundane close combat does not cause Power Strain by itself; applying a power to an attack follows its authored costs, limits, resources and cooldowns. Narrate this fighter closing, clinching and striking with the power woven into the contact; resolve the physical half through Close Quarters Combat and the power half through its lane (Power Routing). They are at their best inside arm's reach and at a disadvantage against anything that keeps them out. Charged Strike is theirs: a close blow that delivers the power's effect on contact.

Hand-to-Hand.name: Hand-to-Hand
Hand-to-Hand.description: Rely primarily on unarmed fighting: punches, kicks, grappling, takedowns and restraint. No power, no weapon, nothing to confiscate; the fighter is always armed and always nonlethal by default.
Hand-to-Hand.traitNarrativeEffects: Use Close Quarters Combat for meaningful uncertainty; do not assume formal training, guaranteed hits, or immunity to weapons. Narrate this fighter controlling distance, grip and the ground: restraint, takedown and escape are their answers, and their fights end in holds and unconsciousness, not blood, unless they choose otherwise. They cannot be disarmed and are never caught without their weapon; against reach, armour or a power that keeps them off, they need an opening. Takedown Chain is theirs: a sequence that takes a standing opponent to the ground and holds them.

Blades.name: Blades
Blades.description: Rely primarily on edged weapons: knives, swords or other established blades. The blade is quick, quiet and serious; every cut is a decision about how much harm this fight deserves.
Blades.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established blade, training, Weapon Proficiency, and attention to injury, legality, concealment and escalation. Narrate this fighter working angles, tempo and the opponent's hands; a blade turns a nonlethal intent into careful work and a lethal one into a short fight, and the law and witnesses read a drawn blade as escalation. Precision Cut is theirs: one cut placed to disable (a weapon hand, a strap, a cable, a tendon) rather than to wound broadly.

Blunt Weapons.name: Blunt Weapons
Blunt Weapons.description: Rely primarily on clubs, batons, hammers, staffs or other established impact weapons. Reach, leverage and mass; the fighter stops people and breaks things without needing to cut anyone.
Blunt Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established weapon, training, Weapon Proficiency, and attention to injury, reach, legality and escalation. Narrate this fighter using reach and leverage: parries, sweeps, strikes that stagger, and the option to end a fight without a wound that bleeds. Against speed in close they need their footwork. Staggering Blow is theirs: one hit that leaves the target staggered and open for the next exchange.

Smoker.name: Smoker
Smoker.description: A habitual tobacco user who gains familiar short-term stress relief from cigarettes but carries ongoing health and resource costs. Mechanically: Energy maximum -10.
Smoker.traitNarrativeEffects: Cigarettes may provide slightly more reliable short-term Stress relief for this character, but smoking costs money, uses one cigarette from a pack, creates odor and social consequences, can reduce stamina, worsen coughs and colds, impair long-term health, and create habit pressure. Never force smoking, withdrawal, dependence, or use of cigarettes without player choice.

Fast Healer.name: Fast Healer
Fast Healer.description: A character whose body recovers from ordinary fatigue and minor injuries faster than usual. Mechanically: health +10, Energy maximum -5 (healing burns fuel).
Fast Healer.traitNarrativeEffects: Recovery from minor injuries, soreness, and ordinary illness may be faster, but this does not prevent injury, restore full health instantly, reverse death, erase lasting damage, or bypass hospitalization. Severe injuries and supernatural conditions still require appropriate care.

Iron Constitution.name: Iron Constitution
Iron Constitution.description: A robust constitution that resists ordinary illness, fatigue, and environmental discomfort better than most people. Mechanically: Energy maximum +10.
Iron Constitution.traitNarrativeEffects: The character gains resilience against common colds, minor sickness, and fatigue, but can still become ill, exhausted, injured, or affected by serious disease, toxins, powers, and supernatural conditions.

Poor Sleep.name: Poor Sleep
Poor Sleep.description: A recurring difficulty getting restful sleep, including possible trouble falling asleep, waking during the night, or being unable to return to sleep. Mechanically: Energy maximum -10, Focus +1 (used to running on empty).
Poor Sleep.traitNarrativeEffects: Poor sleep can reduce Energy, increase Stress, impair concentration, slow recovery, and sometimes interrupt or shorten a rest period. Sleep disruption should remain contextual and player-directed, not a forced condition in every scene. Establish routines, safe environments, support, treatment, accommodations, or coping strategies when relevant; these can make recovery habits meaningful without guaranteeing perfect sleep.

Chronic Condition.name: Chronic Condition
Chronic Condition.description: A player-defined ongoing health condition that requires accommodations, management, treatment, or periodic care. Mechanically: Boundary Setting +1; every other effect is yours to define.
Chronic Condition.traitNarrativeEffects: The player defines the condition, symptoms, triggers, treatment, limits, privacy, and accommodations. Do not invent a diagnosis, symptoms, disability, medication, or medical history. Benefits may include planning, support access, self-knowledge, or resilience developed through management; costs may include appointments, fatigue, expenses, restrictions, or flare-ups.

High Metabolism.name: High Metabolism
High Metabolism.description: A body that burns energy quickly, requiring more frequent meals and creating both useful recovery and practical costs. Mechanically: Energy maximum +10; hunger arrives sooner and meals cost more.
High Metabolism.traitNarrativeEffects: Food can restore Energy somewhat efficiently, but hunger arrives sooner, meal costs increase, and missed meals can cause fatigue, irritability, or concentration problems.

Sensitive Lungs.name: Sensitive Lungs
Sensitive Lungs.description: A vulnerability to smoke, pollution, respiratory illness, and strenuous exertion. Mechanically: vulnerable to poisoning damage, Energy maximum -5, Investigation +1 (you smell smoke, gas and chemicals first).
Sensitive Lungs.traitNarrativeEffects: Smoke, poor air, colds, and intense exertion can reduce Energy or worsen symptoms, while clean air, rest, and medical care help. Do not invent a diagnosis or force symptoms without context.

Adrenaline Seeker.name: Adrenaline Seeker
Adrenaline Seeker.description: A strong attraction to high-intensity activity that can improve performance under pressure but makes calm recovery difficult. Mechanically: Combat Energy +1, Energy maximum -10.
Adrenaline Seeker.traitNarrativeEffects: During danger, competition, or urgent action the character may resist hesitation or fatigue briefly, but reckless choices, poor rest, injury risk, and difficulty settling down can create consequences. Never override player decisions.

Slow Healer.name: Slow Healer
Slow Healer.description: A character whose body heals more slowly than normal but ultimately recovers more completely from ordinary injuries and illness. Mechanically: Guard +4, health -5.
Slow Healer.traitNarrativeEffects: Recovery begins slowly and may require more rest, treatment, rehabilitation, and missed obligations than usual, but the character can recover more thoroughly over time from minor and moderate injuries or ordinary illness. This does not prevent injury, reverse death, erase lasting damage automatically, or bypass appropriate medical care.

No Power.name: No Power
No Power.description:
You have no supernatural power and rely on training, equipment, planning and ordinary skills. Its strength is that nothing about you can be nullified, drained or exposed, and every skill you own is one you earned; its limits are reach and scale against powered opponents, which preparation, allies, terrain and gear have to make up.

Builds well with: Unpowered; Strike Class or Skirmisher Class; the Duelist or Skirmisher or Marksman core; Hand-to-Hand or Blades. Its Awakenings raise Dexterity first.
No Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Present non-powered solutions, practical preparation, equipment, social tactics and environmental advantages without treating the character as helpless; a trained, prepared human beats an unprepared power often enough to matter. Do not invent supernatural abilities for them, ever. Their checks run through Close Quarters Combat, Weapon Proficiency, Strike Tactics and the ordinary skills, never a power skill. The world reads them as either an underdog or a professional, by conduct. Ask what they trained in, what they carry, and why they do this without a power. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Power and Weapons.name: Power and Weapons
Power and Weapons.description: Combine established powers with trained weapon use, tactical positioning and practical combat judgment. The weapon is the conduit: the power travels down the blade, the barrel or the haft, and the fighter picks the ground.
Power and Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Using a weapon requires an established weapon category, access, training, and attention to legality, injury, concealment and escalation; applying a power to a weapon follows its authored costs, limits, resources and cooldowns. Narrate this fighter choosing position first and striking with the weapon and the power as one; resolve the weapon through Weapon Proficiency and the power through its lane (Power Routing). Disarmed, they fall back to the power alone. Conduit Strike is theirs: one weapon attack that carries the power's effect to the target.

Ranged Weapons.name: Ranged Weapons
Ranged Weapons.description: Rely primarily on ranged weapons: bows, guns, firearms, thrown weapons and other established projectile equipment. Distance is the fighter's armour and the shot is a decision made before the target knows it.
Ranged Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established ranged weapon, appropriate ammunition or recoverable projectiles, training, Weapon Proficiency, lawful access or consequences where applicable, and attention to collateral risk; this style covers bows, guns, firearms, thrown weapons and similar equipment without granting access to any particular weapon. Narrate this fighter choosing lines of fire, cover and the moment; ammunition, reloads and bystanders are real. Caught at arm's length they are in the wrong fight. Called Shot is theirs: one aimed shot at a declared target point (a hand, a weapon, a strap, a leg) that resolves as that choice.

Hero Operations.name: Hero Operations
Hero Operations.description: You studied coordinated hero deployment, rescue logistics, and field leadership.
Hero Operations.traitNarrativeEffects: Agency obligations, formal reporting, and public accountability follow you into early work.

Combat Academy.name: Combat Academy
Combat Academy.description: You focused on practical combat training and controlled engagements.
Combat Academy.traitNarrativeEffects: Your direct approach brings higher collateral scrutiny and pressure to solve conflicts visibly.

Power Research.name: Power Research
Power Research.description: You studied power theory, testing, limits, and controlled application.
Power Research.traitNarrativeEffects: You begin with less field experience and must adapt when situations become chaotic.

Support Engineering.name: Support Engineering
Support Engineering.description: You trained in support equipment, maintenance, and practical hero technology.
Support Engineering.traitNarrativeEffects: You depend more heavily on functioning equipment, replacement parts, and repair access.

Medical and Rescue.name: Medical and Rescue
Medical and Rescue.description: You focused on stabilization, emergency care, and extracting people from danger.
Medical and Rescue.traitNarrativeEffects: Teams expect you to prioritize stabilization and civilian safety before pursuing threats.

Investigation and Law.name: Investigation and Law
Investigation and Law.description: You studied evidence, procedure, criminal investigation, and hero law.
Investigation and Law.traitNarrativeEffects: Mandatory reporting, evidence rules, and procedural limits shape your available choices.

Media and Public Relations.name: Media and Public Relations
Media and Public Relations.description: You trained in public communication, interviews, reputation, and crisis messaging.
Media and Public Relations.traitNarrativeEffects: Image management, interviews, and agency publicity obligations compete with field work.

Independent Hero Studies.name: Independent Hero Studies
Independent Hero Studies.description: You built a self-directed education around the skills most relevant to your own hero identity.
Independent Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: You have less institutional support and a weaker professional network at the start.

Emergency Management.name: Emergency Management
Emergency Management.description: You studied large-scale crisis coordination, evacuation, and disaster logistics.
Emergency Management.traitNarrativeEffects: You are expected to prioritize civilians, evacuation, and stabilizing the scene over pursuit.

Hero Ethics and Mediation.name: Hero Ethics and Mediation
Hero Ethics and Mediation.description: You studied de-escalation, negotiation, hero ethics, and conflict resolution.
Hero Ethics and Mediation.traitNarrativeEffects: Supervisors and civilians expect you to attempt negotiation before using force when practical.

Forensics and Crime Analysis.name: Forensics and Crime Analysis
Forensics and Crime Analysis.description: You studied crime scenes, evidence patterns, and investigative reconstruction.
Forensics and Crime Analysis.traitNarrativeEffects: Field response can slow while you secure evidence and preserve chain of custody.

Agency Management.name: Agency Management
Agency Management.description: You studied leadership, scheduling, administration, and the systems behind hero agencies.
Agency Management.traitNarrativeEffects: Paperwork, scheduling duties, and responsibility for team failures follow you into the field.

Community Hero Studies.name: Community Hero Studies
Community Hero Studies.description: You studied neighborhood trust, outreach, and long-term public safety relationships.
Community Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: Local visibility and ongoing neighborhood obligations make it harder to disappear after a case.

Covert Operations.name: Covert Operations
Covert Operations.description: You studied infiltration, concealment, intelligence gathering, and discreet intervention.
Covert Operations.traitNarrativeEffects: Oversight and secrecy requirements limit what you can reveal, while covert work receives limited public recognition.

International Hero Studies.name: International Hero Studies
International Hero Studies.description: You studied cross-border hero work, cultures, languages, and jurisdictional differences.
International Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: Travel demands, jurisdiction issues, and unfamiliar legal systems complicate assignments outside your home area.

Hero Technology and Communications.name: Hero Technology and Communications
Hero Technology and Communications.description: You studied agency networks, field communications, and technical coordination.
Hero Technology and Communications.traitNarrativeEffects: You rely more heavily on functioning networks, devices, and agency support.

Adaptive Field Studies.name: Adaptive Field Studies
Adaptive Field Studies.description: You pursued a broad practical education instead of specializing in one hero discipline.
Adaptive Field Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: You have no deep specialization and may face inconsistent expectations from institutions and teammates.

Alien.name: Alien
Alien.description:
Your power originates from extraterrestrial biology, technology, lineage, training or a connection to a civilization beyond Earth. Its strength is that it was never meant for human limits; its limits are what Earth lacks that it needs, and the attention it draws.

Builds well with: Keyed to Strength; Bruiser Class or Powerhouse Class; the Vanguard or Reaver core; Power and Hand-to-Hand. Its Awakenings raise Strength first.
Alien.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the connection is (biology, device, lineage, training), what it needs that Earth may not provide, what gives the character away, and who on Earth already knows. Alien origin draws government, media and faction attention the moment it is suspected. Resolve alien power through Power Force by default (a body or core built for more); a precise application is Power Finesse, an alien device understood is Power Theory, holding a transformation is Power Endurance. Earth's conditions set the limits: what the power needs and cannot get here is the ongoing cost. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Flunked Out.name: Flunked Out
Flunked Out.description: You entered higher education but failed to complete the program, leaving with unfinished training, damaged confidence, or unresolved obligations. You may still use what you learned, return to study, pursue work outside the field, or build a new path without being defined by the failure.
Flunked Out.traitNarrativeEffects: This character may face incomplete credentials, lost opportunities, academic debts, strained faculty relationships, or gaps in formal training. Their unfinished education can also provide practical knowledge, contacts, self-taught skills, and a reason to prove themselves. Do not assume the cause, shame, finances, disability, discrimination, burnout, misconduct, or personal history behind leaving; establish it through player choice or authored backstory. Flunking out does not determine intelligence, morality, competence, or future success.

Bruiser.name: Bruiser
Bruiser.description: A close-range role built around force, endurance, and staying in the fight.
Bruiser.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors direct pressure, physical resilience, and close-quarters problem-solving. This is a starting emphasis, not a requirement to be violent or to use only blunt weapons.

Ranged Specialist.name: Ranged Specialist
Ranged Specialist.description: A precision role built around distance, timing, mobility, and accurate equipment use.
Ranged Specialist.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors positioning, precision, and projectile or ranged-power decisions. Ammunition, collateral risk, line of sight, and lawful access remain meaningful.

Support Specialist.name: Support Specialist
Support Specialist.description: A team-oriented role built around protection, recovery, coordination, and practical problem-solving.
Support Specialist.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors keeping people safe, enabling allies, treating injuries, managing equipment, and finding nonviolent solutions. Support does not require self-sacrifice or obedience.

Defender.name: Defender
Defender.description: A protective role built around resilience, positioning, shielding, and controlling danger near allies.
Defender.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors absorbing pressure, protecting civilians, and creating safe openings. Defense does not require the character to accept harm without limits.

Controller.name: Controller
Controller.description: A tactical role built around battlefield shaping, timing, disruption, and managing risks.
Controller.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors analysis, awareness, planning, and effects that limit danger or create opportunities. It does not guarantee that powers work or that opponents surrender control.

Investigator.name: Investigator
Investigator.description: A problem-solving role built around observation, evidence, deduction, and careful questioning.
Investigator.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors noticing inconsistencies, preserving evidence, interviewing, research, and patient reasoning. It does not guarantee correct conclusions or access to restricted information.

Support Class.name: Support Class
Support Class.description:
A wisdom-focused class built around protection, recovery, coordination, and practical care.

Suits: Psychic Power, Supernatural, Spirit Manifestation, Invoker, Nullification Power, Healing Power, Yōkai; Keyed to Wisdom; the Channeler or Sentinel core.
Support Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors keeping people safe, enabling allies, treating injuries, managing risk, and finding nonviolent solutions. Support does not require self-sacrifice or obedience.

Strike Class.name: Strike Class
Strike Class.description:
A dexterity-focused class built around precision, timing, and decisive attacks.

Suits: No Power, Mobility Power, Shadow Power, Time Power, Portal Power; Keyed to Dexterity; the Duelist or Skirmisher or Marksman core.
Strike Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors accurate attacks, quick reactions, and exploiting openings at close or long range. It does not require violence when restraint is safer.

Vanguard Class.name: Vanguard Class
Vanguard Class.description:
A constitution-focused class built around endurance, initiative, and remaining effective under pressure.

Suits: Mutation Power, Parasite, Cursed Item, Barrier Power, Turned, Vampire; Keyed to Constitution; the Bulwark or Warden core.
Vanguard Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors stamina, sustained action, frontline reliability, and entering uncertain situations prepared to endure consequences. It does not grant immunity to injury.

Defense Class.name: Defense Class
Defense Class.description:
A constitution-focused class built around resilience, shielding, positioning, and protecting others.

Suits: Mutation Power, Parasite, Cursed Item, Barrier Power, Turned, Vampire; Keyed to Constitution; the Bulwark or Warden core.
Defense Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors absorbing pressure, protecting civilians, and creating safe openings. Defense does not require accepting harm without limits.

Control Class.name: Control Class
Control Class.description:
An intelligence-focused class built around tactics, battlefield shaping, timing, and disruption.

Suits: Elemental Power, Construct Power, Technological Hero, Magical Power, Probability Power; Keyed to Intelligence; the Strategist or Analyst core.
Control Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors analysis, planning, systems, and effects that limit danger or create opportunities. It does not guarantee control over opponents or powers.

Command Class.name: Command Class
Command Class.description:
A charisma-focused class built around leadership, coordination, authority, and motivating a team.

Suits: Sound Power, Illusion Power, Demonic Contract, God, Kitsune; Keyed to Charisma; the Provocateur or Commander core.
Command Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors clear communication, social leverage, planning, and maintaining group cohesion. Command does not grant authority over NPC choices or force obedience.

Bruiser Class.name: Bruiser Class
Bruiser Class.description:
A strength-focused class built around close-range pressure, physical force, and taking space.

Suits: Energy Power, Gravity Power, Alien; Keyed to Strength; the Vanguard or Reaver core.
Bruiser Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors grappling, striking, lifting, breaking obstacles, and direct physical problem-solving. Strength does not guarantee success or require violence.

Powerhouse Class.name: Powerhouse Class
Powerhouse Class.description:
A strength-focused class built around overwhelming force, heavy impacts, and exceptional physical output.

Suits: Energy Power, Gravity Power, Alien; Keyed to Strength; the Vanguard or Reaver core.
Powerhouse Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors feats of force, powerful attacks, carrying capacity, and physically imposing solutions. It does not grant invulnerability or unlimited exertion.

Skirmisher Class.name: Skirmisher Class
Skirmisher Class.description:
A dexterity-focused class built around speed, mobility, repositioning, and opportunistic action.

Suits: No Power, Mobility Power, Shadow Power, Time Power, Portal Power; Keyed to Dexterity; the Duelist or Skirmisher or Marksman core.
Skirmisher Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors movement, initiative, escape routes, and adapting under pressure. It does not grant automatic evasion or immunity to danger.

Tech Class.name: Tech Class
Tech Class.description:
An intelligence-focused class built around engineering, equipment, research, and technical problem-solving.

Suits: Elemental Power, Construct Power, Technological Hero, Magical Power, Probability Power; Keyed to Intelligence; the Strategist or Analyst core.
Tech Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors understanding devices, repairing systems, designing solutions, and using technology responsibly. It does not grant instant expertise or unrestricted equipment access.

Recon Class.name: Recon Class
Recon Class.description:
A wisdom-focused class built around awareness, observation, scouting, and reading situations before acting.

Suits: Psychic Power, Supernatural, Spirit Manifestation, Invoker, Nullification Power, Healing Power, Yōkai; Keyed to Wisdom; the Channeler or Sentinel core.
Recon Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors noticing danger, tracking context, gathering information, and making careful decisions. Recon does not guarantee accurate conclusions or hidden information.

Diplomat Class.name: Diplomat Class
Diplomat Class.description:
A charisma-focused class built around negotiation, trust-building, de-escalation, and navigating competing interests.

Suits: Sound Power, Illusion Power, Demonic Contract, God, Kitsune; Keyed to Charisma; the Provocateur or Commander core.
Diplomat Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors persuasion, mediation, reading social boundaries, and finding agreements without assuming consent or cooperation. Diplomacy does not guarantee trust or compliance.

Natural.name: Natural
Natural.description: The character's power emerged as a natural part of who they are: it was always there, grew with the body, and needs no trigger, device or bargain. The body is built around it.
Natural.traitNarrativeEffects: The power is as familiar to the character as a hand; they have never not had it, and their childhood, family and school records show it. Ask when it first showed, who noticed, and what they were told about it. It cannot be revoked, hacked or argued with, but it also has no one to blame and no manual: its limits were learned by living with it.

Inherited.name: Inherited
Inherited.description: The character received or developed the power through family, lineage or ancestry. The name came with it, and so did the expectations, the relatives, and the people who remember what the last one did.
Inherited.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who in the family has or had the power, what the family expects, and what the character owes or refuses. Relatives with the same power are NPCs with opinions; the family's reputation precedes the character with institutions, factions and the press. The power's known family limits are public knowledge among those who know the name.

Accident.name: Accident
Accident.description: The character's power began through an accident, exposure, disaster, experiment or malfunction. They survived something, and what they carry out of it is the power and the memory.
Accident.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what happened, who else was there, what was lost, and whether anyone is responsible. The accident is a matter of record somewhere: medical files, a news item, a company that would rather it stayed quiet. The character knows what an emergency feels like from the inside, which is why they move first when one happens; the power may still be unstable in the ways the accident was.

Artificial.name: Artificial
Artificial.description: The character's power was created, implanted, engineered or enabled through technology or cybernetics. Someone built it, someone can maintain it, and someone has the schematics.
Artificial.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who made it, why, what it needs (power, maintenance, parts, updates), and whether the maker still has a say. The power has documentation and dependencies: it can be serviced, upgraded, damaged, remotely affected or legally contested. The character understands their own mechanism better than most people understand their phone, and other engineers notice.

Training.name: Training
Training.description: The character developed the power through disciplined practice, study, ritual or specialised instruction. Nothing about it was free; every edge was drilled, and the teacher's voice is still in their head.
Training.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who taught them, what the discipline forbids, what the next lesson would be, and what they still cannot do. A trained power is deliberate: the character knows their limits exactly, rarely overreaches by accident, and reads other people's powers as a practitioner. Their school or master is an NPC with standards and a reputation that attaches to the student.

Contract.name: Contract
Contract.description: The character gained the power through an agreement with a person, being, artifact, faction or force. The terms exist, the other party exists, and the price is still being paid.
Contract.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who the other party is, what the terms say, what was promised in return, and what happens if the character breaks them. The other party is an NPC with interests and a way to collect; the contract's terms are exact and known to the character. People who deal in agreements recognise a contractor, and the character has learned to read a bargain.

Cursed.name: Cursed
Cursed.description: The character's power was imposed or awakened through a curse, relic, ritual or supernatural event. They did not ask for it, cannot give it back, and have learned to live with what it costs.
Cursed.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the curse is, what it takes from the character, what eases it, and who or what laid it. The curse has a cost that is paid regardless of whether the power is used; the character is good at enduring, improvising and making do, because they have had to be. Those who know curses can see the marks; a cure or a lifting is a quest, never a line.

Alien Origin.name: Alien Origin
Alien Origin.description: The character's power is connected to extraterrestrial biology, technology or an astral source. Earth is not quite where it belongs, and the character has spent their life working out what that means.
Alien Origin.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the connection is, what gave it away, who on Earth knows, and what the power needs that Earth may not provide. Government, agency and faction attention follows the suspicion of an off-world origin; the character has learned to investigate, because nobody else could tell them what they are. The power's needs and vulnerabilities are unlike human ones.

Transformation.name: Transformation
Transformation.description: The character's power began through a permanent or recurring transformation of body or state. The body is not the one they were born with, or not always, and it is stronger for it.
Transformation.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what changed, whether it recurs or holds, what triggers it, and what of the old self remains. The changed body is capable and sometimes conspicuous; clothes, doors, food and medicine may not fit it. A recurring transformation has a trigger and a cost; a permanent one has a before that people remember.

Awakened.name: Awakened
Awakened.description: The character's dormant potential activated through age, stress, ritual, crisis or another major event. It was in them all along, and the moment it woke is the moment they still measure things by.
Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what woke it, who was there, what the character felt, and whether it could happen again or go further. An awakened power tends to answer to emotion and to other people's: the character reads a room because the room is what woke them. The event may have witnesses, consequences or a pattern others want to study.

Granted.name: Granted
Granted.description: The character's power was bestowed by another person, institution, deity, artifact or force. It can be taken back, and the one who gave it is owed something, even if only gratitude.
Granted.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who or what granted the power, why, on what understanding, and whether it can be withdrawn. The grantor is an NPC or force with expectations; the character has had to speak for themselves to keep what they were given. Institutions that grant powers keep records, and a granted power carries the grantor's reputation with it.

Unknown.name: Unknown
Unknown.description: The character does not know the power's origin, or several conflicting explanations remain possible. Not knowing has made them careful about what they show and quick about what they hide.
Unknown.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the character believes, what they have been told, what evidence exists, and who else is curious. The origin is a mystery the world can pursue: researchers, agencies and factions may have theories, and the truth, when it comes, is a story beat with consequences. Until then the character has learned to keep the power's unknowns off their face.

Patient.name: Patient
Patient.description: You can wait, observe, and act only when timing is favorable.
Patient.traitNarrativeEffects: Patience supports careful exchanges but can allow urgent opportunities to pass.

Impulsive.name: Impulsive
Impulsive.description: You act quickly when an opportunity or provocation appears.
Impulsive.traitNarrativeEffects: Impulse creates initiative but can undermine careful planning.

Prideful.name: Prideful
Prideful.description: You protect your competence and reputation fiercely.
Prideful.traitNarrativeEffects: Pride supports confident confrontation but makes concession difficult.

Humble.name: Humble
Humble.description: You give credit freely and rarely need to dominate a room.
Humble.traitNarrativeEffects: Humility supports cooperation but can make self-advocacy harder.

Suspicious.name: Suspicious
Suspicious.description: You look for hidden motives before trusting an offer.
Suspicious.traitNarrativeEffects: Suspicion helps detect deception but can slow cooperation.

Empathetic.name: Empathetic
Empathetic.description: You notice emotional states and respond to them quickly.
Empathetic.traitNarrativeEffects: Empathy supports social reading but can make emotional pressure distracting.

Adaptable.name: Adaptable
Adaptable.description: You adjust plans smoothly when circumstances change.
Adaptable.traitNarrativeEffects: Adaptability supports survival but can reduce commitment to long preparation.

Pride.name: Pride
Pride.description: You protect your dignity and resist being made to look weak.
Pride.traitNarrativeEffects: Pride supports intimidation but can make compromise difficult.

Impulsiveness.name: Impulsiveness
Impulsiveness.description: You react before every consequence has been considered.
Impulsiveness.traitNarrativeEffects: Impulsiveness supports fast action but undermines careful investigation.

Guilt-Ridden.name: Guilt-Ridden
Guilt-Ridden.description: Past harm remains close to the surface when choices affect others.
Guilt-Ridden.traitNarrativeEffects: Guilt supports empathy but can disrupt confidence under moral pressure.

Jealousy.name: Jealousy
Jealousy.description: You compare your place in relationships and fear being replaced.
Jealousy.traitNarrativeEffects: Jealousy sharpens social attention but clouds objective judgment.

Fear of Abandonment.name: Fear of Abandonment
Fear of Abandonment.description: Separation and rejection can feel more threatening than the situation warrants.
Fear of Abandonment.traitNarrativeEffects: This fear supports attachment and vigilance but complicates independent decisions.

Reckless Loyalty.name: Reckless Loyalty
Reckless Loyalty.description: You take disproportionate risks for people or causes you have claimed as yours.
Reckless Loyalty.traitNarrativeEffects: Loyalty supports rescue and endurance but can undermine planning.

Financial Pressure.name: Financial Pressure
Financial Pressure.description: Money problems narrow your choices and demand practical compromises.
Financial Pressure.traitNarrativeEffects: Financial pressure supports bargaining and resource awareness but distracts from long-term planning.

Conflict Avoidance.name: Conflict Avoidance
Conflict Avoidance.description: You instinctively seek exits, compromises, or silence before confrontation.
Conflict Avoidance.traitNarrativeEffects: Avoidance supports de-escalation but weakens direct intimidation.

Approval-Seeking.name: Approval-Seeking
Approval-Seeking.description: You measure choices against the reactions of people whose approval matters to you.
Approval-Seeking.traitNarrativeEffects: Approval-seeking supports reading an audience but weakens independent decisions.

Poor Emotional Regulation.name: Poor Emotional Regulation
Poor Emotional Regulation.description: Strong feelings can alter your judgment before you regain control.
Poor Emotional Regulation.traitNarrativeEffects: Emotional intensity supports expressive performance but complicates persuasion under pressure.

Difficulty Asking for Help.name: Difficulty Asking for Help
Difficulty Asking for Help.description: You hide need until circumstances become difficult to manage alone.
Difficulty Asking for Help.traitNarrativeEffects: Self-reliance supports survival but makes cooperation and recovery harder.

Overconfidence.name: Overconfidence
Overconfidence.description: You assume your preparation or ability will carry you through uncertain situations.
Overconfidence.traitNarrativeEffects: Confidence supports intimidation but can undermine investigation.

Routine Dependence.name: Routine Dependence
Routine Dependence.description: Unexpected changes unsettle you until a new pattern is established.
Routine Dependence.traitNarrativeEffects: Routine supports disciplined preparation but complicates adaptation.

Easily Distracted.name: Easily Distracted
Easily Distracted.description: Noise, novelty, and competing concerns can pull attention away from the immediate task.
Easily Distracted.traitNarrativeEffects: Distraction supports noticing unusual details but undermines sustained investigation.

Fear of Rejection.name: Fear of Rejection
Fear of Rejection.description: The possibility of being refused can delay direct requests and honest vulnerability.
Fear of Rejection.traitNarrativeEffects: This fear supports cautious observation but weakens confident persuasion.

Indecision.name: Indecision
Indecision.description: Competing possibilities can hold you in place when a choice is needed.
Indecision.traitNarrativeEffects: Indecision supports weighing evidence but delays decisive action.

Workaholism.name: Workaholism
Workaholism.description: You use constant work to avoid rest, uncertainty, or difficult feelings.
Workaholism.traitNarrativeEffects: Workaholism supports sustained task focus but undermines recovery and balance.

Homesickness.name: Homesickness
Homesickness.description: Distance from familiar people or places weighs on your attention.
Homesickness.traitNarrativeEffects: Homesickness supports memory and attachment but complicates unfamiliar social settings.

Status Anxiety.name: Status Anxiety
Status Anxiety.description: You track how others rank, judge, and compare you.
Status Anxiety.traitNarrativeEffects: Status anxiety supports reading social hierarchies but can weaken open cooperation.

Moral Scruples.name: Moral Scruples
Moral Scruples.description: You hesitate when success requires violating a principle you protect.
Moral Scruples.traitNarrativeEffects: Moral scruples support ethical judgment but complicate coercion and ruthless tactics.

Poor Impulse Control.name: Poor Impulse Control
Poor Impulse Control.description: Provocation, temptation, or sudden opportunity can override your plans.
Poor Impulse Control.traitNarrativeEffects: Poor impulse control supports fast reactions but undermines careful persuasion.

Grief.name: Grief
Grief.description: A meaningful loss continues to shape attention, memory, and choices.
Grief.traitNarrativeEffects: Grief supports empathy and remembrance but can disrupt focus.

Secretive Past.name: Secretive Past
Secretive Past.description: You protect information about earlier choices, relationships, or affiliations.
Secretive Past.traitNarrativeEffects: A secretive past supports concealment but complicates trust and honest cooperation.

Alcoholic.name: Alcoholic
Alcoholic.description: You have an ongoing alcohol-use disorder or serious dependence that affects health, routines, finances, relationships, and recovery. This trait does not define your entire identity and does not force drinking, relapse, or a particular outcome. Mechanically: Energy maximum -10.
Alcoholic.traitNarrativeEffects: Track cravings, withdrawal risk, access, support, consent, medical care, stress, and recovery goals without glamorizing alcohol or treating relapse as inevitable. Alcohol use can impair judgment, sleep, health, finances, work, school, relationships, combat readiness, and power control. The character may seek treatment, harm reduction, sobriety, controlled support, or another player-defined path; emergencies require medically plausible care.

God.name: God
God.description:
A narrative power origin: divine lineage, a deity's blessing, sacred office, worship, revelation, or another godlike connection. The origin explains where the power comes from, not what it can do; define the power's actual expression with the Power Attribute pick and in the character's description.

Builds well with: Keyed to Charisma; Command Class or Diplomat Class; the Provocateur or Commander core; Powers Only. Its Awakenings raise Charisma first.
God.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask which god, what the connection actually is, what it grants, what it asks, and who believes. A divine connection is a social fact before it is a power: believers, sceptics, clergy and rivals all react, and a claim that cannot be witnessed is just a claim. Resolve a divine connection through Power Presence by default (it is real where it is witnessed and believed); what the character's power actually does resolves through the skill of that expression, and the player's definition sets what is granted and what is asked in return. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Parasite.name: Parasite
Parasite.description:
A body-horror power whose source is a living, invasive, or symbiotic organism that alters the host's body and may demand adaptation, nourishment, or negotiation.

Builds well with: Keyed to Constitution; Vanguard Class or Defense Class; the Bulwark or Warden core; Power and Hand-to-Hand. Its Awakenings raise Constitution first.
Parasite.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask how the parasite entered or awakened, where it lives, what changes it causes, what it needs, whether it has instincts or a voice, and what boundaries the host maintains. Body changes may be disturbing, painful, useful, stigmatized, or difficult to control, but do not assume loss of agency, evil, or non-consensual behavior. Resolve the parasite's adaptations through Power Endurance by default (the host bears them); an attack with a grown weapon is Power Force, a sensory read is Power Control. Hunger, the parasite's instincts and the host's boundaries are the ongoing costs; feeding is a scene, not a stat line.

Heartless.name: Heartless
Heartless.description: You present as emotionally hardened, unsentimental, or difficult to move, whether that impression is deliberate, defensive, or partly true.
Heartless.traitNarrativeEffects: Heartlessness may help maintain composure around danger, pain, or morally difficult choices, but can make empathy, reassurance, intimacy, and trust harder. Do not assume the character lacks feelings, conscience, or the ability to care.

Overthinker.name: Overthinker
Overthinker.description: You analyze possibilities repeatedly, anticipating failure and consequences before committing to a choice.
Overthinker.traitNarrativeEffects: Overthinking can improve preparation, investigation, and threat recognition, but may delay decisions, drain Energy, and complicate spontaneous social or physical action. Keep it contextual and player-directed rather than forcing indecision.

Nightmares.name: Nightmares
Nightmares.description: Disturbing dreams or power-related sleep experiences can affect rest and mood, and may sometimes interrupt sleep before the character is rested. Mechanically: Energy maximum -5, Focus +1.
Nightmares.traitNarrativeEffects: Nightmares may interrupt sleep, reduce sleep quality and Energy recovery, and affect emotional steadiness after difficult scenes. An interrupted night can create fatigue, stress, concentration problems, or a need to rest again later. Nightmares may also give the player opportunities for dream imagery, memory processing, warning-like symbolism, grounding, or deliberate coping. Do not treat dreams as automatically prophetic, force a specific interpretation, or diagnose a disorder. Sleep interruption should be contextual and not happen every night.

Depression.name: Depression
Depression.description: A player-defined mental-health struggle that may affect energy, motivation, hope, concentration, and connection. Mechanically: Empathy +1; every other effect is yours to define.
Depression.traitNarrativeEffects: The player defines how this affects them, if at all, and what support, treatment, coping, accommodations, or privacy they want. It may create meaningful difficulty while also encouraging self-knowledge, support-seeking, patience, and resilience. Do not romanticize it, use it as shorthand for cruelty, invent symptoms or diagnosis, or replace professional care.

Disassociation.name: Disassociation
Disassociation.description: A player-defined experience of disconnection from self, surroundings, memory, or immediate emotion. Mechanically: Boundary Setting +1; every other effect is yours to define.
Disassociation.traitNarrativeEffects: The player defines its form, triggers, warning signs, coping methods, support needs, and privacy. It may complicate focus, continuity, or stressful scenes while making grounding, trusted support, preparation, and self-awareness meaningful. Do not use it to remove player agency, invent a diagnosis, imply danger, or replace professional care.

Lonely Loner.name: Lonely Loner
Lonely Loner.description: You are used to being alone and often keep people at a careful distance, whether by choice, habit, or circumstance.
Lonely Loner.traitNarrativeEffects: Solitude can support self-reliance, observation, and focused work, but may make trust, asking for help, and maintaining connections more difficult. Do not force isolation or loneliness; let the player define how this trait appears.

Cast Out.name: Cast Out
Cast Out.description: You were pushed away from a former home, community, institution, or organization and now carry the consequences of that separation.
Cast Out.traitNarrativeEffects: Being cast out may create distrust, social stigma, or practical obstacles while also encouraging self-reliance and awareness of exclusion. Preserve ambiguity about who cast the character out and why unless the player defines it.

Spirit Manifestation.name: Spirit Manifestation
Spirit Manifestation.description:
The character's supernatural power takes physical form as a temporary level 1 spirit manifestation connected to them. The manifestation is an extension or effect of the user rather than an independent character. It may fight, defend, support, manipulate the environment, or produce unusual effects, but its strength and persistence come from the user.

Builds well with: Keyed to Wisdom; Support Class or Recon Class; the Channeler or Sentinel core; Powers Only. Its Awakenings raise Wisdom first.
Spirit Manifestation.traitNarrativeEffects: The manifestation is temporary and level 1 by default. It is not an independent NPC, companion, party member, or character by default. If the engine requires a temporary NPC-like representation, use only the Spirit Manifestation NPC type and remove or dismiss the representation when the summoning ends. It cannot speak, whisper, narrate, hold conversations, or communicate through words. During an attack, the user may shout a brief established callout such as “ORA!” or “MUDA!”; this is the user's voice, never the manifestation speaking. The user may also yell the manifestation's player-established name to summon or direct it. The manifestation may express intent through movement, posture, visual changes, or effects. Its appearance, role, range, autonomy, senses, vulnerabilities, and behavior remain player-defined or are established through play. Resolve the manifestation's acts through Power Control by default (its strength and persistence are the user's steadiness); its blows are Power Force, its precision Power Finesse, keeping it out through a long fight Power Endurance. Damage to the manifestation is felt by the user as Power Strain.

Brash.name: Brash
Brash.description: You act boldly and speak or move before caution catches up.
Brash.traitNarrativeEffects: Brashness can create momentum and surprise, but may cause avoidable escalation or missed details.

Loudmouth.name: Loudmouth
Loudmouth.description: You speak freely, forcefully, and often at greater volume than a situation requires.
Loudmouth.traitNarrativeEffects: A loud, confident presence can draw attention and energize a room, but can make discretion and subtle negotiation more difficult.

Nonchalant.name: Nonchalant
Nonchalant.description: You meet danger, pressure, and uncertainty with an outwardly casual attitude.
Nonchalant.traitNarrativeEffects: A calm exterior can steady others and resist intimidation, but may cause people to underestimate your concern or make you overlook urgency.

Arrogance.name: Arrogance
Arrogance.description: You overestimate your judgment, importance, or ability compared with those around you.
Arrogance.traitNarrativeEffects: Arrogance can project authority and confidence, but may damage cooperation, obscure mistakes, and make useful criticism difficult to accept.

Yapper.name: Yapper
Yapper.description: You talk constantly and tend to fill silence with commentary, stories, questions, observations, or unfiltered thoughts.
Yapper.traitNarrativeEffects: Your relentless conversation can build rapport, reveal useful information, keep nervous people engaged, and make social scenes lively. It can also exhaust others, interrupt important moments, reveal more than intended, undermine secrecy, and make quiet observation difficult. The character still chooses what to say; Yapper does not override player agency.

Thinks Out Loud.name: Thinks Out Loud
Thinks Out Loud.description: You process thoughts verbally, speaking through possibilities, plans, and reactions instead of keeping every thought private.
Thinks Out Loud.traitNarrativeEffects: Thinking aloud can organize ideas, expose patterns, and invite collaboration, but can reveal intentions, undermine stealth, and irritate people who need quiet. Never invent the character's dialogue.

Super Sensitive.name: Super Sensitive
Super Sensitive.description: You notice emotional shifts, criticism, tension, and sensory details intensely.
Super Sensitive.traitNarrativeEffects: Heightened sensitivity can improve empathy and reading a room, but criticism, conflict, noise, or emotional tension may be more draining and distracting. This is not a diagnosis and does not remove agency.

Crybaby.name: Crybaby
Crybaby.description: You tear up easily when overwhelmed, hurt, frustrated, moved, or emotionally exposed.
Crybaby.traitNarrativeEffects: Visible emotion can invite comfort, honesty, and support, but emotional exposure may complicate confrontation and intimidation. Never force tears or invent feelings; Crybaby does not mean weak or childish.

Chaos Gremlin.name: Chaos Gremlin
Chaos Gremlin.description: You are mischievous, unpredictable, and drawn to clever trouble, strange solutions, and entertaining disruption.
Chaos Gremlin.traitNarrativeEffects: Chaos Gremlin energy can create surprise, improvisational openings, comic relief, and unconventional solutions. It can also derail plans, attract unwanted attention, provoke conflict, and make reliability harder to prove. The character chooses whether to act; this trait never forces reckless behavior or removes player agency.

Hyper.name: Hyper
Hyper.description: You are intensely energetic, quick to react, and eager to keep moving, talking, or engaging with whatever is happening.
Hyper.traitNarrativeEffects: Hyper energy can create initiative, enthusiasm, rapid improvisation, and momentum in urgent scenes. It can also cause impatience, distractibility, overcommitment, and difficulty staying quiet or still. The character chooses their actions; Hyper never forces behavior or removes player agency.

Turned.name: Turned
Turned.description:
A human permanently transformed by exposure to another Turned being. Turned look completely human in everyday life but require human blood or flesh to remain healthy and stable; ordinary food is rejected and vomited back up.

Builds well with: Keyed to Constitution; Vanguard Class or Defense Class; the Bulwark or Warden core; Power and Hand-to-Hand. Its Awakenings raise Constitution first.
Turned.traitNarrativeEffects: Turned biology is publicly understood: people generally know Turned require human blood or human flesh and cannot digest ordinary food. Eating normal food causes vomiting rather than nourishment. Well-fed Turned have completely normal human-looking eyes. Severe hunger causes Hunger Eyes: completely black eye whites with vivid blood-red irises. This may appear suddenly when severely hungry, smelling blood while hungry, beginning to feed, or losing control to predatory instinct; it returns to normal after sufficient feeding and restored control. Hunger Eyes are a recognizable exposure risk. Turned also have enhanced physical abilities and recovery, plus one unique predatory manifestation made from living organic tissue: glossy crimson, blood-red, black, or deep-violet flesh with veins, fibers, membranes, segmented tissue, wet or glass-like surfaces, and sharp biological edges. It may form tendrils, tails, tentacles, wings, blades, claws, armored limbs, or branching appendages, moves as an extra limb, rapidly extends and retracts, visibly regenerates, and retracts completely when dismissed. It is physically connected flesh, not magic, energy, equipment, or a separate creature. Preserve agency, concealment, feeding boundaries, and self-definition; never force a form, morality, victim, or loss of control. Resolve the manifestation and the Turned body through Power Endurance by default (living flesh, borne); a manifested blade or tendril strike is Power Force, a precise reach is Power Finesse, keeping Hunger Eyes down in company is Power Control.

Turned Origin.name: Turned Origin
Turned Origin.description: A narrative origin: the character was permanently transformed by exposure to another Turned being. This is how it happened; the Turned power style is what it made them.
Turned Origin.traitNarrativeEffects: This origin explains how the character became Turned; its only mechanical mark is the discipline of living with the hunger and a knack for getting by. The player defines who or what caused the transformation, whether it was consensual, accidental or forced, and what the character remembers. The one who turned them may still be out there, and Turned biology being publicly known means the story of how it happened is a secret worth keeping.

Kitsune.name: Kitsune
Kitsune.description:
A supernatural fox-spirit power style. Kitsune normally appear human and use foxfire, charms, blessings, curses, illusions, spiritual techniques, and supernatural mobility.

Builds well with: Keyed to Charisma; Command Class or Diplomat Class; the Provocateur or Commander core; Powers Only. Its Awakenings raise Charisma first.
Kitsune.traitNarrativeEffects: Kitsune powers primarily scale from Charisma, Wisdom, and Dexterity. They favor support, control, skirmishing, trickery, utility, evasion, and clever combinations over brute force. Fox ears, tails, unusual eyes, spiritual markings, talismans, foxfire, or spectral fox forms may appear during power use but remain player-defined and concealable when inactive. Tails represent spiritual development, learned abilities, milestones, or story growth; they do not automatically grant enormous power or godhood. Foxfire is supernatural rather than ordinary fire. Illusions deceive perception and do not rewrite reality or control actions automatically. Blessings are temporary and do not permanently increase attributes. Curses require appropriate conditions and meaningful limits. Fox Step provides advanced mobility through authored abilities. Kitsune are less durable and less effective at brute-force damage, and can be vulnerable when cornered or unable to use charms or techniques. Resolve charms and foxfire through Power Presence by default (a charm is a thing believed); a ward held is Power Endurance, a precise mark is Power Finesse, a glamour kept steady in a crowd is Power Control.

Kitsune Origin.name: Kitsune Origin
Kitsune Origin.description: A narrative origin: the character is kitsune, or became one, and has lived among humans wearing a human face. This is where the fox came from; the Kitsune power style is what it can do.
Kitsune Origin.traitNarrativeEffects: This origin explains the character's fox-spirit nature: born to it, inherited, blessed or changed, as the player defines. Its only mechanical mark is a fox's cunning and a lifetime of performing as something they are not. Shrines, elders and the superstitious may recognise the signs; the character's true shape, tails and age are theirs to reveal.

Yōkai.name: Yōkai
Yōkai.description:
A yōkai: a supernatural being of Japanese folklore, or a human changed into one, with one limited, player-defined manifestation appropriate to the concept. Its strength is being something the ordinary world has rules for; its limits are the concept's own taboos, exposure, and what the manifestation cannot yet do.

Builds well with: Keyed to Wisdom; Support Class or Recon Class; the Channeler or Sentinel core; Powers Only. Its Awakenings raise Wisdom first.
Yōkai.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what kind of yōkai, what the manifestation is, what it costs, what the folklore says about its kind, and how the character passes for ordinary. The world knows yōkai from stories: shrines, elders, curse squads and the superstitious react to a recognised sign, and a yōkai's own taboo is real. Resolve the manifestation through Power Control by default (a yōkai is its nature kept in hand); a bodily form is Power Endurance, a glamour is Power Presence, a trick placed exactly is Power Finesse. The manifestation stays within the concept; growth deepens it. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Invoker.name: Invoker
Invoker.description:
You can form a supernatural Pact with an independent Invocation: a legend, historical figure, mythological being, monster, or other story powerful enough to survive beyond death.

Builds well with: Keyed to Wisdom; Support Class or Recon Class; the Channeler or Sentinel core; Powers Only. Its Awakenings raise Wisdom first.
Invoker.traitNarrativeEffects:
The player chooses the Invocation class before the ritual: Blade, Lancer, Marksman, Rider, Caster, Stalker, or Berserker. After class selection, the ritual generates an appropriate Invocation influenced by class, player personality and attributes, circumstances, catalysts, location, compatibility, and chance; the player does not automatically choose which legend answers. An Invocation is not a Spirit Manifestation, equipment, pet, or fragment of the player's mind. It is a persistent independent NPC with its own True Name, possible alias, origin, personality, memories, legend, abilities, goals, secrets, and agency. It may speak, explore, fight independently, protect the player, form relationships, disagree, refuse, hide information, pursue personal goals, and remember treatment.

Forming the Pact places an Invocation Seal on the back of the Invoker's hand. The Seal looks like an intricate tattoo, sigil, crest, or geometric symbol reflecting the Invoker, their Invocation, and the Pact, normally appearing as a dark or colored marking against the skin. It does not constantly glow, burn, pulse, or shed particles. It may briefly react during summoning, Command Seal use, Resonance Attacks, Legendary Releases, or major Pact events. The Seal consists of three distinct sections representing the three Command Seals. Each time a Command Seal is used, one section permanently disappears or fades: three seals is a complete design, two seals shows one missing section, one seal shows most of the design gone, and zero seals leaves only the central Pact symbol representing the continuing connection. Losing all three Command Seals does not automatically end the Pact. The Seal is a recognizable physical trait; characters familiar with Invokers may recognize it and realize what the player is.

The Pact awakens Invocation Magic in the Invoker. This personal magic remains available when the Invocation is not manifested and may develop into offensive, defensive, reinforcement, support, detection, movement, enchanting, trap, or Pact-related techniques. Its style does not need to match the Invocation's class; the Invoker can become a mage, fighter, healer, battlemage, ranged combatant, defensive specialist, or hybrid. Invoker Magic belongs to the player, not the Invocation. The Pact begins with three scarce Command Seals. Hidden Bond changes through meaningful actions; high Bond can improve synchronization, efficiency, autonomy, Legendary Release control, and unlock pair-specific Resonance Attacks, while low Bond can cause refusal, conflict, failures, or independent behavior. Invoker combat is a two-character style. A critically wounded Invocation may dematerialize and recover through the intact Pact, but Pact damage or permanent loss is a rare major story event. Do not make Invocations automatically heroic, obedient, romantic, truthful, or disposable.

Invoker Origin.name: Invoker Origin
Invoker Origin.description: Your power comes from forming a supernatural Pact with an independent Invocation. The Pact's origin may be ritual, inherited, accidental, granted, discovered, or unknown; the Invocation remains its own person.
Invoker Origin.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this origin alongside the Invoker Power Style. It establishes how the Pact entered the character's life without choosing the Invocation's class or legendary identity. The player must still choose Blade, Lancer, Marksman, Rider, Caster, Stalker, or Berserker before the Invocation Ritual. Do not treat the Invocation as part of the player's soul, a Spirit Manifestation, equipment, or a disposable summon. The origin informs backstory and world reaction; the Invocation's independent identity and relationship develop through play.

Analyst.name: Analyst
Analyst.description:
You fight with your head: every guard has a flaw, every power has a seam, and you find it before you swing.

Primary Attribute: Intelligence
Analyst.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as an Analyst: watching, testing, then hitting exactly where it counts. Opponents who notice being studied get rattled; careless ones get taken apart.

Sentinel.name: Sentinel
Sentinel.description:
Calm in the middle of it. You feel the next attack coming, and you are already somewhere else when it lands.

Primary Attribute: Wisdom
Sentinel.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Sentinel: aware, unhurried and hard to catch. Ambushes rarely work on them; allies drift toward them when things go wrong.

Commander.name: Commander
Commander.description:
People move when you speak. In a fight your voice turns a scramble into a plan.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Commander.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Commander: the voice that holds a team together. Allies take their calls; enemies try to cut them off from the group first.

Blade Invocation.name: Blade Invocation
Blade Invocation.description: Your Invocation answers as a Blade: a swordsman, duelist or warrior whose legend was won at sword's length. You fight beside it with Combat Technique (+1) and hold the pair technique Crossed Steel.
Blade Invocation.traitNarrativeEffects: At the Pact ritual the narrator generates an Invocation of the Blade class, influenced by the player's personality, attributes, circumstances, catalysts, place, compatibility and chance; the class sets its combat category only, never its personality, and the player does not pick which legend answers. The character fights beside it with Combat Technique and holds the pair technique Crossed Steel, which works only while the Invocation is manifested and chooses to act with them; at low Bond it may refuse, improvise or take its own opening. The Invocation remains an independent person in every scene.

Lancer Invocation.name: Lancer Invocation
Lancer Invocation.description: Your Invocation answers as a Lancer: a spear-bearer, charger or skirmisher whose legend is reach, speed and a line held. You fight beside it with Defense (+1) and hold the pair technique Line of the Spear.
Lancer Invocation.traitNarrativeEffects: At the Pact ritual the narrator generates an Invocation of the Lancer class, influenced by the player's personality, attributes, circumstances, catalysts, place, compatibility and chance; the class sets its combat category only, never its personality, and the player does not pick which legend answers. The character fights beside it with Defense and holds the pair technique Line of the Spear, which works only while the Invocation is manifested and chooses to act with them; at low Bond it may refuse, improvise or take its own opening. The Invocation remains an independent person in every scene.
abilities: Lancer Invocation: Line of the Spear

Marksman Invocation.name: Marksman Invocation
Marksman Invocation.description: Your Invocation answers as a Marksman: an archer, gunner, thrower or sniper whose legend was made at a distance. You fight beside it with Tactics (+1) and hold the pair technique Pact Mark.
Marksman Invocation.traitNarrativeEffects: At the Pact ritual the narrator generates an Invocation of the Marksman class, influenced by the player's personality, attributes, circumstances, catalysts, place, compatibility and chance; the class sets its combat category only, never its personality, and the player does not pick which legend answers. The character fights beside it with Tactics and holds the pair technique Pact Mark, which works only while the Invocation is manifested and chooses to act with them; at low Bond it may refuse, improvise or take its own opening. The Invocation remains an independent person in every scene.

Rider Invocation.name: Rider Invocation
Rider Invocation.description: Your Invocation answers as a Rider: a cavalier, charioteer, pilot or beast-tamer whose legend moves. You fight beside it with Athletic Mobility (+1) and hold the pair technique Pact Stirrup.
Rider Invocation.traitNarrativeEffects: At the Pact ritual the narrator generates an Invocation of the Rider class, influenced by the player's personality, attributes, circumstances, catalysts, place, compatibility and chance; the class sets its combat category only, never its personality, and the player does not pick which legend answers. The character fights beside it with Athletic Mobility and holds the pair technique Pact Stirrup, which works only while the Invocation is manifested and chooses to act with them; at low Bond it may refuse, improvise or take its own opening. The Invocation remains an independent person in every scene.

Caster Invocation.name: Caster Invocation
Caster Invocation.description: Your Invocation answers as a Caster: a sorcerer, scholar, shaman, saint or witch whose legend is knowledge and working. You fight beside it with Power Theory (+1) and hold the pair technique Shared Circle.
Caster Invocation.traitNarrativeEffects: At the Pact ritual the narrator generates an Invocation of the Caster class, influenced by the player's personality, attributes, circumstances, catalysts, place, compatibility and chance; the class sets its combat category only, never its personality, and the player does not pick which legend answers. The character fights beside it with Power Theory and holds the pair technique Shared Circle, which works only while the Invocation is manifested and chooses to act with them; at low Bond it may refuse, improvise or take its own opening. The Invocation remains an independent person in every scene.

Stalker Invocation.name: Stalker Invocation
Stalker Invocation.description: Your Invocation answers as a Stalker: an assassin, spy, thief or ghost of a legend whose weapon was never being seen. You fight beside it with Deception (+1) and hold the pair technique Seal Silence.
Stalker Invocation.traitNarrativeEffects: At the Pact ritual the narrator generates an Invocation of the Stalker class, influenced by the player's personality, attributes, circumstances, catalysts, place, compatibility and chance; the class sets its combat category only, never its personality, and the player does not pick which legend answers. The character fights beside it with Deception and holds the pair technique Seal Silence, which works only while the Invocation is manifested and chooses to act with them; at low Bond it may refuse, improvise or take its own opening. The Invocation remains an independent person in every scene.

Berserker Invocation.name: Berserker Invocation
Berserker Invocation.description: Your Invocation answers as a Berserker: a warrior, monster or tragedy whose legend is fury, frenzy or a curse that fights. You fight beside it with Power Control (+1) and hold the pair technique Leash of Will.
Berserker Invocation.traitNarrativeEffects: At the Pact ritual the narrator generates an Invocation of the Berserker class, influenced by the player's personality, attributes, circumstances, catalysts, place, compatibility and chance; the class sets its combat category only, never its personality, and the player does not pick which legend answers. The character fights beside it with Power Control and holds the pair technique Leash of Will, which works only while the Invocation is manifested and chooses to act with them; at low Bond it may refuse, improvise or take its own opening. The Invocation remains an independent person in every scene.

No Power: Awakened.name: No Power: Awakened
No Power: Awakened.description: Your training stops being something you remember and becomes something you are. You read a powered opponent the way a boxer reads shoulders: the breath before a blast, the stance before a lunge, the habit they fall back on when pressed. You gain Opening Read, a trained counter that turns a watched tell into a clean, professional strike. None of it is supernatural; all of it is earned.
No Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character now notices power tells that ordinary people miss: the tension before activation, the glance toward a target, the rhythm of a fighter who relies on one trick. Portray this as experience and focus, never a sense or a power. It lets them time strikes, dodges and disarms against powered opponents with real reliability. It does not let them read minds, see invisible things or ignore a power that has no tell. Instructors and agency scouts start describing them as a professional rather than an underdog; powered rivals who lose to them tend to take it personally. Checks still run through Close Quarters Combat, Weapon Proficiency and Strike Tactics.

No Power: Breakthrough.name: No Power: Breakthrough
No Power: Breakthrough.description: Your preparation becomes a system. You carry kit chosen for the city's powers, rehearse what to do when a plan breaks, and arrive at fights already knowing the exits. You gain Contingency Play, a prepared countermeasure drawn from what you actually carry: a flashbang for a shadow user, insulated gloves for a shock power, restraint foam for a brute. It is gear and nerve, never a power.
No Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character now plays the long game: they scout, pack for the threat they expect, and keep a fallback ready. The narrator should reward that by letting stated gear and prior preparation matter, while asking what the character actually carries and where they got it. Specialized equipment has legal and supply consequences; agencies may supply it, police may question it, and the Blacklisted market sells it at a price. Countermeasures blunt and interrupt powers, they never remove or nullify them, and a power the character did not prepare for still hits hard. Powered students begin asking to train with them; villains begin planning around them.

No Power: Pinnacle.name: No Power: Pinnacle
No Power: Pinnacle.description: You reach the edge of what an unpowered human can do, and you know exactly where that edge is. Every hour of training, every scar and every plan converges into Human Limit, a single all-in sequence that powered opponents remember for the rest of their careers. It costs everything you have in that moment, and it is still only a person doing it.
No Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character is now regarded as one of the best unpowered fighters of their generation, the kind of name agencies and villains both keep files on. Human Limit should be portrayed as total commitment: perfect timing, terrain, gear and body used together, with a visible physical price. Afterward the character is spent, shaking, bruised and at real risk of injury. It cannot defeat a named opponent instantly, cannot stop powers that work at a scale no human can touch, and never becomes supernatural. Public reaction is split between admiration and alarm that someone without a power can do this; some powered heroes will feel shown up. Hero Reputation moves sharply with how it is used.

Elemental Power: Awakened.name: Elemental Power: Awakened
Elemental Power: Awakened.description: Your element finally answers the same way twice. Shapings hold their form longer, you can draw on smaller and poorer sources of your material, and you can compress a burst into a narrow, aimed strike instead of a spray. Your new technique, Tempered Lance, turns the element into a focused line that hits what you aim at and little else.
Elemental Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's element now behaves like a trained skill rather than a reflex: shapes come out on the first try, hold through a hit, and can be pulled from thin sources such as a lighter flame, a damp wall, a breeze through a corridor. Precision now limits collateral, so careful use draws less Legal Heat. It still cannot create material from nothing, cannot outscale a disaster, and forceful use still costs Power Strain. Instructors and agency scouts notice the control more than the strength; rivals start studying the character's element and planning around its material needs.

Elemental Power: Breakthrough.name: Elemental Power: Breakthrough
Elemental Power: Breakthrough.description: Your power stops being something you throw and becomes something you occupy.
