You can saturate an area with your element, holding the ground, air or water of a room or a street section under your influence at once. Your new technique, Dominion Field, lets you reshape that space and strike from any part of it, at the price of serious Power Strain.
Elemental Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now hold a whole area of their element under influence: the floor of a warehouse, the rain over an intersection, the air in a stairwell. Inside it they can raise cover, open footing, lash out from unexpected angles and feel movement through the element. This is a visible, unmistakable display; bystanders film it, police and agencies treat it as a scale event, and any collateral is clearly attributed. The field still needs real material, still obeys the element's physics, and collapses if the character is knocked down, distracted or overstrained. Sustaining it leaves them drained and shaky afterwards.

Elemental Power: Pinnacle.name: Elemental Power: Pinnacle
Elemental Power: Pinnacle.description: Your element reaches its peak for someone your age: for a few moments you can call it at the scale of weather or terrain, a storm, a flood, a collapse, a firestorm held on a leash. Your new technique, Unbound Element, is your defining move and the most dangerous thing you can do, with a heavy cost to your body and everything nearby.
Elemental Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now release the element at disaster scale for one decisive moment, the kind of display that ends up on the news and in agency case files. It can break a siege, stop a vehicle, smother a fire or flatten a fortified position, but it is not precise, it is not quiet, and it is never free: Power Strain spikes toward injury, property damage is likely, Legal Heat follows, and afterward the character is close to locked out of their power for the rest of the scene. It cannot erase a city, cannot kill a named opponent outright, and still needs a source. Heroes respect it; officials fear it; villains want it on their side.

Mutation Power: Awakened.name: Mutation Power: Awakened
Mutation Power: Awakened.description: Your mutation stops fighting you. The body has settled around it: it answers faster, holds longer before it aches, and you have found the use it was really built for. You can now commit the whole mutation to one decisive action without the warm-up, through the technique Honed Form. It is still the same single mutation, and it still shows.
Mutation Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's body has adapted to its mutation instead of merely carrying it. The narrator portrays sharper control: claws that do not snag, senses that filter noise, armour that flexes, reach that lands where intended. Everyday friction eases a little (they have learned the doors, the clothes, the chairs), but the mutation is still always on and still visible; strangers still stare. Growth deepens the one mutation and never adds another. Classmates and agency scouts start to treat it as a real asset rather than an oddity. Pushing past its design still hurts, as pain, bleeding or exhaustion.

Mutation Power: Breakthrough.name: Mutation Power: Breakthrough
Mutation Power: Breakthrough.description: Your mutation reaches a second stage. For a short stretch you can let it surge past its everyday shape: bigger, denser, sharper, more of what it already is. Surge State lets the body run at full expression for a fight or a crisis. It is still your mutation and nothing else, and the bill arrives when the surge ends.
Mutation Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now drive the mutation into a heightened state that makes the existing trait dramatically stronger for a short period. The narrator shows the change as visible and a little frightening: bones creak, plating thickens, senses flood, the body looks less like the person people know. It is the same mutation scaled up, never a new one. Bystanders back away, footage spreads, and some agencies start asking about containment as much as recruitment. When the surge ends the body pays: deep fatigue, bruising from inside, appetite and sleep thrown off, possible injury if pushed too long. A surge cannot be hidden.

Mutation Power: Pinnacle.name: Mutation Power: Pinnacle
Mutation Power: Pinnacle.description: Your mutation reaches its peak: the body becomes, for a few moments, exactly what the mutation was always pointing toward. Apex Form is your defining move, the one feat that only your body could do. It is costly enough that you will only reach for it when it truly matters, and you will feel it for days.
Mutation Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now drive the mutation to its absolute limit for a single defining feat: tearing open a steel door, taking a blast that would kill anyone else, outrunning a vehicle on mutated legs, sensing a hidden attacker through walls. The narrator plays this as a moment people remember and film. Afterward the body is spent: the character may be unable to fight, needs real rest or medical care, and carries the after-effects into the next days. It is still one mutation, cannot become another, cannot kill a named NPC outright, and cannot heal others or undo deaths. Fame, fear and official scrutiny all rise with each use.

Parasite: Awakened.name: Parasite: Awakened
Parasite: Awakened.description: Your parasite and your body have reached a working accord. Adaptations come when you ask instead of when it feels like it, they hold their shape through a short exchange, and you can trade one for another mid-fight. The hunger and the demands are still there, but they arrive as terms you can negotiate. You gain the technique Living Arsenal.
Parasite: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character and the parasite now cooperate rather than wrestle. The narrator should portray adaptations forming smoothly and on cue: a blade of bone sliding out, plates of hide rising, then shifting to something else as the fight changes. It still cannot heal the host fully, spread to others, or act without the host's say. Classmates and medics who see it are more unsettled by how practised it looks than by the change itself. Every exchange held in a grown shape leaves the parasite hungrier, and the narrator should let that hunger surface later as a scene the character has to answer.

Parasite: Breakthrough.name: Parasite: Breakthrough
Parasite: Breakthrough.description: Your parasite no longer settles for one change at a time. It can spread through your whole body into a combat form: armored, longer-reaching, with grown weapons where you need them, held for a full fight if you can pay for it. That form is louder, stranger and harder to walk back. You gain the technique Overgrowth Form.
Parasite: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now let the parasite take over the whole frame for a scene. The narrator should make it visible and visceral: the silhouette changes, joints bend wrong, the parasite's instincts press closer to the surface. The host still decides; the parasite still asks. Bystanders scream, cameras come out, and a hero agency will want a medical file. After the form ends the hunger is urgent rather than background, a change persists for days (a patch of hide, an eye that does not match), and the parasite remembers what it was allowed to become. Feeding should follow as a real scene with consent and consequences.

Parasite: Pinnacle.name: Parasite: Pinnacle
Parasite: Pinnacle.description: Your parasite can now rebuild you in the middle of a fight. It sheds ruined tissue, regrows what it needs, and for a few moments makes you the apex of whatever it is. It is the most complete thing the two of you can become, and it leaves a mark that never fully goes away. You gain the technique Final Molt.
Parasite: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character and the parasite have reached the deepest form of their partnership. The narrator should portray Final Molt as horrifying and magnificent: old skin splitting, something new and fierce stepping out of it. It allows a decisive strike and a partial return from injury, never a full heal and never a return from death. Afterward the host collapses, starving, and the parasite's demand is loud and specific; feeding has to happen soon and it must be a scene with consent, secrecy and cost. A permanent change remains. Agencies, doctors and villains who see it will want to study, recruit or cage the character.

Psychic Power: Awakened.name: Psychic Power: Awakened
Psychic Power: Awakened.description: Your power steadies. The noise of other minds stops leaking in uninvited, and what you push now arrives where you aim it. You gain Focused Spike, a tight, directed psychic strike that rattles one target's senses or concentration. Distance and walls matter less, but resistance, distraction and fatigue still do, and the headaches still come when you overreach.
Psychic Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character now controls their range and focus instead of fighting their own power. The narrator can show calmer use: fewer accidental reads, cleaner sending, a steady face while doing it. Focused Spike lets them disrupt one person's concentration or deliver a painful mental shock. It cannot read memories, rewrite thoughts or control a player character, and a strong will, training or another psychic blunts it. Overreach still shows as nosebleeds, headaches and dulled senses. Instructors start trusting them with sensitive work; anyone who feels the spike knows something touched their mind, and unconsented use is still treated as assault by the law.

Psychic Power: Breakthrough.name: Psychic Power: Breakthrough
Psychic Power: Breakthrough.description: Your reach widens from one mind to a whole room. You can hear the emotional weather of a crowd, find the person in it who is about to do something terrible, and press a single broad feeling across everyone near you. You gain Room Resonance. The scale is new; the ethics, the resistance and the cost are not.
Psychic Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now sense and touch many minds at once. Portray it as a sudden wash of fear, anger, grief and boredom, with the character choosing what to hold onto. Room Resonance can calm a panicking crowd, steady frightened civilians, unnerve a gang or find the hidden attacker in a station concourse. It pushes feelings, never orders, and it never controls player characters. Willing allies feel it as company; unwilling targets feel it as intrusion, and the law treats broad unconsented influence seriously. Agencies want this for crowd control, and civil-liberty groups watch them for exactly the same reason. Strain hits harder now: overload brings vertigo, nosebleeds and hours of dulled senses.

Psychic Power: Pinnacle.name: Psychic Power: Pinnacle
Psychic Power: Pinnacle.description: At your peak, you can bring the full weight of your mind down on another. You gain Mind Overload: a focused surge that floods one person's senses and concentration until their power gutters and their body forgets how to stand. It is the most frightening thing you can do, and it costs you nearly as much as it costs them.
Psychic Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character now possesses a psychic technique powerful enough to stop a dangerous powered opponent in their tracks. The narrator should portray it as overwhelming pressure: the target's power falters, their balance fails, and the air feels heavy to anyone nearby. It cannot erase memory, rewrite personality, kill outright, or control a player character, and an opponent with an exceptional will or psychic defense can endure it. The character pays visibly: nosebleed, shaking, blurred vision and a mind that will not focus for a while. Witnesses who felt the edge of it talk; the public reads it as heroic or monstrous depending on the target and on consent. Hero Reputation and legal scrutiny both follow its use.

Construct Power: Awakened.name: Construct Power: Awakened
Construct Power: Awakened.description: Your constructs gain working parts. Where you once made a single solid shape, you can now build something with hinges, joints, springs or folds that moves as designed, and it lasts longer before it fades. Your new technique, Articulated Construct, makes a construct that does a real job in sequence, within your substance's rules.
Construct Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's constructs are now designs rather than shapes: a shield that folds open, a clamp that closes, a ladder that extends, a ramp that tilts when weight hits it. They last longer and survive a hit or two. They are still made of the defined substance, still visible and attributable, and still cannot be living creatures, true machines or weapons unless the player's definition allowed it. Classmates in support courses start asking for help with projects; the character also becomes the obvious person to blame when a construct fails at the worst moment.

Construct Power: Breakthrough.name: Construct Power: Breakthrough
Construct Power: Breakthrough.description: Your power now builds places, not just objects. You can raise a structure people stand inside or cross: a bridge, a shelter, a stairway up a building face, a corridor through a crowd. Your new technique, Raised Architecture, shapes the battlefield itself, and holding it together under pressure costs you real Power Strain.
Construct Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now construct at architectural scale for a scene: a walkway across a gap, a bunker around civilians, a maze of walls that funnels an attacker. This changes how rescues and fights unfold, and professional heroes start asking whether the character can hold a structure during evacuations. The structure is only as strong as the substance and the character's focus; heavy blows crack it, and when it fails, people on it fall. It cannot be a working building system, cannot be alive, and fades when the character is knocked out or overstrained. Collapses are scenes, and any injuries are attributed to the character.

Construct Power: Pinnacle.name: Construct Power: Pinnacle
Construct Power: Pinnacle.description: Your power reaches its peak: one masterwork construct built at full size and full complexity, the best thing your substance can be. A titan-sized guardian frame, a fortress around a city block, a colossal tool that does one impossible job. Your new technique, Masterwork Edifice, is your defining creation and leaves you wrung out when it falls.
Construct Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now raise a single masterpiece construct at the limit of their power: a fortress around a hospital, a giant framework that catches a falling train car, a towering armature that wrestles a monster. It is unmistakable and unforgettable, footage of it spreads, and agencies and villains both start treating the character as a strategic asset. It still obeys the substance's definition: no true life, no working engine unless defined, no permanent building. When it dissolves, the character is left exhausted, with Power Strain near injury and their power barely responsive for the rest of the scene. It cannot erase a threat outright or kill a named opponent in one move.

Mobility Power: Awakened.name: Mobility Power: Awakened
Mobility Power: Awakened.description: Your movement gets reliable. Arrivals land where you meant them to, you can chain two moves without losing your footing, and you have learned to use momentum as a weapon instead of a hazard. Your new technique, Slipstream Strike, turns a reposition into a hit. Range, safe destinations and repeated bursts still limit you.
Mobility Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's chosen movement (speed, teleport, flight, phasing or whatever the player defined) is now dependable. The narrator shows cleaner arrivals, fewer stumbles and a knack for appearing at the right angle. The character can fold an attack into a move, but it is still bounded by range, sight or a run-up as the player set. Movement remains the most witnessed power: Pulse clips spread fast, and arriving somewhere off-limits is still trespass. Repeated bursts still cost Power Strain and Energy, and a blind arrival is never free.

Mobility Power: Breakthrough.name: Mobility Power: Breakthrough
Mobility Power: Breakthrough.description: Your movement scales up. You can now carry someone with you, or chain a rapid run of moves across a whole scene, covering ground faster than anyone can follow. Relay Rush is that new mode: rescue, extraction or a sweeping assault. It costs far more than a single burst, and every passenger is a risk.
Mobility Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now move others or sustain a rapid sequence of movements. The narrator portrays it as a real leap: pulling civilians from a collapsing floor, crossing a district in minutes, sweeping through several enemies. Passengers feel it (nausea, bruising, disorientation), and an unsafe destination now endangers more than the user. Agencies take notice because rescue capability is valuable; police take notice because so is getaway capability. Range and destination rules still hold; the scale is greater, not unlimited. Heavy use leaves the character winded and strained.

Mobility Power: Pinnacle.name: Mobility Power: Pinnacle
Mobility Power: Pinnacle.description: Your movement reaches its peak: for one decisive moment you are simply everywhere the fight needs you. Vanishing Point is your defining move, a single impossible run that resolves a situation before anyone else has moved. It burns you out, and it cannot take you anywhere your power could never reach.
Mobility Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now perform one defining feat of movement: crossing a whole battlefield, evacuating a floor in a heartbeat, landing a hit from somewhere no one could have been. The narrator frames it as the clip people replay, and the one heroes and villains study. Afterward the character is spent, possibly lightheaded, bleeding from the nose or unable to move fast for a while. It still follows the power's own rules: no crossing sealed or warded spaces it could not already enter, no carrying the unwilling, no killing named NPCs outright. Public fame and official scrutiny both spike.

Energy Power: Awakened.name: Energy Power: Awakened
Energy Power: Awakened.description: Your energy no longer only flows out. You can catch incoming energy of your kind, or pull it from a source nearby, hold it a breath, and send it back with your own behind it. Your control has grown enough that a returned blast goes where you aim it. You gain the technique Redirected Surge.
Energy Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has learned the other half of the power: absorbing and returning. The narrator should show it as a visible catch, energy bending into the character's hands or body and coming back brighter. It only works on the character's own kind of energy, or a source the player defined; it does nothing to a punch, a bullet or a different element. Holding too much burns, and a mistimed catch hurts. Bystanders read it as dramatic, rivals read it as a counter to plan around, and the reputation question of where the returned discharge lands still applies.

Energy Power: Breakthrough.name: Energy Power: Breakthrough
Energy Power: Breakthrough.description: Your power now works at the scale of a room or a street, not a single target. You can let the energy bloom outward in a wave, a burst or a storm, and choose how hard it hits the people inside it. The output is huge; so is the bill. You gain the technique Overload Bloom.
Energy Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's discharges have leapt from a line to an area. The narrator should make Overload Bloom loud and bright: windows blowing out, lights dying for a block, the smell of scorched air. Dialling it down to spare people in it takes real control, and failing that control has consequences. Property damage follows every full use, and the public, the press and hero agencies all remember whose energy that was. Afterward the character is drained of Energy and sparking at the fingertips, and pushing again soon risks injury or a lockout of the power.

Energy Power: Pinnacle.name: Energy Power: Pinnacle
Energy Power: Pinnacle.description: Your power can now gather everything you have, and everything nearby, into one discharge that people will talk about for years. It is the brightest thing you will ever do, and nothing comes after it in that fight. You gain the technique Critical Mass.
Energy Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has reached the peak of output for a student or young pro. The narrator should build Critical Mass as a visible wind-up (air shimmering, lights flickering for blocks) and then a single release that lights the skyline. It is aimed, but it is never gentle: whatever lies behind the target pays too. Afterward the character is completely spent, sparking at most, and may be hurt by their own power. News crews, agencies and the public will judge the character by where that discharge landed. It cannot level a district, and it cannot kill a named character outright.

Cursed Item: Awakened.name: Cursed Item: Awakened
Cursed Item: Awakened.description: The item knows you now. It answers faster, holds its benefit longer, and finds its way back when it is taken from you. You gain Paid in Full: a stronger invocation of the item's defined benefit, bought by paying its curse up front and in full. The curse still comes every time; you have simply learned to pay it deliberately.
Cursed Item: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The bond between character and item has deepened. The item can be recalled to hand when stolen or dropped, though thieves, wards and distance can delay it, and anyone who wanted it still wants it. Paid in Full lets the character push the defined benefit harder by accepting a sharper dose of the curse in the scene, exactly as the player established it. It never grants an unagreed benefit. NPCs who recognize cursed objects grow wary; collectors, occult brokers and agencies with confiscation powers take more interest. The narrator should show the cost plainly: the curse paid in front of witnesses is part of the character's public story.

Cursed Item: Breakthrough.name: Cursed Item: Breakthrough
Cursed Item: Breakthrough.description: The item opens a deeper bargain. Something it held back is now offered: a new mode of its defined power, or a second benefit you and the item agree on, with a curse that grows to match. You gain Unsealed Bargain. Accepting is your choice, and so is the price you set; the item never takes what you did not agree to give.
Cursed Item: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The item reveals more of what it is. The player defines the new mode or benefit and its added cost at this tier, and the narrator holds the item to that bargain exactly. The unsealed form may look different, louder or older, and people who know cursed objects can tell. Its pull grows: rival bearers, cults, collectors and agencies notice, and confiscation or theft attempts become more likely. The curse continues whether or not the power is used. The narrator should make the new bargain feel tempting and expensive, never free, and should never invent a benefit or a cost the player did not set.

Cursed Item: Pinnacle.name: Cursed Item: Pinnacle
Cursed Item: Pinnacle.description: You can call on the item's whole authority for one decisive moment. You gain Final Clause: the item gives everything it was made to give, in its truest form, and in return the curse marks you more deeply than it ever has. It is the strongest thing the item can do, and it is the most expensive thing you can choose.
Cursed Item: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now unleash the item at its full, defined authority. The narrator should portray it as the object waking completely: its oldest appearance, its true sound, an unmistakable presence that anyone with occult knowledge recognizes at a distance. The cost must be serious and lasting, as defined with the player: a mark, a debt, a lost sense for a time, a bargain extended. It cannot resurrect, kill a named opponent outright, or grant any benefit outside its established nature. After use, every party hunting the item learns roughly where it is; Hero Reputation depends on what it was used for and who saw the price paid.

Technological Hero: Awakened.name: Technological Hero: Awakened
Technological Hero: Awakened.description: Your technology gets its first real upgrade. After testing, failures and repairs, you have integrated a second core function into the same system and tuned the original so it fails less often. Your new technique, Integrated Module, adds that function as a dependable part of the kit, as long as battery, heat and maintenance allow.
Technological Hero: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's tech has gone from prototype to working build: the original function is more reliable, and a second planned function, whether a weapon system, a sensor suite, a mobility rig or a shield emitter, is now integrated rather than bolted on. Support classmates and agency tech staff take an interest; manufacturers may start sending emails. The gear is still equipment: it can be hacked, damaged, confiscated at a checkpoint or left charging at home, and the upgrade adds new failure points and new maintenance. Improvised uses beyond the design still risk failure.

Technological Hero: Breakthrough.name: Technological Hero: Breakthrough
Technological Hero: Breakthrough.description: Your technology gains a full deployment mode. For a short burst you can switch the whole system into a combat or rescue configuration, plating locked, power routed to every module, sensors linked. Your new technique, Full Deployment, turns your kit into a coordinated machine, and the heat and battery bill comes due fast.
Technological Hero: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now run their entire system as one configuration rather than one function at a time: an exosuit that seals and drives every module, a device array that links and runs together, an implant suite pushed to full output. Heroes and engineers recognize this as professional-grade work; it also attracts corporate interest, copycats and people who want the design. The mode is loud on battery and heat, drains backup power, and leaves components stressed; a hit to a key system in this mode can cascade. Afterward the gear needs repair time and parts, and running it in a public scene invites questions about licensing and safety.

Technological Hero: Pinnacle.name: Technological Hero: Pinnacle
Technological Hero: Pinnacle.description: Your technology hits its peak: a redline protocol that pushes every system past its safety limits for one decisive play. Everything you built runs at once at maximum output. Your new technique, Redline Protocol, can win a fight no one else could, and it almost always breaks something you will need to rebuild.
Technological Hero: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now override every safety limit in their technology for a single decisive moment: thrusters burning past rating, shields dumping all stored power, weapons firing at full discharge. It is the kind of thing that ends up in industry gossip and agency incident reports. The cost is real: components melt, cells drain flat, plating cracks, the character can be burned or bruised by their own gear, and the device may be down until repaired. It cannot do anything the system was never designed for, cannot be repeated without repairs, and cannot kill a named opponent outright.

Supernatural: Awakened.name: Supernatural: Awakened
Supernatural: Awakened.description: Your condition starts to answer you. The manifestation comes more cleanly, with less of the old cost, and you have learned a new way to turn its nature outward. Veil Breach is your signature: the condition reaching through you with real force. The origin's weakness is still yours, and anyone who learns it can still use it.
Supernatural: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's supernatural condition is steadier now. The narrator shows manifestations arriving when called rather than when they please, the cost a little lighter in daily use. The character can now project the condition as an offensive or decisive effect that fits its origin: a curse that bites, shadow that cuts, a lineage's mark that burns. NPCs react by background: fear, faith, curiosity, contempt; the law still has no clean category. The weakness, activation and cost remain exactly what the player defined, and an enemy who learns the weakness can still exploit it.

Supernatural: Breakthrough.name: Supernatural: Breakthrough
Supernatural: Breakthrough.description: Your condition opens a deeper state. You can let more of it through, becoming for a time what the origin has always hinted at. Awakened Aspect is that new mode: the curse, lineage, pact or transformation fully expressed. It is stronger, louder and harder to come back from, and its weakness grows sharper with it.
Supernatural: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now enter a deeper expression of the supernatural condition for a scene: a fuller transformation, a stronger pact manifestation, the lineage's true face. The narrator portrays it as unmistakably uncanny; observers who did not believe now do, and some will never forget it. Power grows, but so does the weakness: the thing that harms the condition harms it more in this state. Returning to normal costs Energy and heavy Power Strain, and may leave temporary marks (eyes, voice, shadow). The player still decides everything the character does in this state; it is never a loss of control unless the player chooses one.

Supernatural: Pinnacle.name: Supernatural: Pinnacle
Supernatural: Pinnacle.description: Your condition reaches its peak: for one moment you call on the full depth of the origin, the thing behind the curse or bloodline or pact. Sovereign Rite is your defining act. It is overwhelming within its own rules, it costs you dearly, and it leaves you exposed to the weakness you have carried from the start.
Supernatural: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now unleash the supernatural origin at its fullest for one defining effect: a curse that breaks a villain's guard, a lineage's power that drives back a monstrous threat, a pact invoked to its limit. The narrator treats it as a moment that ripples through the supernatural factions; the character is noticed by things that watch such matters. Afterward the character is drained, vulnerable to the origin's weakness and may carry a lasting mark or debt the player helps define. It cannot raise the dead, kill a named NPC outright, dominate a player character, or break the origin's own rules.

Spirit Manifestation: Awakened.name: Spirit Manifestation: Awakened
Spirit Manifestation: Awakened.description: Your manifestation comes out cleaner and stays longer. Its form is sharper, its movements faster, and the link between your will and its fists is steadier. You gain Barrage Rush, the full flurry of blows you call out by shout. It is still yours, still silent, and every blow it takes is still felt in your own body.
Spirit Manifestation: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The manifestation is now a reliable extension of the character rather than a flicker. The narrator can show it emerging faster, holding its shape longer and responding to quick commands. It remains temporary, silent and not an independent character; the callouts are always the user's voice. Barrage Rush lets the user direct a rapid flurry of strikes. Damage to the manifestation is still felt as Power Strain, and pushing it beyond its established range or form still fails. Classmates start recognizing its silhouette; rival manifestation users start sizing it up, and the press likes a name they can print.

Spirit Manifestation: Breakthrough.name: Spirit Manifestation: Breakthrough
Spirit Manifestation: Breakthrough.description: Your manifestation awakens its unique ability: a single defining effect beyond punching, fitting its name and nature, chosen by you. You gain Second Verse, the technique that makes your manifestation unlike anyone else's. Its reach grows too, but it is still bound to you, and its strength is still your strength.
Spirit Manifestation: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The manifestation now has a defined special property that the player chooses at this tier: stopping an object's momentum, sealing things into pages, freezing a surface, carrying sound, or another clear effect with obvious limits. The narrator should ask exactly what it does, to what, how far and what it cannot affect, then hold to that. Its range grows modestly. It remains silent, temporary and not an independent character; damage to it is still the user's Power Strain. Rival users and investigators start studying its rules; villains will try to learn its weakness. A clever use earns respect at the academy more than raw force.

Spirit Manifestation: Pinnacle.name: Spirit Manifestation: Pinnacle
Spirit Manifestation: Pinnacle.description: Your manifestation reaches its peak form: its full presence, its unique ability and its fists all moving as one with you. You gain Final Encore, a decisive assault that combines everything your manifestation can do. It is your loudest moment, and when it is over, the bruises it took are yours.
Spirit Manifestation: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The manifestation now shows its fullest form: clearer, larger or more intricate, with the user and spirit moving in perfect sync. Final Encore is the defining moment of a fight. The narrator should portray the strain on the user: the manifestation's injuries appearing as real bruises, cuts or exhaustion, and the risk of being unable to summon it again for a while. It remains silent and is never an independent character, companion or speaker. It cannot kill a named opponent outright or affect the entire battlefield. Public footage of it travels; reputation follows the callout.

Invoker: Awakened.name: Invoker: Awakened
Invoker: Awakened.description: Your Invocation Magic becomes a real discipline of your own. The personal technique you built through play is now dependable, and you can cast it with more force, range or precision whether your Invocation is manifested or not. Your Pact also deepens: through the Seal you can sense your Invocation's direction and condition. Your new technique is Seal-Woven Spell.
Invoker: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's own Invocation Magic has matured into a signature technique that belongs entirely to them and does not depend on the Invocation's class or presence. Through the Pact, the character also feels where their Invocation is and whether it is hurt or in danger, and can send a short mental call that the Invocation is free to answer or ignore. This does not grant orders, borrow the Invocation's abilities or read its thoughts. The Invocation reacts to the character's growth in its own way: pride, competition, worry or indifference, depending on its personality and the Bond. Familiar observers who recognize the Seal start treating the character as a mage in their own right.

Invoker: Breakthrough.name: Invoker: Breakthrough
Invoker: Breakthrough.description: Your Pact reaches a new level of synchronization. When you and your Invocation choose to act together, your magic and its legend can meet in a single combined strike or defense. Your new technique, Pact Resonance, opens that channel, but the Invocation decides whether to join, and the effort costs both of you.
Invoker: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character and their Invocation can now act in true concert when both are willing: the character's own spell becomes the opening the Invocation exploits, or the Invocation's attack carries the character's enchantment. How well it works depends on the hidden Bond; a strained relationship produces clumsy or refused resonance, a strong one produces something fluid and pair-specific. The Invocation keeps full agency and may refuse, delay, or change the plan. This is not control and is not a Command Seal. Rival Invokers and anyone who knows the signs recognize resonance as a sign of a real partnership, which makes the pair a more interesting target.

Invoker: Pinnacle.name: Invoker: Pinnacle
Invoker: Pinnacle.description: Your Pact and your magic reach their peak together. When the Bond is strong and your Invocation agrees, you can pour your own magic into the Pact to share a single moment of its legend: your spell and its story become one decisive act. Your new technique, Shared Legend, is the defining move of your partnership and leaves you badly drained.
Invoker: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now, with the Invocation's consent and a strong enough Bond, open their whole store of Invocation Magic to the Pact for one decisive moment. The Invocation's legend and the character's own magic merge into a single act shaped by both: a Legendary Release steadied by the Invoker, or the Invoker's greatest spell carried by a legend's weight. It is visible, memorable and recognized by anyone who understands Invokers; the Seal reacts briefly. The Invocation remains its own person and can refuse; forcing it requires a Command Seal and damages trust. Afterwards the Invoker is exhausted, near lockout, and the Invocation may need time to recover. It does not raise the dead or end a named enemy outright.

Magical Power: Awakened.name: Magical Power: Awakened
Magical Power: Awakened.description: Your practice matures. Workings you once needed full preparation for now come with a shortened form, and your tradition yields a second reliable working alongside the first. Bound Formula is your new signature: a stronger prepared spell. Components, words, focus and bargains still matter, and an ambushed caster is still vulnerable.
Magical Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's magic is more confident now. The narrator shows faster casting where the tradition allows, cleaner effects and fewer misfires, while preserving what makes magic magic: requirements, preparation, rules. The character can hold a prepared working ready for a scene and release it with a short word or gesture. Teachers and rival practitioners begin to take them seriously. Without components or focus, major magic still fails or misfires, and a misfire is still a scene. The tradition's limits and who taught it still shape what can and cannot be done.

Magical Power: Breakthrough.name: Magical Power: Breakthrough
Magical Power: Breakthrough.description: Your magic reaches a new scale. You can now perform a full ritual in the field: a circle drawn, a bargain called, a working that covers an area or lasts the night. Grand Circle is that new mode. It is slow to set up and devastating when finished, and anyone who breaks your concentration breaks the working.
Magical Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now cast workings at greater scale and duration through ritual. The narrator portrays the preparation in detail (chalk, candles, chant, offerings, whatever the tradition uses), and the payoff as broad and serious: a ward over a building, a binding on a powerful foe, a revealing of an entire neighbourhood. Interruption is the price: an enemy who reaches the caster can shatter it, causing a misfire. Bargains may grow heavier. Mages and supernatural factions take notice; some will want to recruit, some to stop the character.

Magical Power: Pinnacle.name: Magical Power: Pinnacle
Magical Power: Pinnacle.description: Your craft reaches its peak: a culminating working that your tradition reserves for masters. Arcanum Unsealed is your defining spell, the full power of everything you have studied released at once. It requires your best preparation, it exacts a heavy price, and it cannot do what your tradition says magic cannot do.
Magical Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now perform one culminating working of their tradition: a ward that turns aside a disaster, a binding that pins a powerful villain, a bolt that breaks a fortress wall, as the tradition allows. The narrator treats this as a feat that reshapes the character's standing among practitioners. The cost is severe: exhaustion, a bargain called in, a component consumed for good, Power Strain that leaves the character barely standing. It cannot resurrect, kill a named NPC outright, control a player character, or break the tradition's established limits.

Gravity Power: Awakened.name: Gravity Power: Awakened
Gravity Power: Awakened.description: Your fields now have a centre you can place. Instead of making a whole area heavier or lighter, you can set a point of pull that drags loose things and people toward it, then let them drop. You also learn to stand inside your own field without being caught by it. You gain the technique Gravity Well.
Gravity Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has learned to shape gravity around a point rather than a whole zone. The narrator should show debris skittering across asphalt toward an invisible spot, people sliding off-balance, then a hard drop. The character can now remain unaffected inside their own field, which makes close-range work possible. It still struggles with heavy mass and wide areas, and anyone caught near the point is pulled in unless spared. Bystanders who feel themselves tugged sideways will be frightened, and insurers will ask questions about every cracked kerb.

Gravity Power: Breakthrough.name: Gravity Power: Breakthrough
Gravity Power: Breakthrough.description: Your gravity can now change direction. You can turn down into sideways or up across an area, set people drifting or flying, or tip a whole fight onto a new floor. It is disorienting for everyone, including you if you lose focus. You gain the technique Inverted Sky.
Gravity Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now flip the direction of gravity, not just its strength. The narrator should portray it as surreal and dangerous: rain falling sideways, cars sliding up a wall, people clinging to lampposts. Allies can be carried along if shaped into the field. The character must hold it with real effort; a dropped field drops everything at once, and that fall can injure bystanders. Public reaction is a mix of awe and panic, and agencies will treat the character as a serious asset or a serious liability depending on how the landing goes.

Gravity Power: Pinnacle.name: Gravity Power: Pinnacle
Gravity Power: Pinnacle.description: You can now crush gravity down to a single collapsing point: a pull so fierce it bends the street around it and folds whatever is at its heart. It is the most dangerous thing you know how to do, and it hurts you to hold it. You gain the technique Collapse Point.
Gravity Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has reached gravity's peak for their stage. The narrator should portray Collapse Point as a horror of physics: streetlights bending toward a point, asphalt rippling, the air thick and loud. It can devastate one target and wreck everything around them, but it is not a black hole and it cannot swallow a district. The character pays with nosebleeds, blackouts, and a body that feels crushed by its own pull. Collateral damage is likely, and the public and agencies will hold the character responsible for every building it touches.

Shadow Power: Awakened.name: Shadow Power: Awakened
Shadow Power: Awakened.description: Shadow answers you faster and holds longer. You can wait inside darkness without it fraying, and strike out of it before anyone has turned their head. You gain Shade Ambush, a strike delivered from concealment. Light is still your enemy, and sound, heat and cameras still give you away.
Shadow Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's shadow use is now reliable. The narrator can show the character slipping into shade more smoothly and staying unseen longer, with shadows bending slightly toward them. Shade Ambush lets them strike from hiding with real impact. Steady light still breaks the power, and being unseen is still not being undetectable: dogs, thermal cameras and careful listeners still work. Security teams start planning around them; colleagues sometimes find their quiet arrivals unnerving. Rumours begin: a figure in the dark who leaves no footage.

Shadow Power: Breakthrough.name: Shadow Power: Breakthrough
Shadow Power: Breakthrough.description: Your darkness grows from a hiding place to a held space. You can drown a room or alley in shadow that you see through and others do not. You gain Blackout Veil. It is a new scale, and it is costly: every moment you hold it, the dark leans on you, and one steady light can cut a hole straight through it.
Shadow Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now hold darkness over an area, controlling visibility in a room, stairwell or alley. The narrator should portray it as thick, quiet darkness that resists dim light but yields to strong, steady light. Inside it, the character moves and perceives normally and others struggle. Allies can be guided, enemies confused. It does not stop sound, heat, cameras or dogs, and it is not a wall. Public use draws attention: blackouts in public spaces alarm civilians and draw police; agencies value it for extraction and stealth work.

Shadow Power: Pinnacle.name: Shadow Power: Pinnacle
Shadow Power: Pinnacle.description: For a few moments, you stop casting a shadow and become one. You gain Eclipse Passage: your body turns to living dark that slides along connected shadow, untouchable by ordinary blows, and returns to flesh in a single decisive strike. It is the peak of your power, and light can end it violently.
Shadow Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now briefly become shadow itself. The narrator should portray this as eerie and fragile: the body flattening into darkness, moving along connected shade through a floor or building, then tearing back into form for a strike. While in shadow form, ordinary physical attacks pass through, but strong light forces them out painfully and sound or heat can still betray where they are. It cannot carry other people, cross unbroken light, or last long. Witnesses describe it as terrifying; the press may call them a villain until they prove otherwise. Hero Reputation depends on the visible result.

Sound Power: Awakened.name: Sound Power: Awakened
Sound Power: Awakened.description: Your sound learns to aim. You can now shape a tight beam or cone of sound that hits what you point it at and spares the people beside it, and you can tune a note to the resonance of one object. Your new technique, Tuned Beam, makes your power precise instead of public, though your own ears still pay.
Sound Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now direct sound narrowly: a focused beam that rattles one opponent while allies a step away hear only a hum, or a tone tuned to a single pane of glass, lock or weapon until it cracks. This makes them far more usable in crowds and rescues, and teachers notice the improved control. Sound still travels: walls echo, people nearby still hear something, and a beam fired in a city is still a noise complaint. It still cannot shatter what it cannot reach, and heavy use still costs Power Strain as ringing, headaches and bleeding ears.

Sound Power: Breakthrough.name: Sound Power: Breakthrough
Sound Power: Breakthrough.description: Your power now fills and holds a space. You can set a standing wave through a room or a stretch of street, a field of vibration that shakes, maps and muffles everything inside it. Your new technique, Standing Wave, controls an area through sound, and it hurts your own hearing to hold.
Sound Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now sustain sound across an area: echoing it back to map every movement inside, setting a vibration that makes footing and aim unsteady, deadening noise to cover an evacuation, or pushing a pressure wall that slows a charge. Everyone inside is affected unless the character spends effort to spare them, and a field like this is felt through floors and walls nearby, so neighbors, police and agencies notice. It cannot pass through what it cannot reach, struggles in open air, and leaves the character with ringing, headaches and temporary deafness after long use.

Sound Power: Pinnacle.name: Sound Power: Pinnacle
Sound Power: Pinnacle.description: Your sound reaches its peak: one overwhelming crescendo that rolls through a whole block, or one perfect silence that swallows it. Your new technique, Crescendo Break, is your defining move, loud enough to stop a fight and costly enough that you may not hear anything for a while after.
Sound Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now release sound at its peak scale for one decisive moment: a crescendo that blows out windows down a street and drops opponents to their knees, or a silence so total that no alarm, voice or weapon makes a sound inside it. It is unmistakably public; it is reported, recorded and investigated, and Legal Heat follows any damage. The character's ears pay the price: temporary deafness, bleeding and disorientation are likely, and their power is barely usable for the rest of the scene. It cannot shatter what it cannot reach, cannot spare everyone in range automatically, and cannot kill a named opponent outright.

Time Power: Awakened.name: Time Power: Awakened
Time Power: Awakened.description: Your borrowed seconds come cleaner. You can now cut a window precisely, using the instant you need without spilling over, and you can spend it on a sharp chain of actions. Stolen Beat is your signature: a short sequence nobody else gets to answer. Every second is still paid back, and nothing you do can undo what has already happened.
Time Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's control over their temporal window is tighter. The narrator shows the world stuttering for others while the character acts with precision: a dodge that should not have worked, a catch made in a frozen heartbeat, a few strikes that seem to land together. Witnesses are confused and footage is ambiguous; time powers remain hard to see and easy to doubt. The power cannot undo events, rewind, or create additional turns beyond the window. Every borrowed second still returns as Power Strain and Energy, and a window held too long collapses on the user.

Time Power: Breakthrough.name: Time Power: Breakthrough
Time Power: Breakthrough.description: Your power reaches a new mode: you can now lay a slow field over a small space or a few people, or lend your quickened tempo to an ally for a moment. Tempo Field is that leap. It changes the shape of a fight, and the debt you take on for it is much heavier. Time is still not yours to rewind.
Time Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now affect a small area or a handful of people with altered tempo: slowing enemies within a room-sized space, or quickening a single ally briefly. The narrator portrays it as eerie: bullets lazy in the air, rain hanging, an ally moving like a blur. It is still small-scale and still borrowed. Holding the field tears at the user; when it collapses, the character may suffer nosebleeds, headaches, lost time or shaking. It never undoes events, never rewinds, and cannot touch more than a small space. Agencies who see it want it; researchers who hear of it want to study it.

Time Power: Pinnacle.name: Time Power: Pinnacle
Time Power: Pinnacle.description: Your power reaches its peak: you can hold a single moment almost still and walk through it. Still Point is your defining move, a brief stretch where only you move. It is the most expensive thing you can do, and it cannot change anything that has already happened.
Time Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now nearly stop time in a small area for a brief, intensely costly moment, acting while everyone else is all but frozen. The narrator treats it as a defining feat: a rescue no one sees happen, a strike that seems to come from nowhere. The aftermath is brutal: heavy Power Strain, lost Energy, possible injury, temporary confusion or a sense of time slipping for hours. It cannot rewind, undo, freeze a whole district, kill a named NPC outright, or alter past events. It is a held instant, not a reset.

Probability Power: Awakened.name: Probability Power: Awakened
Probability Power: Awakened.description: Your sense of the odds has sharpened. You can now feel how a short run of chances is leaning and nudge several of them, one after another, toward the same goal. Every nudge is still deniable, and every one adds to the bill. You gain the technique Stacked Deck.
Probability Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character now reads probability as a run of events, not a single moment. The narrator should show it as an uncanny chain of small breaks: a door that sticks just long enough, a guard who looks away, a ricochet that finds the cable. Nothing in that chain is impossible and nothing is certain; each nudge can still fail. Nobody can prove a power was used, which means suspicion, not credit. The narrator should let the debt build quietly and pay it later with a coincidence that matters, sized to how much luck the character drew.

Probability Power: Breakthrough.name: Probability Power: Breakthrough
Probability Power: Breakthrough.description: Your luck no longer stays with you. You can push it outward: tilting the odds for allies, or drawing bad luck down on a single opponent as a cascade of small, plausible failures. Nobody can prove you did it, and the bill grows with the spread. You gain the technique Jinx Cascade.
Probability Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has learned to spend probability on others. The narrator should portray Jinx Cascade as an unlucky streak that looks natural: a gun that jams, a heel that snaps, a power that misfires at the worst moment. Every failure is plausible and each one can still be avoided by skill or luck of the target's own. Named NPCs' key choices are not affected, and certainty is never possible. The debt now spreads too: the narrator should bring it due as coincidences that cost the character or the people near them. Rivals start whispering the word jinx.

Probability Power: Pinnacle.name: Probability Power: Pinnacle
Probability Power: Pinnacle.description: You can now lean the whole scene on one long shot: something possible but wildly unlikely, the kind of outcome people call a miracle afterward. It is still only a chance, and the bill for it is the heaviest you will ever pay. You gain the technique Long Shot.
Probability Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has reached the peak of their power: they can make one improbable outcome become a live, likely possibility. The narrator should portray it as a held breath for the whole scene and a result that seems impossible but has a plausible explanation. It can still fail, it cannot make the impossible happen, and it cannot kill a named NPC or override a player character's choice. Afterward the debt arrives hard and in the narrator's timing: a serious misfortune to the character or someone close, a bad streak, a turn of the world. No one can prove what happened, and that can make the character a suspect.

Barrier Power: Awakened.name: Barrier Power: Awakened
Barrier Power: Awakened.description: Your barriers stop being something you raise around yourself and become something you place. You can throw a ward to cover someone across the room before the blow lands. You gain Interception Ward. It saves lives, but every hit it takes is still paid in your Power Strain, and if it breaks it still knocks the breath out of you.
Barrier Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's barriers are now quick, precise and placeable at a distance. The narrator should show them reacting to danger by casting wards to teammates or civilians. Interception Ward can be used reactively, but it is limited to small areas and one target or group at a time. It still costs Power Strain with every hit, and a broken barrier stuns them. Rescue teams want them on call; civilians who see them catch a falling beam remember the face. Failing under people would still be the worst thing that could happen to them.

Barrier Power: Breakthrough.name: Barrier Power: Breakthrough
Barrier Power: Breakthrough.description: Your barriers reach a new scale. You can raise a dome over a street corner, a train platform or a crowd, or turn the same field inward to contain someone dangerous. You gain Sanctuary Dome. It is the power people pray for in a disaster, and holding it is the hardest thing you have ever done.
Barrier Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now shield or contain large areas. Sanctuary Dome can protect a crowd from debris or attack, or trap a dangerous opponent inside a field. The narrator should show the effort plainly: sweating, trembling, cracks spreading through the field as it takes hits. Every hit costs Power Strain, and if it breaks, everyone inside is at risk and the user is stunned. Agencies and emergency services value this highly; public expectation rises, and so does the pressure if it fails. Villains learn to attack the user rather than the field.

Barrier Power: Pinnacle.name: Barrier Power: Pinnacle
Barrier Power: Pinnacle.description: For one critical moment, your barrier does not break. You gain Unbreaking Line: a wall that holds against a building collapse, a villain's strongest attack, or a disaster that should have killed everyone behind it. When it ends, you fall. It is the defining rescue of your career.
Barrier Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now create a barrier that refuses to break for a short span, absorbing catastrophic force. The narrator should portray it as the moment everyone remembers: the field shining under impossible pressure, the user screaming or silent with effort. When it ends, the user collapses or is badly drained, with real risk of injury or temporary inability to use their power. It cannot hold forever, cannot cover an entire district, and does not heal anyone it protects. News crews film it; Hero Reputation can rise dramatically, and so do expectations.

Portal Power: Awakened.name: Portal Power: Awakened
Portal Power: Awakened.description: Your gates open faster and land more precisely. You can now open a portal in the path of something already moving, catching an incoming attack or a falling person and sending it where you choose. Your new technique, Return Gate, turns the opponent's own momentum into your weapon, within your normal range and rules.
Portal Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now open gates on reflex: in front of a bullet, beneath a falling worker, in the path of a punch. Things that pass through keep their momentum, which means an opponent's attack can come back at them or hit a wall instead of a hostage. This is the first time the character's power reads as a fighting style rather than a convenience, and opponents begin fighting more carefully around them. Portals still need the far side seen or known, still carry only what the player's rules allow, and remain doors: anything can come back through. Misplaced gates have consequences.

Portal Power: Breakthrough.name: Portal Power: Breakthrough
Portal Power: Breakthrough.description: Your power reaches the scale of a network. You can now hold several linked gates at once, or open one large enough for a group or a car, and move people across a scene like pieces on a board. Your new technique, Linked Thresholds, makes distance stop mattering for everyone around you, at the cost of serious Power Strain.
Portal Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now coordinate multiple linked portals or a single large one: evacuating a floor, moving a team behind the enemy, routing traffic away from a collapse. This is a qualitative leap for rescue and tactics, and agencies start asking about logistics work. Portals remain doors: each one can be watched, entered or attacked from both sides, and enemies can use the network if the character does not close it quickly. The character must know or see each destination, and holding several gates under load is exhausting. A wrong exit or a gate collapsing mid-transit is a real scene with consequences.

Portal Power: Pinnacle.name: Portal Power: Pinnacle
Portal Power: Pinnacle.description: Your power reaches its peak: one door that goes far beyond your usual range, or one gate wide enough to swallow a disaster and release it somewhere empty. Your new technique, Horizon Door, is your defining move, and it leaves you drained and unable to open more than the smallest gate afterward.
Portal Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now open a single portal at the far edge of what any young pro can do: across Tokyo to a place they know intimately, or wide enough to take in a collapsing beam, a flood or a villain's full-power attack and release it into empty sky, sea or a cleared lot. It changes how heroes plan around them and draws the attention of people who want the character's power for smuggling, escapes or worse. The cost is severe: heavy Power Strain, nosebleeds or blackouts, and near lockout afterward. It still needs a known destination, still works both ways while open, cannot cut or erase named opponents, and a bad exit remains a consequence.

Illusion Power: Awakened.name: Illusion Power: Awakened
Illusion Power: Awakened.description: Your illusions grow sharper. They hold better under a glance, cover more than one sense at once, and survive a little doubt. Phantom Ambush is your signature: a layered deception that pulls an enemy's attention exactly where you want it. They still do no harm themselves, still break on contact, and still fail against a mind that knows.
Illusion Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's illusions are more convincing: sound matches sight, shadows fall right, a fake opponent moves with real weight. The narrator shows enemies swinging at nothing, turning toward the wrong door, hesitating at a fire that does not burn. A target who touches the illusion, is told, or has good reason to doubt still sees through. Illusions never damage directly; what a convinced target does is their own act. Civilians may panic or feel betrayed when the trick is revealed, and the public sometimes questions whether anything the character shows is real.

Illusion Power: Breakthrough.name: Illusion Power: Breakthrough
Illusion Power: Breakthrough.description: Your illusions take on a new scale. You can now hold a whole scene: a false room, a crowd, a disguised street, sustained while you move and act. Living Mirage is that new mode, and it lets you rewrite what many people perceive at once. It strains you heavily, and one sharp observer can still pull the thread.
Illusion Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now sustain broad illusions covering a space and several people, such as a disguised alley, a fake crowd or a false layout of a building. The narrator portrays it as an elaborate performance, demanding focus and stamina. It still does no harm directly, and anyone who touches, is told, or has strong reason to doubt sees through; others may follow once someone shouts the truth. Holding it drains Energy and builds Power Strain quickly. Its reach invites distrust: the public and officials begin to wonder what else the character has shown them.

Illusion Power: Pinnacle.name: Illusion Power: Pinnacle
Illusion Power: Pinnacle.description: Your illusions reach their peak: for a few moments you can rewrite a whole scene so completely that even careful minds hesitate. Grand Deception is your defining move. It is the most convincing thing you will ever build, and holding it costs you dearly. It still harms no one and controls no one.
Illusion Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now create a single, nearly flawless illusion over a large area, convincing even trained observers for a brief time: a collapsed building that stands, a hero who is not there, a villain's base that appears empty. The narrator plays it as legendary trickery. The cost is heavy: strain headaches, Energy drained, possible nosebleeds or temporary blurred senses. Contact, a direct contradiction, or a mind that knows still breaks it. It never deals damage, never controls a player character, never kills a named NPC, and cannot change physical reality.

Nullification Power: Awakened.name: Nullification Power: Awakened
Nullification Power: Awakened.description: Your suppression now holds while you move. Once you have touched or reached a power, you can keep it quiet through a short exchange without standing still and concentrating. You also feel unfamiliar powers more clearly before you still them. You gain the technique Severing Touch.
Nullification Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now sustain a suppression through motion, which makes them a real problem for any powered opponent in reach. The narrator should portray the target feeling the power drain away, a blast fading in their hands. It still requires the character's defined reach, a stronger or stranger power still resists, and the power always comes back when the hold ends. Nullification still does nothing to a gun, a fist or a fall. Powered NPCs grow wary near the character, and both agencies and villains begin keeping an eye on them.

Nullification Power: Breakthrough.name: Nullification Power: Breakthrough
Nullification Power: Breakthrough.description: Your nullification spreads from a point to a zone. You can let a quiet settle around you where every active power weakens, flickers or fails, yours and your allies' included. It is the reason agencies want you and villains fear you. You gain the technique Silent Zone.
Nullification Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character now projects a zone of suppression. The narrator should portray it as a strange stillness: lights from energy powers dimming, constructs sagging, flight faltering at its edge. Every power in the zone is weakened, friend or foe, unless the character works hard to exclude someone. Stronger powers push back and may hold on. Nothing ordinary is affected, so armed enemies become more dangerous inside it. Powered NPCs feel it as a pressure and react with fear, anger or calculation, and the character's reputation as a nullifier begins to precede them.

Nullification Power: Pinnacle.name: Nullification Power: Pinnacle
Nullification Power: Pinnacle.description: For a few moments you can achieve total stillness: one power, however strong, goes completely silent in your grip. It is the closest a nullifier gets to absolute, and it takes everything you have to hold it. The power still comes back when you let go; you only ever silence, never erase. You gain the technique Total Stillness.
Nullification Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has reached the peak of suppression. The narrator should portray Total Stillness as a terrible quiet: a powerful foe suddenly ordinary, confused and exposed. Even then, the strongest powers get a chance to resist, and the suppression ends after a few moments, with the power returning fully intact. It never permanently erases a power. Afterward the character is numb, shaking, their own power, if any, gone quiet for a while. Witnesses will tell stories; agencies will want contracts, villains will put a price on the character's head, and powered NPCs will treat them as a threat.

Healing Power: Awakened.name: Healing Power: Awakened
Healing Power: Awakened.description: Your healing becomes something you can do under pressure, for more than one person. You sense injuries before you touch them and know where to stop. You gain Field Triage, quick stabilization of several wounded people in a single push. You still cannot restore what is gone or reverse death, and every life you steady still costs you.
Healing Power: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now heal quickly and reliably in chaotic scenes. The narrator should show them moving between wounded, sensing who is worst off and stabilizing them. Field Triage closes wounds, stops bleeding and steadies the dying for a short time, but it cannot restore lost limbs, reverse death or heal lasting conditions. It costs Power Strain and Energy. Rescue teams and hospitals request them constantly; families remember them. The character may find it hard to rest while people around them are still hurt.

Healing Power: Breakthrough.name: Healing Power: Breakthrough
Healing Power: Breakthrough.description: Your healing reaches deeper. You can pull someone back from the edge by taking part of their wound into your own body. You gain Shared Burden. It saves people who would otherwise die, and it leaves you carrying their injury until your own body heals it.
Healing Power: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now treat grave wounds by sharing them. Shared Burden can save someone near death, but the healer takes a portion of the injury, visibly bruised, bleeding or weakened. The narrator should show that cost honestly. It cannot reverse death, restore lost body parts or cure lasting conditions. Hospitals and agencies value this skill immensely, and some will pressure the character to overuse it. Patients' families may idolize them; rivals may see them as a target.

Healing Power: Pinnacle.name: Healing Power: Pinnacle
Healing Power: Pinnacle.description: At your peak, your power floods out to everyone near you. You gain Last Light, a single surge that pulls a whole team or crowd back from the brink. It saves more lives in one moment than you could have saved in a week. When it is over, you will need someone to carry you.
Healing Power: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now heal many people at once to a dramatic degree. Last Light can stabilize a crowd or restore a team after disaster. The narrator should portray it as a wave of warmth, light or restored breath, followed by the healer's collapse. It still cannot reverse death, restore what is gone or cure lasting conditions. The character is left exhausted, with real risk of injury or temporary loss of their power. Public recognition is enormous; so is pressure to repeat it.

Demonic Contract: Awakened.name: Demonic Contract: Awakened
Demonic Contract: Awakened.description: You have read your contract properly and earned an amendment. Through a negotiated scene with the other party, one new clause has been added to your pact with its own agreed benefit and its own agreed price. Your new technique, Amended Clause, invokes that second term, and the entity keeps exact accounts of both.
Demonic Contract: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has grown from a desperate signer into a party who understands the deal: they can recite their terms, recognize loopholes against them, and have negotiated one new clause with a defined benefit and price. The other party respects this, or resents it, according to its interests, and may want something in return later. Faith, consecrated places and people who know the signs react more strongly as the pact deepens. The contract still never grants an unagreed benefit, the price is still paid in scenes, and overreaching draws the entity's attention. The character may now be approached by others who want to learn how to bargain.

Demonic Contract: Breakthrough.name: Demonic Contract: Breakthrough
Demonic Contract: Breakthrough.description: Your pact has deepened enough that you can wear it. For a short time the other party's power settles on you bodily, as the contract defines: horns of shadow, a burning brand, a voice that is not quite yours. Your new technique, Infernal Mantle, makes you its agent in full, and the price grows to match.
Demonic Contract: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now take on a partial manifestation of the contracted entity for a short exchange, gaining its agreed strengths at a qualitatively higher level. The change is visible and alarming: faith communities, consecrated places and anyone who knows the signs react sharply, and agencies may flag the character as a supernatural risk. The entity is present through the mantle and pays close attention; it may comment, tempt or remind the character of what is owed. The mantle grants only what the contract allows, the price is heavier and collected in scenes, and the character remains in control of their own choices; the entity cannot take over their body without an agreed term.

Demonic Contract: Pinnacle.name: Demonic Contract: Pinnacle
Demonic Contract: Pinnacle.description: Your pact reaches its peak: you can call in the greatest term the contract holds and have the other party act through you in full for one decisive moment. Your new technique, Grand Covenant, is your defining move, and its price is the largest you have ever agreed to, set in advance and collected without mercy.
Demonic Contract: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now invoke the contract's highest clause, the full weight of the entity's agreed power acting through them for a single decisive act. It is unmistakable and terrifying: people who know the signs recognize what is happening, consecrated places resist it, and the entity's attention turns fully to the character. The price must have been negotiated beforehand and is collected in a meaningful scene: a memory, a service, a debt, a public mark, never an unagreed loss. Heavy Power Strain and near lockout follow. It cannot exceed the contract, cannot kill a named opponent outright, cannot bind another person's will, and cannot be invoked by surprise without consequence.

Alien: Awakened.name: Alien: Awakened
Alien: Awakened.description: Your Astral Core begins to acclimate to Earth. Its output steadies, its flares come less often, and you can now focus it into a concentrated burst. Stellar Lance is your signature: a beam drawn straight from the core. Earth still lacks what the core truly needs, and every use draws attention.
Alien: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's Astral Core is steadier now, less prone to the instability Earth's atmosphere caused at first. The narrator shows tighter blasts, cleaner barriers, and short flight that holds its line. The character can now project a focused beam from the core. Use still draws government, media and faction attention, and watchers start comparing notes. Earth's conditions remain the cost: the core still needs what Earth cannot fully provide, and heavy use still risks flare-ups, collateral and Power Strain.

Alien: Breakthrough.name: Alien: Breakthrough
Alien: Breakthrough.description: Your Astral Core reaches a new mode: you can now draw it through your whole body in a radiant form, raising barriers, flight, gravity and blasts together. Core Ascendant is that leap. It is far stronger, impossible to hide, and the core burns hot and unstable when held too long.
Alien: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now channel the Astral Core into a full-body radiant state: blasts, barriers, flight and gravity work together at greater strength. The narrator portrays it as visibly alien: light under the skin, the air bending, the ground shifting. Footage spreads, governments and factions act on it. Holding the state strains the body and destabilizes the core; Earth's conditions make the backlash worse. Afterward the character may feel drained, feverish, or unable to use the core for a while.

Alien: Pinnacle.name: Alien: Pinnacle
Alien: Pinnacle.description: Your Astral Core reaches its peak: for one moment you release its full, unacclimated strength, the power it was built for beyond Earth. Starfall Release is your defining move. It is overwhelming, it is unmistakable, and it leaves the core dim and your body wrecked.
Alien: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character can now unleash the Astral Core's full strength in a single defining release: a blast that breaks a villain's defense, a barrier that shields a crowd, a gravity surge that pins a monstrous threat. The narrator frames it as an event observed far and wide, likely prompting official and possibly extraterrestrial attention. The core dims afterward and may need time to recover; the character suffers heavy Power Strain and exhaustion. It cannot destroy a city, kill a named NPC outright, control a player character, or resurrect anyone.

God: Awakened.name: God: Awakened
God: Awakened.description: Your connection now settles over a place, not just a moment. Where you and the faithful stand, you can consecrate the ground so your defined blessing lingers for the fight. The more people who witness and believe, the steadier it holds. You gain the technique Sanctified Ground.
God: Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's divine connection now leaves a lasting mark on a space. The narrator should portray it through the player's defined expression: a warmth in the air, a light on the pavement, a calm that steadies allies. It works best with witnesses who believe, and it fades quickly without them. Sceptics may scoff, clergy may approve or object, and rivals may call it a trick. The god's asks grow with the gift, and the narrator should bring them due in a way the player defined: an offering, a duty, a word kept.

God: Breakthrough.name: God: Breakthrough
God: Breakthrough.description: Belief now answers you. With witnesses who believe present, your connection can carry across a crowd at once: one great protection, revelation, mending or strike, of the kind your god grants. It also grows harder to deny and harder to escape. You gain the technique Divine Mandate.
God: Breakthrough.traitNarrativeEffects: The character's connection now works at the scale of a gathering. The narrator should portray Divine Mandate as a moment people will retell: a whole street feeling protected, a crowd struck silent by revelation, a strike that lands like judgment. It needs witnesses; alone, it collapses to a lesser blessing. Believers grow in number, sceptics grow louder, clergy and rival faiths take an interest, and media will name the character. What the god asks grows heavier and sooner, and the narrator should let the bill arrive in the player's defined terms.

God: Pinnacle.name: God: Pinnacle
God: Pinnacle.description: For a few moments you can let your god be seen through you. Witnesses will not forget what they saw, and neither will your god. It is the fullest expression of your connection, and the price is the largest you will ever pay. You gain the technique Manifest Divinity.
God: Pinnacle.traitNarrativeEffects: The character reaches the height of the divine connection. The narrator should portray Manifest Divinity as unmistakable and unforgettable: the god's presence visible, heard, felt, in the form the player defined. It is witnessed by many and becomes a social fact at once: news, sermons, protests, recruitment. It is never resurrection, never compels a player character, and named NPCs still choose for themselves. Afterward the god asks something serious, on the player's defined terms, and the character is drained. Without witnesses, it is only a claim and gives only a blessing.

Turned: Awakened.name: Turned: Awakened
