help_or_scout.text: Help evacuate beachgoers, question a lifeguard, or scout the breakwater.

find_route.text: Find a route onto the breakwater toward the tide-control station.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to begin the Breakwater Assault or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has handled the opening situation and either entered Harborlight Beach: Breakwater Assault or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

Storm Over the Breakwater.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 41–60 replayable Raid instance on the Harborlight breakwater. Open with immediate storm and tide pressure: evacuating civilians, a lifeguard needing help, waves overtopping the sea wall. Signal the level band through the storm's scale and the armed figures on the breakwater. Support rescue, investigation, stealth, direct assault, or leaving. Do not reveal the breakwater boss, the storm miniboss, or the full layout. After this quest, the breakwater remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Signals from the Glass Reef.name: Signals from the Glass Reef
Signals from the Glass Reef.questStatement: A distress beacon is pulsing from a partially submerged glass research complex off the Odaiba shoreline. Divers who went out to check it came back with glass growing in their wetsuits, and someone inside is still transmitting a looping message.
Signals from the Glass Reef.mainObjective: Investigate the glass research complex off Odaiba and find out what is broadcasting from inside.

respond_beacon.text: Respond to the distress beacon from the Odaiba shoreline.

examine_divers.text: Examine the returning divers or the glass washing ashore.

find_access.text: Find a way out to the half-submerged complex.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to begin the Glass Reef Assault or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has handled the opening situation and either entered Odaiba Shoreline: Glass Reef Assault or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

Signals from the Glass Reef.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 41–60 replayable Raid instance at a partially submerged glass research complex. Open with flooding and glass-growth pressure: injured divers, glass spreading on the shoreline, a looping message from inside. Support medical aid, investigation, sample collection, stealth approach, direct assault, or leaving. Signal the level band through the danger of the reef and its defenders. Do not reveal the glass-reef boss, the reef-warden miniboss, or the full layout. After this quest, the complex remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

The Seal Beneath the Heritage Quarter.name: The Seal Beneath the Heritage Quarter
The Seal Beneath the Heritage Quarter.questStatement: A utility crew digging under the Old Tokyo heritage quarter broke into a buried shrine. Hours later, the crew is missing, ward tags are smoking on nearby doorframes, and relic thieves have been seen slipping through the excavation tent.
The Seal Beneath the Heritage Quarter.mainObjective: Investigate the buried shrine under the heritage quarter and stop the relic thieves before the seal fails.

inspect_excavation.text: Inspect the excavation site and the smoking ward tags.

ask_residents.text: Ask residents, shopkeepers, or caretakers what they noticed.

track_thieves.text: Track the relic thieves to the shrine entrance.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to begin the Buried Shrine Blitz or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has handled the opening situation and either entered Old Tokyo: Buried Shrine Blitz or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

The Seal Beneath the Heritage Quarter.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 41–60 replayable Raid instance beneath the Old Tokyo heritage quarter, distinct from the lower-level Cursed Shrine Archive. Old Tokyo's social memory matters: residents and caretakers notice things officials do not. Open with collapse and ward pressure. Support investigation, warding, rescue of the missing crew, stealth, assault, or leaving. Do not reveal the buried-shrine boss, the relic-guardian miniboss, or the full layout. After this quest, the shrine remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Lights On in the Dead Floors.name: Lights On in the Dead Floors
Lights On in the Dead Floors.questStatement: The damaged Skyteeth supertower was evacuated and fenced off, yet its upper floors are lit tonight. Security drones are patrolling the façade, a service elevator is running on its own, and a maintenance worker trapped in the lobby is calling for help.
Lights On in the Dead Floors.mainObjective: Investigate who reactivated the damaged Skyteeth supertower and what they are doing at the summit.

approach_tower.text: Approach the fenced-off Skyteeth tower and observe the activity.

help_worker.text: Help or question the trapped maintenance worker in the lobby.

read_security.text: Learn how the tower's drones and elevators are being controlled.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to begin the Ascension Raid or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has handled the opening situation and either entered Tokyo Skyteeth: Ascension Raid or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

Lights On in the Dead Floors.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 61–80 replayable Raid instance inside a damaged supertower. Open with security pressure: drones on patrol, an elevator moving by itself, a trapped worker. Clearly signal that the tower is dangerous for under-leveled characters through drone firepower and visible damage. Support rescue, hacking, stealth, assault, or leaving. Do not reveal the Skyteeth boss, the drone-gallery miniboss, or the full layout. After this quest, the tower remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

The Train That Isn't Scheduled.name: The Train That Isn't Scheduled
The Train That Isn't Scheduled.questStatement: At 2:13 a.m. a train with no line designation stops at a disused platform beneath Tokyo. Commuters who board it do not reappear at any station, and the transit authority's logs insist the platform has been sealed for decades.
The Train That Isn't Scheduled.mainObjective: Investigate the unscheduled train and follow the Null-Line to its terminus beneath Tokyo.

witness_train.text: Witness the unscheduled train at the disused platform.

gather_evidence.text: Gather evidence from missing-person reports, transit logs, or a witness.

find_way_down.text: Find a way down to the Null-Line terminal.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to enter the Null-Line Terminus or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has handled the opening situation and either entered The Black Rail: Null-Line Terminus or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

The Train That Isn't Scheduled.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 61–80 replayable Raid instance at a deep-transit terminal beneath Tokyo. Open with eerie transit pressure: an impossible train, missing commuters, rail and power hazards. Signal the level band through what the train has done to those near it. Support investigation, rescue, stealth boarding, assault, or leaving. Do not reveal the Null-Line boss, the transit-warden miniboss, or the full layout, and do not link it to other instances unless established. After this quest, the terminus remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Where the City Ends.name: Where the City Ends
Where the City Ends.questStatement: A block of service tunnels beneath southern Tokyo has stopped existing properly. Maintenance crews describe stairways that keep going down, rails that run into something that is not darkness, and colleagues who came back unable to remember their own names.
Where the City Ends.mainObjective: Investigate the consumed infrastructure beneath southern Tokyo and decide whether to begin the Last Descent.

reach_threshold.text: Reach the edge of the consumed tunnels and witness what is happening.

help_survivor.text: Help, question, or protect a maintenance worker who came back changed.

measure_danger.text: Learn enough about the consumption to judge the danger of descending.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to begin the Last Descent or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has handled the opening situation and either entered Oblivion's Crucible: The Last Descent or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

Where the City Ends.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for Chikara Tokyo's level 81–100 endgame Raid instance. The threshold must feel like the end of the known city: reality and transit hazards, memory loss, consumed structures. Communicate overwhelming danger to under-leveled characters through clear warnings. Oblivion is not a party member: never place her in the party, as a guide, or as an ally here; any link to her or her Crucible remains rumor unless established. Support investigation, rescue, careful preparation, descent, or leaving. Do not reveal the Crucible boss, miniboss, or full layout. After this quest, the descent remains freely replayable.

Water Under the Floor.name: Water Under the Floor
Water Under the Floor.questStatement: Vermine runners are carrying stolen hospital supplies through the flooded intake gate of a dead pumping station on Tokyo's western edge. A scavenged drone with a Blacklisted task-force sticker is circling overhead, and the runners have not noticed it yet.
Water Under the Floor.mainObjective: Investigate the supply run at the Sunken Pumpworks and decide how to handle the Vermine cell and the people hiding inside.

watch_the_runners.text: Observe or approach the Vermine supply runners at the intake gate.

read_the_situation.text: Learn who is inside the pumpworks: militants, refugees, or both.

handle_the_drone.text: Decide what to do about the task-force drone that is mapping the entrance.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to enter the Sunken Pumpworks or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has dealt with the supply runners and the task-force drone in some way and either entered the Sunken Pumpworks: Vermine Warren or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

Water Under the Floor.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 21–40 replayable Hideout. The opening sets up the cell's moral split: Vermine runners move stolen medicine for Turned refugees while militants inside plan a strike, and an anti-Turned task-force drone threatens to expose everyone. Support observation, stealth, social approach to the runners, sabotage or theft of the drone, direct intervention, or combat. Do not reveal Daigo Hachisuka, the strike target, or the full layout during the opening. Provide a route clue or useful information even if the player does not enter. After this quest, the warren remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

The Assets in Storage.name: The Assets in Storage
The Assets in Storage.questStatement: A refrigerated courier truck is backing into the loading dock of a windowless records-storage building south of Central Tokyo. Its manifest says archival boxes, but someone inside the truck just pounded on the wall, and two agency security consultants are pretending not to hear it.
The Assets in Storage.mainObjective: Investigate the delivery at the Quiet Ward Annex and decide how to deal with whatever the Obsidian Crown Agency is storing inside.

observe_delivery.text: Observe or approach the suspicious delivery at the loading dock.

identify_cargo.text: Find out what, or who, is inside the courier truck.

choose_approach.text: Choose how to handle the consultants and the truck: deceive, steal, sabotage, intervene, or fight.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to enter the Quiet Ward Annex or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has dealt with the loading-dock delivery and either entered the Obsidian Crown: Quiet Ward Annex or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

The Assets in Storage.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 41–60 replayable Hideout. Signal the danger of the level band through professional, well-armed agency staff. The cargo is a powered detainee; the player may free, follow, ignore, or report them. Support observation, stealth, social deception using the consultancy front, investigation, intervention, or combat. Do not reveal Corvin Asaba, the null vault, or the full layout during the opening. Provide a route clue or useful information even if the player does not enter. After this quest, the annex remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Collateral Due.name: Collateral Due
Collateral Due.questStatement: A dockworker is being walked toward a bonded customs warehouse in the Tokyo Bay logistics yards by two contract hires. From what he is begging, his family's debt marker is held somewhere inside, and he has been told to work off the interest tonight.
Collateral Due.mainObjective: Investigate the Tidewater warehouse and decide what to do about the dockworker, his debt, and the Nightshade Exchange vault beneath it.

approach_warehouse.text: Observe or approach the dockworker and his escorts outside the bonded warehouse.

learn_escrow.text: Learn what the Exchange holds in escrow beneath the warehouse.

handle_escorts.text: Decide how to handle the contract hires: bargain, deceive, outbid, intervene, or fight.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to enter the Tidewater Escrow Vault or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has dealt with the dockworker's escorts in some way and either entered the Nightshade Exchange: Tidewater Escrow Vault or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

Collateral Due.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 41–60 replayable Hideout. The opening shows how escrow collateral ruins ordinary people and that the vault is also a market: any approach may have a price. Support observation, negotiation, outbidding, deception, theft, intervention, or combat. Violence can post the party to the Nightshade app as a lasting consequence. Do not reveal Ottoline Vey or the full layout during the opening. Provide a route clue or useful information even if the player does not enter. After this quest, the vault remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

The Index That Wasn't There.name: The Index That Wasn't There
The Index That Wasn't There.questStatement: Frost is forming on a drainage grate in the eastern landfill on a warm night, and an unmarked salvage van is parked beside it. Two contractors with Obsidian Crown patches are hauling up a server sled whose casing carries a calibration code from records that should no longer matter.
The Index That Wasn't There.mainObjective: Investigate the salvage operation at Reclamation Bunker 9 and decide what should happen to the leftover records being stripped from it.

observe_salvage.text: Observe or approach the salvage crew at the frost-covered drainage grate.

identify_records.text: Identify what is on the server sled and why it was never in any index.

handle_crew.text: Decide how to handle the salvage crew and their cargo: follow, bargain, steal, sabotage, or fight.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to enter the Coldline Archive or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has dealt with the salvage crew and their cargo in some way and either entered Reclamation Bunker 9: Coldline Archive or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

The Index That Wasn't There.questDesignBrief: A one-time post-arc discovery quest for a level 61–80 replayable Hideout, available only after The Machine Beneath the Brand is completed or meaningfully concluded. Respect whatever the player chose in the Broken Crown finale; Coldline is a forgotten backup tier, not a reversal, and the arc stays resolved. Do not reintroduce arc NPCs as hostages or villains. Signal the high level band through elite salvage gear and archive defenses. Support observation, stealth, negotiation, theft, sabotage, or combat. Do not reveal Mirei Oshiro, the harmonizer, or the full layout during the opening. After this quest, the bunker remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

A Throne Nobody Voted For.name: A Throne Nobody Voted For
A Throne Nobody Voted For.questStatement: A procession of crew cars is pulling through the construction gate of the unfinished Saltmarsh Tower. Each crew carries a tribute case, and one is escorting a bound rival crew member toward the tower's work elevator.
A Throne Nobody Voted For.mainObjective: Investigate the tribute procession at Saltmarsh Tower and decide how to deal with the Regent's citadel.

watch_procession.text: Observe or approach the tribute procession at the construction gate.

learn_regent.text: Learn who rules Saltmarsh Tower and what the tribute buys.

handle_hostage.text: Decide what to do about the rival crew member being taken inside.

decide_entry.text: Decide whether to enter the Regent's Citadel or leave with what you learned.

completionCondition.query: The player has dealt with the tribute procession and the captive in some way and either entered Saltmarsh Tower: Regent's Citadel or deliberately left with meaningful information about it.

A Throne Nobody Voted For.questDesignBrief: A one-time first-arrival discovery quest for a level 61–80 replayable Hideout. The Regent is a usurper inside the Villain Empire Network: a villainous player may see rivalry or opportunity, a heroic player a warlord. Never assume the player's allegiance. Support observation, infiltration posing as a crew, negotiation, rescue, sabotage, or combat. Signal the high level band through the crews' firepower and discipline. Do not reveal Valentin Arai-Sokolov, Brannoc Ise, or the full layout during the opening. After this quest, the citadel remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Hideout Ledger.name: Hideout Ledger
Hideout Ledger.questStatement: Tokyo's hideouts and raids keep score: every clear is noticed by the people who run them.
Hideout Ledger.mainObjective: Clear hideouts and raids across Chikara Tokyo, from the 1-20 dens to Oblivion's Crucible.

raid.text: Clear a raid of level 41 or higher.

crucible.text: Clear Oblivion's Crucible: The Last Descent.

Hideout Ledger.questDesignBrief: A standing ledger for the hideout system; its objectives tick themselves from the run ledger. Never run it as a mission, never send the party anywhere for it, and never complete an objective in narration: only the hideout triggers do.

First Baton.name: First Baton
First Baton.questStatement: A disturbance at Old Tokyo Station draws the player into an unforeseen encounter with Haruka Mori. The party must determine what is happening rather than arriving with a briefing.
First Baton.mainObjective: Intercept Haruka Mori, survive Second Self, discover The Silver Witness's transfer condition, and prevent the Relay handoff.

handoff_rule.text: Discover that The Silver Witness transfers only when its owner deliberately offers it and the recipient knowingly and willingly accepts.

travel.text: Reach Old Tokyo Station and stumble into the disturbance.

investigation.text: Search the aftermath for evidence connected to Haruka's next Relay contact.

find_haruka.text: Find Haruka at Old Tokyo Station and determine what she is carrying and whether a handoff is already underway.

second_self.text: Survive Haruka's opening advantage and observe how Second Self creates physical duplicates from clear reflections.

duplicate_limits.text: Test the duplicates and determine their limits, including the difference between copied visible abilities and knowledge, memories, relationships, or judgment the copies do not possess.

identify_original.text: Identify the real Haruka while she uses reflective surfaces, movement, and duplicates to protect the delivery.

resolve_resistance.text: Overcome Haruka's resistance through combat, strategy, negotiation, deception, environmental counterplay, or another meaningful solution.

resolve_artifact.text: Resolve The Silver Witness according to its actual transfer rule. Theft, grabbing the case, distraction, charm, or simple possession cannot complete the transfer.

completionCondition.query: Complete First Baton when Haruka has been defeated or otherwise overcome, The Silver Witness and its container have been meaningfully resolved according to the artifact's willing-transfer rule, the mirror outcome has been established, and physical or testimonial evidence has been recovered. Defeating Haruka alone is not sufficient, and discovering the next Runner's location is not required.

First Baton.questDesignBrief: Q1. Arrival at Old Tokyo Station begins the encounter. The player must resolve Haruka's resistance and investigate The Silver Witness rather than merely win combat. The mirror or artifact outcome and physical or testimonial evidence must be established before completion. Preserve player agency and do not invent player dialogue, thoughts, feelings, consent, or decisions.

Heartbreaker.name: Heartbreaker
Heartbreaker.questStatement: A coded reservation and damaged audio evidence exist, but Yurika Asano's venue and performance window remain unknown until investigation verifies them.
Heartbreaker.mainObjective: Confront Yurika during her performance, preserve the group's emotional agency, discover The Lovers' Needle's attachment rule, and stop the Relay handoff.

enter_booking.text: Enter the verified private-room booking and identify Yurika without prematurely triggering the confrontation.

recognize_effect.text: Recognize that emotional numbness, confusion, or shifting attachment is supernatural rather than ordinary interpersonal conflict.

observe_power.text: Observe Yurika's power and determine how her performance attacks emotional certainty and existing bonds.

protect_agency.text: Protect the group from manipulation without inventing feelings, forcing affection, or deciding anyone's relationships for them.

needle_rule.text: Discover that The Lovers' Needle follows the owner's strongest attachment and can transfer when that attachment genuinely changes.

escalation.text: Survive Yurika escalating the performance when the party begins resisting her control.

resolve_encounter.text: Defeat, outmaneuver, interrupt, or persuade Yurika without manufacturing attachment merely to satisfy the artifact.

resolve_artifact.text: Resolve or prevent The Lovers' Needle's transfer according to its established rule.

investigation.text: Recover evidence concerning Yurika's next Relay contact.

completionCondition.query: Yurika's encounter and the Needle's rule are resolved, rewards and aftermath occur, and evidence suggests the next Relay stage involves belief, rumors, or a school-linked social network. Rumor Has It remains hidden at Unknown until investigation verifies Chikara Academy, the social-belief connection, and Hearsay or Satoshi Kurose.

Heartbreaker.questDesignBrief: Q2. Hidden until verified. Jinwoo has meaningful spotlight involvement, but his emotions and boundaries remain his own. Yurika uses music, attention, uncertainty, isolation, and the Needle to divide the party. A single generic social, combat, stealth, or Investigation success cannot resolve the encounter. After completion, show aftermath, injuries, reactions, rewards, and evidence; then investigate separately before Rumor Has It activates.

Rumor Has It.name: Rumor Has It
Rumor Has It.questStatement: Contradictory supernatural rumors spread across Chikara Academy, but Satoshi Kurose's identity and location remain unverified.
Rumor Has It.mainObjective: Break Satoshi's rumor network, expose a contradiction, survive belief becoming reality, and resolve The Paper Crown.

investigate_rumors.text: Investigate contradictory supernatural rumors spreading across Chikara Academy.

distinguish_network.text: Distinguish Satoshi's actual network from ordinary gossip, supernatural manifestations, and deliberate decoys.

sincere_repetition.text: Identify how sincere repetition strengthens Satoshi's claims.

protect_agency.text: Prevent the party from simply coercing students into repeating counter-rumors.

locate_satoshi.text: Locate Satoshi while he uses crowds, phones, social positioning, and rumor-created hazards to stay ahead.

contradiction.text: Expose at least one meaningful contradiction that destabilizes an active rumor.

belief_hazards.text: Survive the physical consequences of widespread belief.

crown_rule.text: Discover that The Paper Crown recognizes whoever enough people sincerely believe has the rightful claim.

resolve_network.text: Defeat, outmaneuver, or socially undermine Satoshi's control over the network.

resolve_artifact.text: Resolve The Paper Crown through belief and recognition rather than simple physical possession.

evidence.text: Recover financial or intermediary evidence tied to Romeo's Relay payments.

completionCondition.query: Satoshi survives unless otherwise established, his active network is destabilized, the Crown rule is resolved, rewards are granted, and a financial trail is recovered. House Edge remains hidden at Unknown until investigation verifies Goro Shindo and a specific private brokerage meeting at Tokyo Financial District Exchange.

Rumor Has It.questDesignBrief: Q3. Hidden until verified. Satoshi adapts when rumors fail by redirecting crowds, seeding contradictions, exploiting reputation, or forcing competing priorities. Kiyomi contributes through organization, school knowledge, rumor flow, and contradiction spotting. One persuasion, theft, combat, stealth, or Investigation success cannot resolve the chapter. Aftermath, injuries, reactions, rewards, and evidence must precede a separate investigation for House Edge.

House Edge.name: House Edge
House Edge.questStatement: A payment trail and exchange receipt exist, but Goro Shindo's venue and wager window remain unknown until financial investigation verifies them.
House Edge.mainObjective: Survive Goro's escalating wagers, determine what he genuinely risks, and resolve The Devil's Chip through a real stake.

reach_lounge.text: Reach the verified private brokerage lounge without exposing the investigation prematurely.

find_fear.text: Determine what Goro is actually afraid to lose.

chip_reaction.text: Observe how The Devil's Chip reacts to genuine wagers with mutually understood stakes.

reject_fake_stakes.text: Recognize and reject fake, symbolic, or meaningless stakes that do not satisfy the artifact.

probability.text: Survive escalating probability manipulation as Goro tests increasingly dangerous wagers.

real_risk.text: Force, trick, persuade, or maneuver Goro into risking something that genuinely matters to him.

resolve_chip.text: Win, prevent, or redirect the Chip's transfer according to its rule.

terms_change.text: Survive any consequence of Goro attempting to change the terms once real risk exists.

evidence.text: Recover Romeo's payment records, receipts, or surveillance-related evidence.

completionCondition.query: The wager and artifact rule are resolved, aftermath and rewards occur, and evidence points toward a mobile surveillance target. Missing Frame remains hidden at Unknown until investigation verifies Mikaido Ren and a credible route or observation window.

House Edge.questDesignBrief: Q4. Hidden until verified. Goro becomes more dangerous as stakes become real, not through arbitrary stat increases. Cleo contributes through contracts, money, ownership, fraud, payment structure, and evidence. A single generic check cannot resolve the wager or artifact. Aftermath, injuries, reactions, rewards, and evidence precede a separate investigation for Missing Frame.

Missing Frame.name: Missing Frame
Missing Frame.questStatement: A payment record and camera fragment identify a Central Tokyo suspect pool, but Mikaido Ren's route remains unknown until the party establishes a credible observation window.
Missing Frame.mainObjective: Maintain observation of Mikaido, survive his reversal tactics, and resolve The Blind Man's Watch.

visual_contact.text: Establish visual contact with Mikaido without immediately revealing the whole team.

follow_route.text: Follow him through the verified route while maintaining overlapping observation.

sightline_rule.text: Discover what changes when nobody directly observes him.

prevent_escape.text: Prevent Mikaido from exploiting blind corners, crowds, reflections, transit, or broken sightlines.

coordinate_observation.text: Coordinate party observation rather than relying on one person.

reverse_surveillance.text: Survive Mikaido turning surveillance and positioning against the hunters.

watch_rule.text: Discover that The Blind Man's Watch requires direct observation of the previous owner's relinquishment.

resolve_artifact.text: Resolve Mikaido's stage and the Watch's transfer rule.

completionCondition.query: Mikaido and the Watch are resolved, rewards occur, and evidence points toward an unknown theater connection. Dead Air remains hidden at Unknown until investigation verifies Heritage Theater and Eri Sawada.

Missing Frame.questDesignBrief: Q5. Hidden until verified. This is a pursuit and observation puzzle, not a stationary fight. Lost sightlines create fair consequences such as changed position, lost evidence, or tactical disadvantage, not arbitrary teleportation. A single generic check cannot resolve the chapter. Aftermath, injuries, reactions, rewards, and theater evidence precede a separate investigation for Dead Air.

Dead Air.name: Dead Air
Dead Air.questStatement: Theater evidence exists, but Eri Sawada's venue and performance window remain unknown until investigation verifies Heritage Theater.
Dead Air.mainObjective: Discover Eri's sound condition, adapt under pressure, and resolve The Bell Without a Tongue.

enter_theater.text: Enter Heritage Theater through the verified route and locate Eri.

initial_confrontation.text: Survive the initial confrontation without being told her defensive rule in advance.

test_attacks.text: Test different attacks and observe which actions affect her.

sound_condition.text: Discover that an attacking action must produce sound to affect Eri.

adapt.text: Adapt powers, weapons, environment, or teamwork around the sound condition.

stage_control.text: Survive Eri manipulating silence, acoustics, stage machinery, or positioning.

bell_rule.text: Discover The Bell Without a Tongue's ownership or transfer condition.

resolve_artifact.text: Resolve Eri and the Bell according to the established rule.

evidence.text: Search the theater for archived transfer evidence.

completionCondition.query: Eri and the Bell are resolved, rewards occur, and evidence connects the Relay to Curse Squad historical records. Chain of Custody remains hidden until the archive connection is verified.

Dead Air.questDesignBrief: Q6. Hidden until verified. The party must discover Eri's defensive rule through testing rather than receive it in advance. Eri manipulates silence, acoustics, machinery, and positioning. Aftermath, injuries, reactions, rewards, and archived evidence precede a separate investigation for Chain of Custody.

Keepsake.name: Keepsake
Keepsake.questStatement: A handoff trail exists, but Reina Kisaragi's sale and route remain unknown until investigation verifies them.
Keepsake.mainObjective: Catch Reina during the handoff, understand what The Keepsake Box measures, and decide whether her attempted betrayal of Romeo is genuine.

meaning.text: Prevent possession, price, or physical control from being treated as equivalent to personal meaning.

betrayal.text: Survive the consequences of Reina attempting to run, bargain, mislead, or betray Romeo.

follow_trail.text: Follow the verified handoff trail without destroying evidence.

locate_reina.text: Locate Reina while preserving her possible escape routes and contacts for investigation.

box_rule.text: Discover what The Keepsake Box recognizes as sentimental value.

refusal.text: Determine why Reina refuses the sacrifice Romeo expects.

resolve_box.text: Resolve the Box according to its rule.

decision.text: Decide whether to help, bargain with, distrust, expose, or abandon Reina.

message.text: Recover or receive Reina's next message.

completionCondition.query: The Box's rule and Reina's stage are resolved. Her ultimate loyalty remains uncertain. The Runner Who Ran remains hidden at Unknown until a verified escape route is established.

Keepsake.questDesignBrief: Q9. Hidden until verified. Preserve evidence and escape routes while pursuing Reina. The Box measures sentimental value, not possession or price. Reina may run, bargain, mislead, or betray Romeo. Aftermath, rewards, and her next message precede a separate investigation; The Runner Who Ran activates only after the escape route is verified.

Last Call.name: Last Call
Last Call.questStatement: Evidence points toward a tower contact, but Toma Arakawa's meeting window remains unknown until investigation verifies it.
Last Call.mainObjective: Survive Toma's final conditions, overcome the last Runner test, and earn a credible route to Romeo.

reach_toma.text: Reach Toma during the verified meeting window.

understand_stage.text: Determine the rules governing his stage before committing blindly.

final_attempts.text: Survive Toma's declared final attempts or conditions.

adapt.text: Adapt when the obvious solution fails.

motive.text: Identify what Toma actually wants from the confrontation.

condition.text: Exploit the real condition rather than brute-forcing the stage.

resolve_toma.text: Defeat, persuade, outmaneuver, or survive Toma.

romeo_location.text: Obtain information identifying Romeo's final archive.

verify_information.text: Verify Toma's information instead of automatically trusting it.

completionCondition.query: Toma's stage is resolved and rewards occur. The party obtains a strong lead to Romeo's archive. The Devil's Relay remains hidden at Unknown until a separate investigation verifies Old Tokyo Cursed Shrine Archive.

Last Call.questDesignBrief: Q13. Hidden until verified. Toma's stage requires discovery, adaptation, and counterplay rather than brute force. Aftermath, rewards, and a strong archive lead precede a separate investigation that cross-checks Toma's route against records, shrine access, prior evidence, and Romeo's behavior.

Chain of Custody.name: Chain of Custody
Chain of Custody.questStatement: Theater evidence connects the Relay to Curse Squad records. The party must verify archive access before beginning the investigation chapter.
Chain of Custody.mainObjective: Reconstruct the Relay's transfer history and determine why Doge's katana matters to Romeo's experiment.

access.text: Enter the relevant archive under plausible access conditions.

compare_records.text: Compare recovered Runner evidence against historical transfer records.

contradictions.text: Identify missing, altered, sealed, or contradictory reports.

experiment.text: Determine that Romeo is studying supernatural ownership transfer rather than merely collecting cursed objects.

complication.text: Resolve an archive complication such as damaged records, hostile artifact activity, missing evidence, interference, or another established threat.

inheritance.text: Discover that Doge's katana carries a meaningful inheritance relationship.

pressure_point.text: Verify that Romeo has identified Doge's weapon as a Relay problem he intends to test.

completionCondition.query: The party understands the Relay experiment at a deeper level and confirms Doge's katana as Romeo's next pressure point. Old Dog, Old Sword activates only after this chapter completes.

Chain of Custody.questDesignBrief: Q7. This is the archive investigation chapter, not an automatic combat transition. Verify access first, then compare records, resolve contradictions, handle a complication, and establish why Doge's katana matters. Old Dog, Old Sword activates only after completion.

Old Dog, Old Sword.name: Old Dog, Old Sword
Old Dog, Old Sword.questStatement: Archive evidence confirms Romeo's interest in Doge's katana, but the party must investigate and prepare before the pressure chapter begins.
Old Dog, Old Sword.mainObjective: Understand the katana's inheritance state, preserve Doge's agency, and stop Romeo from forcing an ownership outcome.

history.text: Examine the katana's inheritance history without forcing Doge to surrender it.

meaning.text: Determine what the artifact recognizes as inheritance, stewardship, possession, or claim.

message.text: Analyze Romeo's message and identify what he wants Doge to prove.

protections.text: Establish protections around Doge, the katana, and the surviving evidence.

pressure.text: Survive any pressure, interference, or test Romeo introduces.

agency.text: Prevent another character from casually claiming ownership merely by taking or holding the katana.

doge_choice.text: Allow Doge to decide how he responds.

evidence.text: Recover evidence pointing toward the next handoff.

completionCondition.query: Doge retains agency, the inheritance issue remains intact, rewards occur, and evidence points toward another Runner. Keepsake remains hidden at Unknown until investigation verifies Reina Kisaragi and Old Tokyo Lantern Quarter.

Old Dog, Old Sword.questDesignBrief: Q8. This chapter activates after Chain of Custody completes. Preserve Doge's agency and do not let taking or holding the katana create ownership. Resolve pressure through the artifact's rule and meaningful counterplay, then produce aftermath, rewards, and evidence. Keepsake remains hidden until separate investigation verifies the target.

The Runner Who Ran.name: The Runner Who Ran
The Runner Who Ran.questStatement: Reina's message and movement trail exist, but her escape route remains unknown until investigation verifies it.
The Runner Who Ran.mainObjective: Find Reina after she abandons her assigned Relay stage and determine whether she can become a useful but unreliable ally.

message_trail.text: Follow Reina's message and movement trail.

romeo_misdirection.text: Identify where Reina deliberately misled Romeo.

party_misdirection.text: Identify where Reina also misled the party.

catch_up.text: Catch up with her without automatically treating her as hostile.

sacrifice.text: Learn what sacrifice Romeo demanded during her original stage.

decision.text: Decide whether to protect, bargain with, expose, arrest, or abandon her.

betrayal_consequence.text: Survive any consequence of Romeo discovering her betrayal.

shrine_evidence.text: Obtain evidence concerning a shrine-related confrontation.

completionCondition.query: Reina becomes an ally, unreliable contact, enemy, neutral survivor, or protected witness according to player choices. Good Boy remains hidden at Unknown until Reina's information and at least one independent source verify the shrine route.

The Runner Who Ran.questDesignBrief: Q10. Hidden until verified. Reina may mislead both Romeo and the party. Do not automatically treat her as hostile or trustworthy. Aftermath, rewards, and evidence precede a separate investigation using Reina's information plus an independent source before Good Boy activates.

Good Boy.name: Good Boy
Good Boy.questStatement: A shrine-related lead exists, but Romeo's confrontation point and timing remain unknown until investigation verifies them.
Good Boy.mainObjective: Reach Doge and Romeo before the inheritance condition closes, survive Romeo's setup, and support Doge without controlling his decision.

verify_confrontation.text: Verify Romeo's intended confrontation point and timing.

reach_doge.text: Reach Doge before Romeo completes the setup.

romeo_test.text: Determine what Romeo is attempting to prove through Doge and the katana.

layered_rules.text: Survive Romeo combining previously studied ownership concepts against the team.

support_doge.text: Support Doge through the confrontation without inventing Doge's or the player's choices.

preserve_condition.text: Preserve the katana's unresolved inheritance condition.

reversal.text: Survive Romeo's protection dilemma or reversal.

doge_death.text: Witness Doge's established death at Romeo Vane's hands.

evidence.text: Secure Doge's remaining evidence without falsely claiming ownership of the katana.

completionCondition.query: Doge dies as established. The immediate aftermath, shock, injuries, reactions, and absence land before rewards and surviving evidence are resolved. What He Left Behind remains hidden at Unknown until the aftermath progresses into investigation.

Good Boy.questDesignBrief: Q11. Hidden until verified. Do not begin another chase immediately after Doge's death. Preserve Doge's agency and the katana's unresolved inheritance. Aftermath, injuries, reactions, rewards, and evidence precede What He Left Behind.

What He Left Behind.name: What He Left Behind

response.text: Choose how to respond while respecting Junpei Tsukishiro's boundaries and the player's own.

completionCondition.query: Junpei Tsukishiro shares or confronts a personal pressure with the player, and the player chooses how to respond.

Junpei Tsukishiro: After Action.questDesignBrief: Personal Quest 2/4. Unlock tier: relationship 41+ (Confidant) and completion of 'Junpei Tsukishiro: Off Duty'. Canon focus from this NPC's authored record: Junpei likes people and maintains several friendships independent of the player. Junpei's competence becomes a problem because he has built much of his identity around being the person who can handle things. Build the quest from this established material rather than inventing a contradictory backstory. Use existing locations and NPC relationships where plausible. Keep the NPC active in solving their own problem. The player may accept, decline, delay, disagree, leave, set boundaries, or choose a platonic interpretation. Do not force romance, attraction, confession, forgiveness, violence, treatment, recruitment, or a fixed emotional response.

completionCondition.query: Junpei Tsukishiro's serious personal conflict reaches a meaningful decision or consequence, with the player's involvement resolved.

Junpei's competence becomes a problem because he has built much of his identity around being the person who can handle things. Build the quest from this established material rather than inventing a contradictory backstory. Use existing locations and NPC relationships where plausible. Keep the NPC active in solving their own problem. The player may accept, decline, delay, disagree, leave, set boundaries, or choose a platonic interpretation. Junpei Tsukishiro: After the Sirens.mainObjective: See Junpei Tsukishiro's personal arc through a major choice about who they are, what they keep, and what comes next.

future.text: Let Junpei Tsukishiro make their own lasting choice and decide what the relationship means going forward.

He wants to open a rehabilitation practice specializing in powered people whose abilities permanently alter how their bodies move, heal, fatigue, or experience physical strain. Build the quest from this established material rather than inventing a contradictory backstory. Use existing locations and NPC relationships where plausible. Keep the NPC active in solving their own problem. The player may accept, decline, delay, disagree, leave, set boundaries, or choose a platonic interpretation. Do not force romance, attraction, confession, forgiveness, violence, treatment, recruitment, or a fixed emotional response.

minato-training-rivalry.title: Minato's Training Rivalry
minato-training-rivalry.beats: During an afternoon training session at Chikara Academy, Minato challenges the player in front of their classmates. She begins hostile at relationship score -41 and assumes the player's power is unstable or overhyped. The scene should offer meaningful approaches: controlled sparring, defensive endurance, rescue-focused tactics, strategic use of the environment, negotiation, or creative restraint. Track Power Strain and make reckless escalation risky, but do not require the player to defeat Minato outright. Minato should react to discipline, adaptability, courage, collateral damage, and whether the player respects the training rules. A strong success moves her from Hostile toward Respect or Warm, reveals that her hostility hides insecurity about being valued only for her family, and unlocks future training or conversation opportunities. A partial success preserves hostility but creates grudging interest. A failure may worsen the relationship or create a rematch hook without ending the story.

weekly-club-life.title: Weekly Club Life
weekly-club-life.beats: Across each school week, the player may choose whether to attend a club, visit another club as a guest, pursue independent training, work, socialize, date, study, cook, explore, or rest. Club meetings should feel active rather than static: members arrive with personal goals, disagreements, rumors, projects, deadlines, and changing moods. Let club activities create practical choices and consequences. Combat Club can produce controlled rivalries and injuries; Rescue & First Aid Club can present emergency drills and moral decisions; Cooking Club can teach recipes and reveal preferences; Support Engineering Club can create equipment opportunities and dangerous prototypes; Investigation Club can uncover academy secrets; Arts & Media Club can alter public reputation; Rooftop Wellness Group can provide recovery and emotional scenes. NPCs may attend or miss meetings without the player, make plans, recruit others, form alliances, quit, or create conflicts. Do not require club membership for the main story. Let sustained participation unlock skills, relationships, special scenes, festival roles, internships, signature technique milestones, and alternate opportunities.

chikara-cultural-festival.title: Chikara Academy Cultural Festival
chikara-cultural-festival.beats: The Cultural Festival unfolds over several school days. Let the player choose a role or remain independent. Cooking Club runs food stalls under Numeri's anxious leadership, with Minato potentially joining to protect the club's reputation. Combat Club stages dramatic demonstrations led by Guy, with Nyanta emphasizing safety and Minato seeking attention. Rescue & First Aid Club, coordinated by Keito Takeda, manages safety and emergency drills. Support Engineering builds attractions and equipment, with Felix improvising risky shortcuts and Renji solving problems while pretending not to care. Investigation Club, led by Hyun, notices missing supplies, strange access records, or a hidden academy connection. Arts & Media, fronted by Hikari with Jinwoo's social influence, controls publicity and may create rivalry over attention. Rooftop Wellness Group offers quiet conversations, recovery, dates, and emotional scenes away from the crowds. NPCs should pursue their own festival plans, attend or skip activities, argue, recruit, perform, flirt, investigate, or leave without waiting for the player. During the festival, introduce a crisis such as sabotage, a dangerous prototype, a staged villain scare, a missing student, or a real intrusion. Allow solutions through combat, rescue, investigation, negotiation, engineering, social influence, or creative power use. Track attendance, club participation, relationships, reputation, grades, Power Strain, collateral damage, and public perception. End with consequences and memories that shape later opportunities, club rosters, rivalries, romances, and the academy's trust in the player.

Phone Invitation Hangout.title: Phone Invitation: Hangout
Phone Invitation Hangout.beats: The player's phone receives a call or text from an NPC with an invitation to spend time together. Establish who contacted the player, why they reached out, the proposed location and activity, and any time pressure. Offer choices to accept, decline kindly, decline harshly, suggest another time, invite someone else, answer later, or ignore. Reflect the NPC's independent reaction and update relationship memories or plans based on the choice.

Friend Group Party.title: Friend Group Party
Friend Group Party.beats: A friend group gathers at an apartment, dorm common room, café, restaurant, park, arcade, club, or rooftop. Establish who invited whom, who is absent, the group's alliances and tensions, food and activities, and at least one personal conversation or complication. Let the player participate, circulate, help someone, leave early, invite another person, or address conflict. The party may strengthen bonds, create rumors, reveal secrets, trigger rivalry or gradual romance, or produce curfew risk without forcing any outcome.

Ability Growth Milestones.title: Ability Growth Milestones
Ability Growth Milestones.beats: When the player or an NPC reaches a meaningful level, improves Power Control, completes focused training, or experiences a major story, emotional, or relationship milestone, offer one ability suited to the character's established power. Progress from Basic Power Technique to Advanced Power Technique, Controlled Output, Signature Technique, and Ultimate Technique. The character may choose, postpone, modify, or decline. NPCs can grow through independent training while the player is elsewhere.

Shadow District Oblivion Rumor.title: Shadow District Oblivion Rumor
Shadow District Oblivion Rumor.beats: Rumors spread through Chikara Academy and Tokyo that a masked figure resembling Oblivion has been seen in the Shadow District. Searching the academy, campus, or ordinary public locations finds no reliable trace. Following the rumor to the Shadow District can lead through informants, the underground club, and the black market toward a possible sighting near Shadow District Market, but Oblivion may be concealed or absent. The player can investigate, question contacts, report the rumor, stake out carefully, or withdraw.

Campus Training Emergency.title: Campus Training Emergency
Campus Training Emergency.beats: A supervised power-control exercise destabilizes when a safety barrier fails. Students are trapped between collapsing practice structures while instructors coordinate a response. The player can stabilize the hazard, evacuate classmates, assist an injured student, call for faculty support, or attempt a risky high-output technique. Power Control, teamwork, Power Strain, collateral damage, and accountability shape the result.

Tokyo Civilian Rescue.title: Tokyo Civilian Rescue
Tokyo Civilian Rescue.beats: During travel through Tokyo, an accident leaves civilians in immediate danger. The player can intervene, direct an evacuation, call professional heroes, use a controlled power technique, investigate a safer approach, or keep moving. The scene judges urgency, rescue priorities, civilian safety, public visibility, and whether the player accepts help.

Public Villain Incident.title: Public Villain Incident
Public Villain Incident.beats: A villain attack erupts in a crowded Tokyo district. The player must decide whether to protect civilians, coordinate with responders, confront the villain, create an escape route, negotiate, or withdraw. Winning the fight is not enough: rescue, restraint, teamwork, control, collateral damage, and the villain's escape all affect the outcome.

Media Pressure Scene.title: Media Pressure Scene
Media Pressure Scene.beats: After a public rescue, accident, or villain incident, reporters and bystanders ask the player what happened. The player can answer honestly, accept responsibility, credit teammates, protect sensitive information, redirect questions, refuse comment, or lie. The response changes public trust, Hero Reputation, school scrutiny, and relationships.

Oblivion Rumor Investigation.title: Oblivion Rumor Investigation
Oblivion Rumor Investigation.beats: A rumor claims that Oblivion has been seen near Shadow District Market. The player can question informants, follow concealed routes, stake out the market, report the rumor, bring allies, or withdraw. Oblivion is not guaranteed to appear and should never be placed at Chikara Academy merely because the player searches there. Evidence may be genuine, misleading, or deliberately planted.

Date Invitation.title: Date Invitation
Date Invitation.beats: An NPC with believable mutual interest invites the player to a specific date activity after school or during free time. Establish the invitation, location, proposed activity, schedule, cost, comfort level, and why the NPC chose it. Present choices to accept, decline kindly, decline firmly, suggest another time, clarify whether it is romantic or friendly, invite someone else, or ask questions. Never assume attraction, consent, or acceptance. Preserve the NPC's independent reaction and update plans, memories, boundaries, and relationship tone based on the player's response.

Date Activity Scene.title: Date Activity Scene
Date Activity Scene.beats: Play a date or intentional one-on-one outing at a suitable Tokyo location: botanical garden, aquarium, Hero Museum, night market, restaurant, traditional dining hall, café, riverside walk, shopping area, study session, training session, or cooking activity. Establish the activity's sensory details and the NPC's preferences. Let the player choose conversation, kindness, honesty, humor, boundaries, shared activity, or an early departure. Keep chemistry gradual and mutual. Outcomes may be positive, mixed, awkward, interrupted, friendly, or romantic without forcing a relationship.

Date Interruption.title: Date Interruption
Date Interruption.beats: An outing is interrupted by a believable complication such as a civilian emergency, villain incident, media attention, school obligation, power-control problem, rival appearance, urgent phone call, transit delay, or criminal contact. Let the player and NPC decide whether to help, leave, hide, call professionals, protect privacy, continue later, or end the outing. Show consequences for trust, safety, Hero Reputation, schedule, and the date's emotional tone without treating heroics as automatically more important than the NPC's needs.

Relationship Turning Point.title: Relationship Turning Point
Relationship Turning Point.beats: A meaningful relationship moment follows a promise, betrayal, rescue, disagreement, vulnerable confession, boundary clarification, rivalry breakthrough, successful date, rejection, or reconciliation. Show the NPC's independent perspective without narrating the player's unchosen thoughts or feelings. Let the player respond honestly, cautiously, warmly, firmly, or by leaving. Update only appropriate relationship dimensions and create a concise memory. Romance remains optional and mutual; friendship, rivalry, trust, respect, distance, and repair are all valid outcomes.

Power Control Breakthrough.title: Power Control Breakthrough
Power Control Breakthrough.beats: During training, rescue, a Battle Test, or a high-pressure incident, the player faces a power-control challenge. Present options based on the described power, current mastery, Power Strain, surroundings, allies, and risks. Success may improve control or efficiency and reveal a technique; failure may cause proportionate fatigue, minor injury, collateral, embarrassment, or temporary lockout without invalidating the character. Harmless use should not be punished severely. Ultimate techniques require appropriate training, story, emotional, or relationship milestones and meaningful costs.

School Evaluation.title: School Evaluation
School Evaluation.beats: A class, exam, Battle Test, rescue drill, attendance issue, discipline review, or teacher evaluation tests the player's growth. Assess preparation, teamwork, restraint, power control, rescue judgment, attendance, and consequences rather than victory alone. Present choices and preserve agency. Outcomes may affect grades, teacher approval, Hero Reputation, relationships, training access, detention, internships, or repair opportunities. Do not make one failure end the story.

Hero Rescue Incident.title: Hero Rescue Incident
Hero Rescue Incident.beats: A civilian emergency, accident, villain incident, disaster, or suspicious event occurs in Tokyo. Establish hazards, civilians, responders, heroes, time pressure, and available information. Let the player intervene, call professionals, evacuate, investigate, negotiate, use powers carefully, retreat, or ignore the situation. Reward rescue judgment, restraint, teamwork, accountability, and civilian protection rather than combat victory alone. Track Power Strain, injuries, collateral, Hero Reputation, media response, police attention, school consequences, and relationship memories.

conditions.query: The player is enrolled at Chikara Academy, it is afternoon training time, Minato is available, and the player has not yet completed the Minato Training Rivalry.

effects.instruction: Start the Training music family for the scene.

The player has returned to their assigned apartment or dormitory for the night. Offer rest, Power Strain recovery, cooking, messages, outfit changes, private reflection, and relationship scenes without forcing sleep unless the player chooses it.

conditions.query: A friend, rival, clubmate, family member, teacher, or romance interest has a believable reason to contact the player by phone today.

effects.instruction: Deliver a phone call or text from an NPC with a specific invitation, request, update, rumor, apology, challenge, party plan, study session, training session, date, errand, or urgent personal problem. Base it on relationship stage, schedule, location, club membership, shared interests, promises, conflicts, and current events. Present choices to accept, decline kindly, decline harshly, suggest another time, invite someone else, answer later, or ignore. Keep calls immediate and conversational; texts may be revisited later. Preserve NPC independence and update memories, plans, promises, and relationship tone based on the player's response.

conditions.query: A friend group has a believable reason and suitable place to gather for a party or group hangout.

effects.instruction: Offer a party or group hangout at a suitable apartment, dorm common room, café, restaurant, park, arcade, club, rooftop, or hidden venue. Establish the host, invitees, absences, current alliances, tensions, food, activities, and one personal complication. Let the player accept, decline, arrive late, invite someone else, circulate, help someone, address conflict, or leave early. NPC attendance and reactions remain independent. The gathering may strengthen bonds, create rumors, reveal secrets, trigger rivalry or gradual romance, or create curfew risk without forcing any outcome.

conditions.query: The player has completed meaningful rest, received suitable medical care, or eaten a restorative meal.

effects.instruction: Reduce Power Strain according to the recovery: light rest or a suitable meal lowers it modestly; a full night's rest or recovery-clinic treatment lowers it substantially. Never reduce it below zero.

Power Control Training.name: Power Control Training

conditions.query: The player completes a focused power-control, precision, collateral-management, or simulation exercise.

effects.instruction: At moderate Power Strain, make difficult or high-output power use require a control check and describe fatigue. Harmless everyday use remains safe. At 80 or higher, major techniques risk collateral effects, injury, exhaustion, or temporary power lockout; recovery and medical care can stabilize the player.

conditions.query: The player completes a rescue, school or rescue test, villain encounter, public emergency, teamwork scene, controlled power action, accepts accountability, causes reckless collateral damage, abandons people, uses unnecessary force, deceives authorities, or commits public misconduct.

effects.instruction: Apply one slow numeric Hero Reputation adjustment per completed encounter or public scene, clamped from 0 to 100. Ordinary helpful conduct: +1. Passing a meaningful school or rescue test: +2. Teamwork, restraint, or controlled power use: +3. Difficult rescue or strong public accountability: +5. Major villain encounter resolved while protecting civilians: +8. Exceptional large-scale rescue or major villain fight: +10. Minor misconduct: -2. Avoidable damage: -5. Serious collateral damage or unnecessary force: -8. Abandonment, deliberate deception, or repeated severe misconduct: -12. Add at most one extra +3 or -3 for major publicity or many civilians. Do not award points merely for winning; judge rescue, restraint, teamwork, control, and consequences. A defeat can still award positive points for brave rescue conduct. At 70+, offer agency trust and public opportunities. At 30 or lower, create scrutiny and repair scenes.

conditions.query: The player has heard a credible rumor about Oblivion and deliberately searches for them or follows the rumor into the Shadow District.

effects.instruction: Do not place Oblivion at Chikara Academy or guarantee a direct encounter. Resolve the search through Shadow District leads, informants, concealed routes, misleading evidence, and possible sightings around Shadow District Market. Oblivion may remain hidden or absent. Reward careful investigation, civilian safety, and restraint with appropriate Hero Reputation; reckless pursuit can cause danger, lost time, exposure, or collateral consequences.

conditions.query: A believable NPC has mutual interest, sufficient trust, suitable availability, and a specific reason to invite or accept an intentional one-on-one outing with the player.

effects.instruction: Offer a date invitation or intentional one-on-one activity using a suitable existing Tokyo location and activity. Consider relationship stage, mutual interest, personality, preferences, schedule, finances, transportation, boundaries, previous memories, promises, conflicts, and current events. Do not equate friendship with romance. Present choices to accept, decline, clarify intentions, reschedule, suggest another activity, invite someone else, or keep the interaction friendly. If accepted, play a gradual date scene with meaningful choices and possible complications. Update memories, relationship tone, trust, friendship, rivalry, and romance only according to the player's actions and the NPC's independent response.

conditions.query: A meaningful relationship event involving trust, friendship, rivalry, respect, romance interest, boundaries, memories, promises, betrayal, rejection, or reconciliation is plausible now.

effects.instruction: Create a focused relationship scene only when supported by recent choices, relationship stage, memories, schedules, and NPC goals. Keep romance gradual, mutual, consent-based, and age-appropriate. Preserve friendship, rivalry, rejection, distance, and reconciliation as valid outcomes. Never invent the player's feelings, attraction, consent, dialogue, or decisions. Let NPCs act independently and remember the result.

conditions.query: The player has a believable training, rescue, Battle Test, emotional, or relationship milestone that could improve power control or unlock a suitably limited technique.

effects.instruction: Offer a power-control challenge or milestone suited to the player's authored power, current mastery, Power Strain, training history, and surroundings. On success, improve control, efficiency, or unlock a limited technique. On failure, use proportionate fatigue, minor injury, collateral, embarrassment, or temporary lockout; do not punish harmless power use severely. Reserve ultimate techniques for substantial milestones and meaningful costs.

conditions.query: A school evaluation, attendance issue, exam, Battle Test consequence, discipline matter, teacher meeting, internship opportunity, or class event is plausible based on schedule and recent actions.

effects.instruction: Generate a school progression scene appropriate to the player's route, attendance, grades, power control, Hero Reputation, relationships, and recent choices. Include meaningful options and consequences involving evaluation, teacher approval, detention, repair, internships, licensing, teamwork, or class standing. Do not end the story from one failure, and do not treat rule-bending as automatic villainy.

conditions.query: A civilian rescue, accident, villain incident, disaster, suspicious activity, or public-safety emergency is plausible at the player's current location or along travel.

effects.instruction: Present the emergency with clear hazards, civilians, responders, time pressure, and incomplete information. Let the player intervene, call police or heroes, evacuate, investigate, negotiate, use powers, retreat, or ignore it. Reward restraint, teamwork, accountability, and civilian protection. Track injuries, Power Strain, collateral, Hero Reputation, media response, police attention, school consequences, and relevant memories.

conditions.query: Time has passed or the current day includes a school, work, club, social, assessment, travel, recovery, or major story transition that gives NPCs a believable opportunity to act independently.

effects.instruction: Advance relevant NPCs off-screen using their established schedules, classes, jobs, clubs, goals, relationships, weaknesses, recent memories, health, Energy, Stress, and prior outcomes. NPCs may attend or miss obligations, train, study, work, rest, socialize, date, resolve conflicts, form or leave cliques, improve skills, control powers, unlock limited abilities, change jobs or clubs, pursue internships, and suffer proportional setbacks. Carry all changes forward. Surface only developments that affect the player, shared locations, schedules, relationships, rumors, quests, or opportunities. Do not force player involvement and never invent player thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, attraction, or decisions.

conditions.query: A meaningful amount of time has passed, or NPC school, work, club, relationship, health, financial, or personal circumstances have changed enough to require autonomous decisions.

effects.instruction: Advance relevant NPC inner lives without player involvement. For each NPC, consider established ambitions, short-term goals, values, fears, coping style, boundaries, relationships, crush possibilities, schedule, Energy, Stress, health, skills, grades, job, club, and recent memories. Let NPCs independently choose actions, pursue ambitions, help or avoid others, study, train, work, rest, seek support, set boundaries, reconcile, withdraw, confess, reject, change direction, or accept proportional consequences. Stress is non-diagnostic: raise it for pressure and reduce it through believable recovery. Use gradual effects such as reduced availability, concentration problems, irritability, mistakes, absence, conflict, help-seeking, or recovery. Keep private thoughts hidden unless revealed through behavior, dialogue, messages, journals, dreams, or direct disclosure. Never force player involvement or invent player thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, attraction, or decisions.

conditions.query: The player is an active member of or has an official ongoing assignment with the Misfit Hero Agency.

effects.instruction: Make an appropriate Misfit Hero Agency duty, rescue, reputation, training, or emergency call available through dispatch, Pulse, phone, briefing, or an in-person agency member. Respect the player's schedule, location, fatigue, injuries, existing commitments, and ability to accept, delay, delegate, or decline. Use existing NPCs and locations only; do not synthesize replacements.

conditions.query: The player is an active member of or has an official ongoing assignment with the Metropolitan Police.

effects.instruction: Make an appropriate Metropolitan Police patrol, welfare call, investigation, evidence follow-up, witness interview, emergency response, or internal-affairs call available through dispatch, Pulse, phone, briefing, or an in-person officer. Respect the player's schedule, location, fatigue, injuries, jurisdiction, existing commitments, and ability to accept, delay, request backup, or decline. Preserve procedure, evidence, de-escalation, and player agency; do not assume guilt or invent a player's power.

Make Zee's optional crash-site encounter available only if the player has not already discovered or resolved it. Present investigation, retreat, observation, or direct contact as possible choices. Do not force the player to notice Zee or help her.

conditions.query: The player has repeatedly helped Zee repair or conceal her ship and Zee has voluntarily chosen to trust the player enough to travel with them.

effects.instruction: Offer Zee as an optional permanent party member. Preserve her ability to refuse, delay, leave, or choose another future; joining is never automatic.

Use the authored A Bizarre Adventure quest exactly once when the player first enters Bizarre Alley. This is a fixed cast scene, not a generic encounter. Move aside random bystanders so they cannot replace the central cast. Place the exact NPCs Gogo Jotaro and Deo Brando together in Bizarre Alley area service-run, actively fist-fighting while arguing. Place the exact NPC Announcer Squirrel visibly perched above them before narration. Verify all three names; if one is absent, restore that exact NPC instead of using substitutes. Begin with the fight and the squirrel's exact opening line: "A stranger enters the alley. The world of Chikara Tokyo is about to become considerably more bizarre!" Then offer watching, interrupting, leaving, calling for help, or choosing Gogo's or Deo's argument. Do not create a replacement quest or invent player dialogue, thoughts, feelings, consent, decisions, or unseen actions.

Ability and Pulse Tutorial Completion Re.name: Ability and Pulse Tutorial Completion Rewards

effects.instruction: Begin the one-time arrival encounter for The Wrong Delivery. Show a delivery van idling in the rear alley beside the shuttered karaoke venue. A nervous courier carries a sealed case toward the concealed service entrance while a lookout watches the street. Do not force combat, reveal the boss, or expose the full Hideout layout. Offer observation, stealth, social deception, investigation, direct intervention, and leaving as possible approaches. Scale any opening combat to the active party using the global Hideout and Raid party-scaling guidance.

conditions.query: Ken Kuroda is present near Kurokawa Underground Den, the player has noticed or approached him, and the player has not already declined or accepted his temporary assistance.

effects.instruction: Have Ken Kuroda speak calmly and offer optional temporary party assistance: "If you need help getting inside, I can come with you." He must not reveal that he is Echo, take control of the player's choices, or assume acceptance. If the player accepts, treat Ken as a temporary guest ally and preserve his established nonlethal boundary, abilities, resources, autonomy, and current priorities. If the player declines, let Ken provide a brief route warning or continue his own investigation.

Begin the arrival encounter for Academy District: Dropout Takeover. Show a fenced, damaged academy training facility with powered dropout lookouts using improvised positions. Kiyomi and Mika Tsukino may be present at the entrance only when their schedules, goals, relationships, and a credible investigation make it plausible. If present, let them offer optional assistance without taking control of the player's choices. Offer negotiation, observation, stealth, solo entry, accepting help, and direct confrontation. Do not reveal the full facility layout or force combat. Scale any combat to the active party using global Hideout and Raid guidance.

Begin the arrival encounter for Central Tokyo: Parasite Lab Investigation. Show a concealed service entrance beneath Central Tokyo with signs of a breached underground laboratory: chemical odor, damaged utility panels, warning lights, discarded protective gear, and recent movement. effects.instruction: Override the normal station arrival. Do not describe smiling students, routine transit, ticket help, or peace. Start inside an active encounter: Nami “Fourfold” Sato crashes into the player while fleeing and urgently asks for help. Five armored Crown Meridian mercenaries pursue her: one seals the exit, two advance, one covers the platforms, and one circles behind the player. Smoke pours from a shattered crate, gates spark, and civilians are trapped near the tracks. Minato shields an injured student, Maya blocks an exit and identifies the formation, and Isabelle treats a bleeding commuter before joining the defense. The mercenaries order Nami to surrender and attack when she refuses. Make the choice live: protect Nami, help civilians, fight, escape, or deceive them. Minato, Maya, and Isabelle assist if combat begins. Do not invent player dialogue, thoughts, feelings, consent, or decisions. Nami may resist, use her power, or flee. Do not reveal the conspiracy before evidence.

The station crisis has begun with Nami, Minato, Maya, and Isabelle in the scene. Nami has reached the player asking for help hiding while mercenaries close in. Keep the next beat urgent and let the player choose whether to hide, escort, protect, investigate, negotiate, confront, help civilians, or refuse. Do not force player or ally actions.

effects.instruction: Initialize only the next authored Broken Crown chapter after the current chapter reaches a meaningful outcome. Preserve failed, partial, delayed, and branch-specific consequences. Do not auto-complete an unresolved quest, force travel, recruit a party, or decide the player’s response.

Keep the station scene in active encounter mode and suppress normal arrival narration. Five mercenaries pursue Nami. When combat begins, Minato, Maya, Isabelle, and Nami must each take meaningful combat action rather than stand idle: Minato uses Tidal Burst, Crown Current, Pressure Veil, or another authored water ability; Maya uses Flashbang Toss, Exit Wedge, or close-quarters tactics; Isabelle uses Blood Lance, Coagulation Snare, Pressure-Point Cut, or hemomancy while protecting the wounded; Nami uses an appropriate authored manifestation. They may be interrupted, injured, miss, retreat, or prioritize civilians, but do not leave them decorative. Present combat, rescue, escape, and deception options. Do not invent player actions or decisions.

At the Central Battle Coliseum registration desk, Mel is present and asks how many fighters are entering and who intends to compete. Present the registration honestly: the player may register solo, with current party members, or with recruited NPC partners, and may select a roster of up to eight competitors with human players always prioritized. Offer a concrete choice about how many entrants and who is competing, while keeping NPC partner acceptance, refusal, withdrawal, and personal reasons valid. Do not force registration, universal tournament combat, prizes, fame, victory, or romance. Leave tournament format selection open for a later Circuit event and allow unused competitors to spectate, train, socialize, or enter side events. When the player registers an eight-person roster, have Mel react with her characteristic understated resignation before outlining training and safety terms. Do not invent the player's dialogue, thoughts, feelings, consent, or decisions.

At the Central Battle Coliseum registration desk, show the current Power Circuit event board only if the player has already registered or explicitly asks about entering an event. Present available formats clearly: 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, 4v4, and special events. Ask who is actually competing from the registered roster; do not assume every party member or NPC is willing. NPCs can accept, refuse, withdraw, disagree, or choose spectating, training, socializing, concessions work, or a side event. For any player-versus-player match, confirm mutual consent and the stakes before combat. Explain permitted powers and equipment, safety oversight, surrender, ring-out, time limits, officials' intervention, and whether consequences are temporary or lasting. Do not invent the player's dialogue, thoughts, feelings, consent, or decisions. Start the Power Circuit Event quest only after the player chooses to enter an event.

Unlock Call Mel on the player's phone after Power Circuit Registration. Do not modify Mel's NPC file or alter her character details, abilities, personality, relationships, established location, or story history. Present Mel as an independent character contact whose combat-finder service is available when she can reasonably answer. The phone menu includes Any fights going on?, Find me a fight, Team fights, Tournament schedule, Check my ranking, Ask about opponent, Training, Rivals, Circuit news, and Never mind. Calling Mel should be the fastest way to find combat content, but she may be unavailable or recommend recovery when the story, time, or her own established circumstances require it.

effects.instruction: Resolve the selected Call Mel request as a repeatable combat-content search without editing Mel's NPC record or changing her established character details, abilities, personality, relationships, location, or story history. Apply the requested solo, team, difficult, easy, underground, monster, special-rule, rival, or major-event filter.

Mel gives an opinionated recommendation in her established voice and may warn about danger or recommend recovery.
